Group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described and thresholded (P<0.001 uncorrected) indicating whole-brain evidence (meets I6). Participants are healthy volunteers (meets I7). Whole-brain results are described and illustrated in figures/text (meets I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing the Paper-Scissors-Rock (PSR) decision-making task, which uses predetermined probabilities for preferred/even/worst responses (90%, 50%, 10%), constituting risky/uncertain decision-making. The analyses include within-task contrasts among decision conditions (preferred, even, worst) rather than only task>baseline contrasts, satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making condition contrast. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps were generated and reported (LME voxelwise tests, cluster correction, tables/figures of significant clusters), meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Participant groups (occasional stimulant users) are acceptable per eligibility. Results are reported in the main text and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to task>rest only, not PET, not ROI-only, and include whole-brain task activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study (n=5) of perceptual decision making using a dot-motion/color coherence task. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses testing parametric contrasts of coherence (i.e., low vs high coherence / hard > easy comparisons) and presents statistical maps, tables, and ROI analyses. The task and contrasts directly match perceptual decision-making criteria (parameterized motion/color coherence; attended vs ignored conditions). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion (introduction, materials and methods, results, modeling, connectivity, discussion), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (this is not PET; contrasts are condition-vs-condition parametric, not only baseline; whole-brain results are reported; not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion for meta-analysis of fMRI perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents performing the Iowa Gambling Task (ambiguous/risky decision-making). It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to decision-making (advantageous > disadvantageous choices; wins > losses) and reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (with ROI and whole-brain follow-ups). Participant groups (ADHD, OCD, healthy controls) are acceptable under the review’s participant inclusion. Results and coordinates/figures are reported in the text and figures/supplement. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (two-choice monetary risk-taking), explicitly tested contrasts comparing decision conditions (risky > safe and related contrasts), and reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (cluster-corrected results, tables, and figures). Participant groups (alcohol-dependent patients and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, fMRI acquisition, whole-brain analysis), Results (within- and between-group contrasts, cumulative-earnings modulation), and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

The study uses fMRI and reports whole-brain, group-level parametric maps of neural activity related to perceived social risk during purchase decisions. However, the task probes social risk / social judgment (anticipated disapproval) in consumer choices rather than risky decision-making defined as decisions involving objective or probabilistic risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. Therefore it reflects social/moral decision-making, not the risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision types targeted by the meta-analysis.

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in 9–11 year-old humans performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game). It includes within-task contrasts comparing Decision versus Directed (control) trials (e.g., risky Decision > Directed sham trials), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM with nonparametric permutation testing) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Participant characteristics fall within eligible age groups. Results are reported in the main text and tables (whole-brain coordinates/clusters), satisfying the meta-analysis’ reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This fMRI study (n=15 healthy adults) directly tests reward-based decision-making under certainty, risk, and ambiguity using an in-scanner task. The manuscript reports within-subject contrasts relevant to the review (risk > certain; ambiguous > certain; ambiguous > risk) and describes group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with statistical thresholds, activation maps, tables, and figures. The report therefore meets inclusion criteria for (I4) task fMRI, (I5) condition-vs-condition contrasts, (I6) whole-brain group-level maps, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) acceptable reporting format. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state/connectivity-only; contains condition-vs-condition contrasts rather than only task>rest). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (hypothetical treatment choices with explicit side-effect probabilities and efficacies). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (mild > severe and severe > mild side-effect conditions), perform group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses, and present corrected peak coordinates and figures (FWE-corrected). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for risky decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain group results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only reporting) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which adolescents performed a lottery choice (risk) decision-making task during BOLD acquisition. The authors modeled a parametric regressor of coefficient of variation (CV) of chosen gambles and report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (cluster-level FWE-corrected), showing greater right amygdala activation to higher-risk versus lower-risk choices (equivalent to a 'high-risk > low-risk' contrast). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. The task and reported contrasts meet the risky-DM specifications, whole-brain maps/coordinates are provided, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or baseline-only). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). It includes within-task contrasts comparing risky vs. safe selections (risky > safe), and also reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates, cluster sizes, and corrected significance (AlphaSim). One-sample t-tests for within-group task effects and between-group contrasts are presented and described in tables and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making that reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (high-risk vs low-risk; high-risk vs equal-risk; risk/reward vs control) in an adolescent sample, so it meets I4 (fMRI), I5 (decision-making contrasts), and I7 (eligible participant groups). However, the paper only reports ROI-constrained voxelwise tests (small-volume correction within pre-specified prefrontal ROIs) and presents ROI-based activations/coordinates rather than an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Although the authors state that activations were collected brain-wide, all reported statistical tests and inference are restricted to a priori ROIs (SVC), and no whole-brain, unmasked group statistical maps or whole-brain voxelwise results are provided. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and falls under exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in human healthy adults that explicitly manipulates and reports neural correlates of decision-making under uncertainty (relative and mean uncertainty). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps (coordinates, FWE-corrected clusters) linking trial-by-trial relative uncertainty to BOLD in RLPFC and mean uncertainty to DLPFC/SPL. Analyses include parametric contrasts (high vs low uncertainty effects) and group contrasts (explorers vs nonexplorers), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast beyond implicit baseline. Methods, results, and coordinates are reported in the main text (with supplemental materials available), and the task involves ambiguous/uncertain decision-making (uncertainty-driven exploration), which fits the meta-analysis’ ambiguous-DM domain. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-eligible task) are met.

Exclusion E5 applies: the study's task is intertemporal choice/delay discounting (explicitly listed as excluded in E5). Although the paper used fMRI (I4), reported an ambiguous > exact contrast (I5), provided whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps (I6), included an eligible participant group (I7), and reported whole-brain results in text/tables (I8), the decision-making paradigm is delay discounting/intertemporal choice, which the meta-analysis explicitly excludes. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that directly examines risky decision-making (choices between risky gambles and certain outcomes) and compares decision conditions (single-play vs aggregated-play) and an EV-judgment task. It reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses with clusterwise correction and identifies brain regions; contrasts include condition-vs-condition (aggregated > single) as well as EV judgment effects. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG-fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) with trial-by-trial confidence measures. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (cluster-corrected) and provides coordinates and statistical maps linking BOLD to parametric contrasts (e.g., confidence-related modulation, EEG-derived high vs. low confidence), satisfying within-task condition comparisons. The methods, results, and discussion are complete in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and contrasts are not only task>rest). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans performing decision-making tasks involving risk/ambiguity (IGT and RDT). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (parametric contrasts for reward and risk prediction errors), conjunction and contrast analyses including IGT > RDT, and whole-brain cluster-level FWE-corrected maps with coordinates. Results are reported in tables/figures and supplemental material. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision tasks), I5 (between-task contrast IGT > RDT and task-related parametric contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy participants allowed), and I8 (coordinates and maps reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original fMRI study in humans that measured brain activation while participants performed a risky decision-making task (repeated choices between a risky stock and a safe bond). It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., stock vs. bond choice in the gain domain — equivalent to risky > safe) and conducts group-level, whole-brain analyses (SPM group-level contrasts, whole-brain FWE-corrected results reported). Participants are healthy adult males. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (experimental design, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLMs), Results (whole-brain and ROI results), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study with healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (categorizing average color/shape). The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise SPM8 analyses (parametric and contrast-based tests of mean-related and variance-related uncertainty) with peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results, satisfying contrasts equivalent to hard>easy / uncertainty contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not rest-baseline-only contrasts, and task is perceptual DM).

This study collected fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (I4) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and ROI coordinates (I6, I8). However, the reported whole-brain contrasts described in the full text are task>background and epoch>rest (instruction/stimulus/confidence > rest) and ROI-defining contrasts were task>background; the paper does not present a qualifying condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast of the form required for perceptual-DM (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>control task). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only contrasts against implicit baseline/rest). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This study reports human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (delayed match-to-category of auditory and tactile frequency sweeps), with condition-vs-condition analyses (up‑sweep vs down‑sweep) and group-level, whole-brain (surface/voxelwise) statistical maps. Methods describe random-effects GLM univariate contrasts and a surface-based whole-brain searchlight MVPA (SVM) decoding up vs down, with cluster-based correction and conjunctions across modalities. Reporting includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for fMRI perceptual decision-making, a decision-vs-decision contrast, whole-brain group analyses, and acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria (e.g., task vs baseline only, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the article should be included.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling (Blackjack) task that manipulates risk. It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (e.g., high-risk hits > low-risk hits; low-risk sits > high-risk sits) matching risky-DM contrast forms. Analyses used group-level, random-effects, voxelwise statistics and report Talairach coordinates and whole-brain/exploratory activations (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Participants are an eligible group (healthy students). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, task>rest contrasts only) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

The study reports human fMRI during an ambiguous/uncertain decision-making task (matching-pennies). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguity/uncertainty (e.g., feedback > no-feedback; uncertain > certain; high- vs low-load) and an event-related feedback vs no-feedback contrast. Analyses are group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with reported MNI coordinates/ROIs. Participants are healthy adults. Results are clearly reported in main text (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not only ROI; not contrasts vs baseline only; not connectivity-only; empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making task (olfactory 2AFC), directly addressing perceptual DM. The authors conducted within-task comparisons and model-based regressions that distinguish difficulty/temporal-integration profiles (analogous to hard > easy or condition-wise contrasts) and tested condition-by-time interactions. Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain GLMs (subject-level contrasts entered into a one-sample t test) with reported significant activations and follow-up ROI deconvolution. Participants are healthy adults and full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a well-established risky decision-making paradigm (experimental gamble vs control gamble) with contrasts of interest (experimental>control; high vs low probability; high vs low gain) and separate decision and outcome phases. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FLAME for within-group effects and OLS for between-group effects) with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants include substance-using and control groups. Thus the study provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for risky decision-making and meets the meta-analysis requirements for risky-DM contrasts and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete (methods, results, tables, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study where adolescent girls performed a risky decision-making task (modified Jackpot) during scanning, with task contrasts comparing decision conditions (Play > Pass, LR > HR, Gain > Loss). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected clusters), and results are described in the main text and supplements. The task qualifies as risky decision-making and multiple condition-versus-condition contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI results, only baseline contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

This fMRI study examined perceptual decision-making (face gender discrimination) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (reward bias vs neutral; evidence vs noise), and used healthy human participants — thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (condition contrasts such as evidence vs noise and reward bias vs neutral), and I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). However, the reported analyses and results are exclusively ROI-based time-course analyses (effector- and stimulus-selective ROIs) with no clear report of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps, coordinates, or whole-brain tables/figures in the provided full text. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map). Exclusion criteria met: E6. Full text appears complete for screening (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Given the absence of unmasked whole-brain task activation results, this study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (face/house discrimination) meeting the review scope. It collected BOLD data while human subjects performed a perceptual decision task (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts and condition comparisons (face vs house, analyses across noise/difficulty and RT bins), satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-vs-decision or difficulty contrast (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (repeated-measures ANOVA, voxelwise GLM) with reported peak coordinates and ROI maps, fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I6) and acceptable reporting formats (I8). Participant group (healthy young adults) is acceptable under participant criteria (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not only task>baseline (E3), not PET (E4), are perceptual DM (not excluded by E5), include whole-brain results (not E6), are not connectivity-only (not E7), and are empirical data (not E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study acquired fMRI while human participants performed decision-making tasks that include explicit risky/uncertainty conditions (uncertainty task with specified probabilities) and a complex task combining delay and uncertainty. First-level contrasts were computed comparing each task against an active control task, and group-level, whole-brain activation maps are reported (figures and thresholded maps). Participants are healthy humans. Thus the paper provides voxelwise, group-level task-evoked fMRI results for decision-making involving risk/uncertainty. It does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not PET, contrasts are task vs control not implicit baseline). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of risky economic decision-making (mixed lotteries) conducted in human participants (MDD and healthy controls), satisfying I4. The analysis includes condition-wise parametric modulators for gains and losses and directly contrasts gain versus loss coding (gains > losses and losses > gains) and group interactions, satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses with whole-brain results and coordinates (including whole-brain and ROI-corrected findings, supplementary tables/figures) meeting I6 and I8. Participant groups (MDD and HC) are acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET (E4), does not use only baseline contrasts (it uses condition contrasts, so E3 not met), reports whole-brain results (not ROI-only, E6), is not connectivity/resting-only (E7), includes within-group task effects (E8), and is empirical (not E9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (BART) during scanning, with appropriate within-task contrasts and task-vs-control contrasts (PumpsParametric > ControlParametric, PumpsAvg > ControlAvg). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with cluster correction and peak coordinates; both within-group and between-group effects are presented. Participants (young smokers and nonsmokers) are within allowable groups. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) during scanning (I4 satisfied) and reports a task>control contrast (IGT > non-gambling control) (I5 satisfied). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses were restricted to an anatomically defined VMPFC region (ROI-based analyses); the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or unmasked whole-brain results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Hence EXCLUDED due to E6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that explicitly investigates risky decision-making. The task required choices between high-risk (40% chance $2.50) and low-risk (80% chance $1.25) gambles, and the authors report a direct contrast of high-risk > low-risk. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (one-sample t tests) with reported peak coordinates (Table 1) and statistical thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in figures/tables and the paper contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not task>baseline only). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing risky decision-making tasks (choices between risky and safe options). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe and high-risk versus low-risk conditions, and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and peak coordinates reported. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain activation reporting, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not PET, not resting/seed-only, not ROI-only, and includes within-group task contrasts).

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents using the HiLo decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (pure uncertainty 50% vs probabilistic conditions). The primary contrast of interest is a condition-vs-condition contrast (50% condition vs other task conditions), which corresponds to an ambiguous/high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty comparison. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction are reported and thresholded maps/clusters are provided in tables and figures. The task and contrasts directly address ambiguous decision-making and meet the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a tactile perceptual decision-making task (spatial pattern discrimination) with parametric manipulation of difficulty. The authors modelled difficulty-related effects using parametric modulators derived from RTs (analogous to 'hard > easy' contrasts) and report group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with cluster correction and Talairach coordinates (supplementary tables). They additionally provide MVPA results and full methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults. The design, analyses, and reported whole-brain activation maps satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task-vs-baseline only, and not non-empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this is a whole-brain fMRI study of human participants performing a probabilistic choice task (I4, I6, I7, I8 satisfied), the reported contrasts focus on outcome processing (gain vs neutral, loss vs neutral), prediction-error regressors, and functional connectivity. The paper does not report any decision-phase contrasts that match the meta-analysis requirements (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or hard > easy) nor a decision-task versus active control contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no clear unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-activation maps required by inclusion criterion I6. This meets exclusion criterion E6. The paper does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (contains risky > safe contrasts), I7 (healthy participants included), and I8 (results described in text/figures). However it does NOT provide the required whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I6), so it cannot be included. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing the risky-gains task (risky decision-making). The authors report within-task contrasts (risky > safe) at the subject level and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 t-maps with voxel-wise threshold and cluster extent), and present activation tables/figures. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making (risky > safe) with whole-brain group maps; no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, baseline-only contrasts, ROI-only reporting) are met.

This study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for decision-making contrasts. Exclusion: E3 applies — the critical task contrast reported is 'last reversal error compared to implicit (unmodeled) baseline' (task > implicit baseline), and the study does not present condition-versus-condition contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and coordinates are reported), I7 (participants are human healthy subjects, an allowable group), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is a probabilistic reversal learning/set-shifting task and is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review), and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude on the basis of E3 (only implicit-baseline contrasts).

This is a methodological paper about real-time fMRI and sequential testing (SPRT). Although it reports human fMRI data (single-subject demonstration within an ROI), the study does not test a risky, ambiguous, or clearly defined perceptual decision-making paradigm as required (task was passive viewing/liking ratings of faces vs houses rather than a perceptual decision/difficulty or uncertainty manipulation). Crucially, the real-data results are presented within a preselected ROI (717 voxels) and the demonstration uses a single subject rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirements for (at least) a whole-brain, group-level task map and a qualifying decision-making task/contrast.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (ambiguous cue conditioning) with explicit choices (obtain reward vs avoid punishment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) including condition contrasts (positive tone vs negative tone) and parametric modulations across tones (linear and quadratic effects indexing valence generalization and ambiguity). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and tables with cluster-level FWE correction. Participants and task fall squarely within the ambiguous decision-making domain. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET-only, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study in human youth performing a well-established risky decision-making task (Cups Task) during scanning, reporting within-task contrasts (risky vs nonrisky; gain vs loss) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME1, cluster-corrected). The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis scope (risky decision-making) and all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants (n=19) performing a visual-lottery decision task that requires perceptual (metacognitive) estimation of success probability and integration with reward value. The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLM analyses and corrected cluster results for parametric contrasts of reward probability, reward value, and expected value (EV), and present tabulated/figure whole-brain results. The reported contrasts constitute within-task, condition-related effects (parametric modulators and EV contrasts) rather than task>rest baselines. Methods describe standard whole-brain mixed-effects analysis and correction for multiple comparisons. The task fits perceptual decision-making under uncertainty. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI/connectivity, task>rest only, between-group-only contrasts) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion and appears complete for screening.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (50:50 monetary gambles), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinate tables; participants are an acceptable sample and results are reported with coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I6 (whole-brain group voxelwise analysis), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (coordinates/figures reported). However, the imaging results do not report a contrast that directly compares decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe, accept > reject, high-risk > low-risk) or an experimental risk task > control task. The primary reported contrast is novel > familiar prime and regressions of that contrast with subsequent risk-taking behavior; no within-task decision-making contrast (risky vs safe) is provided in the reported whole-brain results. Thus inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 is not met.

This study reports simultaneous EEG/fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney image categorization). The authors conducted EEG-informed whole-brain GLM fMRI analyses with condition comparisons (objects vs. scrambled/inverted faces) and direct contrasts (HF>LF, LF>HF) and report group-level, voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction and a table of peak coordinates (Table 1). Thus it includes fMRI during a perceptual decision task (I4), contains condition contrasts suitable for perceptual-DM (I5), provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation maps (I6), uses an eligible participant group (I7), and reports coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This study reports fMRI data collected while participants performed a probability discounting task (probability option vs fixed/certain option), which is a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper includes within-task contrasts (probability > fixed) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 second-level analyses with cluster correction) and reports brain regions/coordinates. Although the study also includes delay-discounting (intertemporal) tasks (which would be excluded), the presence of the probability discounting task satisfies the review’s requirement for a risky decision-making fMRI contrast. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, or reporting only between-group contrasts) are met. Full text contains Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and is includable in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (modified cups task) performed by human participants (I4). The paper reports relevant within-task contrasts (risky > sure / risky–sure and related target×situation×choice contrasts) that match the admissible risky-DM contrasts (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results reported with whole-brain FWE correction and coordinate information (I6, I8). Participants are healthy young adults (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-task contrasts vs rest, or non-decision tasks) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (guesses about a briefly flashed stimulus) with a scanner-based phase manipulating uncertainty and social vs individual information. The authors report group-level, whole-brain (SPM8 random-effects) analyses with cluster FWE correction and local maxima coordinates, and they present condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., I:I vs integration conditions; S:S > I:S). These contrasts constitute within-task condition comparisons relevant to perceptual decision-making under uncertainty. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition vs condition decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI during a risky decision-making game (I4) and reports within-task contrasts comparing non-match (risky) vs match (safe) anticipation and outcome contrasts (I5). Participant sample (OCD patients and controls) is acceptable (I7) and results are described in text/figures (I8). However, the paper reports task activation results primarily via region-of-interest (ROI) extractions (amygdala and nucleus accumbens) using templates from a prior study rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map required for inclusion (I6). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only task activation reporting without whole-brain task results). Because it does not provide the requisite group-level whole-brain task activation maps, it cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (sequential gambles with targets). The paper reports within-task, parametric contrasts (regressors for target level, expected value, variance/risk, skewness) and tests neural correlates of these decision variables at the group level using SPM; results are reported as voxelwise group analyses with stereotactic coordinates and thresholds (whole-brain results and small-volume corrections). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making (I4), contains within-task contrasts/parametric comparisons relevant to risky decisions (I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I6), uses an eligible participant sample (I7), and provides whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). The provided full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study (3T) in healthy human participants performing a decision-making task manipulating uncertainty and financial incentive. It reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to the review (e.g., High vs Low uncertainty, Financial_High vs Neutral_High) matching ambiguous/risky decision-making contrasts. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM8 results with tables of peaks, figures, and cluster thresholds; small-volume corrections are also reported but whole-brain contrasts are present. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a two-choice prediction decision-making task with manipulated error rates indexing reward/uncertainty/punishment (risky/ambiguous decision-making). Within-task contrasts and main effects compare error-rate conditions (e.g., 50% uncertainty > 20%/80%) and interoception conditions, and group- and condition-level voxelwise analyses are reported. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics (LME per voxel) with cluster correction (AlphaSim) are presented. Participant sample (problem stimulant users, desisted users, controls) is acceptable per inclusion. Full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making and provides whole-brain task activation results.

Exclusion: E5 applies. This study’s reported fMRI contrast is Win > No Win (reward receipt vs no reward) from the feedback phase, which is reward receipt without an uncertainty manipulation and not a decision-phase contrast comparing risk levels. Inclusion: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) is satisfied because the Wheel of Fortune is a risky-DM paradigm; I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps) is satisfied — whole-brain ANCOVA results are reported; I7 (participant group acceptable) is satisfied; I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures) is satisfied. Inclusion not met: I5 is not met — the paper does not report a decision-making contrast of interest for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, or risk > certainty); the only analyzed/ reported contrast isolates reward receipt (Win > No Win) across all trial types. Therefore the study should be excluded from the decision-making meta-analysis.

The paper reports an fMRI gambling decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (Win vs Lose blocks) in human participants, providing within-task contrasts (Lose vs Win) and a group-level repeated-measures GLM whole-brain analysis with coordinates and statistical maps. It thus meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (within-task contrast: high uncertainty/lose vs low uncertainty/win), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I7 (human participant groups—GAD and healthy controls are acceptable), and I8 (results reported with coordinates/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not task>baseline only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without whole-brain activation, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning (decision-making under uncertainty) in healthy human participants using within-task contrasts (shift>stay for choice under uncertainty; reward>punishment for outcome). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TFCE, permutation-corrected) and also ROI follow-ups; whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and tables. The shift>stay contrast explicitly models decisional processes under high uncertainty (post-PE and post-reversal trials), which maps onto the review's ambiguous/risky decision-making domain. Participants are healthy adults, and the full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a risky decision-making paradigm). It includes within-task contrasts comparing risky versus non-risk (mean color pump > mean white pump), parametric (linear color > linear white) contrasts of risk level, and outcome contrasts (Explosions > Cashouts), all analyzed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction. Participants (heavy drinkers) are an acceptable group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed a risky decision-making task (risky-gains). The paper reports a within-task contrast comparing risky > safe choices (GLT risky vs safe) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (linear mixed effects and robust regressions) with cluster-corrected results and region descriptions. Participants include HIV+ and seronegative controls (acceptable per criteria). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only, and includes within-group task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full manuscript reports an fMRI study where human participants performed a risky/ambiguous decision-making task (Card-Deck). The paper includes within-group and between-group voxelwise contrasts (decision under risk vs decision under ambiguity; bet vs safe), with group-level whole-brain analyses and tables of activation coordinates. The task and contrasts match risky and ambiguous DM definitions in the meta-analysis. Whole-brain, group-level activation maps are reported (voxelwise GLM, thresholds and cluster correction described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete for screening.

This is a human fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (images of pianos/chairs) that manipulated stimulus discriminability (high/medium/low) and analysed task difficulty (decreasing stimulus quality = hard > easy) and trial-by-trial RT effects. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLMs were reported with FWE-corrected results and clusters in tables/figures. Contrasts correspond to perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., low > high stimulus quality / hard > easy), satisfying the review’s contrast requirements. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study is an fMRI investigation of state-based dynamic reward learning (state-maximizing vs reward-maximizing choices) comparing younger and older adults. However, the task is a history-dependent reward-learning paradigm and does not manipulate or contrast risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or perceptual difficulty conditions as defined by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The paper does meet some inclusion requirements: it reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (I6); uses healthy human participants (I7); and presents whole-brain results described in the text/figures (I8). It does not meet I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and I5 (it does not report the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Therefore it should be excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI study using a mixed gambles task (50/50 gains/losses) that probes risky decision-making in human participants (adolescents and adults). The study reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Accepted Trials > Rejected Trials and Rejected Trials > Accepted Trials) as well as Accepted/Rejected trials versus baseline, and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables. Participants are healthy human subjects across relevant ages. Therefore the paper meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, no ROI-only, not only baseline contrasts, and includes within-task condition contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (sequential ‘boxes’ gamble). Analyses include within-task contrasts and parametric modulators (e.g., magnitude of missed opportunity; loss position) and second-level random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain SPM8 analyses with multiple-comparison correction and reported peak coordinates/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Contrasts are condition-versus-condition/parametric (not only task>baseline). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy humans investigating decision-making under outcome uncertainty with a probabilistic (60%/40%) two-alternative sampling task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and contrasts of task conditions versus an active control (information-gathering > counting; decision event > counting), with coordinates and thresholding described. Thus it meets the review’s scope (risky/probabilistic decision-making) and satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI task, task>control contrasts, whole-brain group analysis, participant eligibility, and reporting of whole-brain results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only, non-empirical) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task. The fMRI analysis includes parametric modulation by pump number (capturing high-risk vs low-risk within trials) and contrasts including active (reward) vs control (white balloon) trials. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results and coordinates), with mixed-effects between-subject analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition, task, GLM), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts indexing risk (parametric modulation by pump number; effectively high-risk > low-risk) and include control pump events (white balloons) to account for motor/visual activity. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME1; voxelwise Z>2.3, cluster p<0.05 corrected). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports human fMRI data collected while participants performed a risky decision-making (loss aversion gamble) task (I4). The analyses include within-task parametric contrasts for gain-related and loss-related activation (i.e., comparisons of decision conditions by magnitude), and group-level voxelwise maps (whole-brain, cluster-corrected) are reported (I5, I6). Participant groups include substance users and HIV+ persons (eligible per review) and are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text, tables, and figures (I8). The task is a risky DM paradigm (not PET, not ROI-only, and not resting/seed connectivity only), and the paper presents unmasked within-group main effects as well as group comparisons, so no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete and includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets the meta-analysis requirements: it acquired fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) and reports condition-wise contrasts (risky vs safe). Analyses were voxel-wise and a whole-brain analysis of group-by-decision effects is reported (supplementary figure/table), with coordinates and cluster results provided. Participants are a qualifying group (substance-using methamphetamine-dependent individuals). Results include task-evoked, group-level voxelwise statistical maps (risk>safe / risky–safe) and reported AUC/ROC for predictive value. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-task contrasts). Full text appears to include introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but main article content is present, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human older adults performing a lottery choice task that manipulates risk via probabilities and magnitudes (risky decision-making). The authors report within-task contrasts using parametric modulators of expected value (EV) and group-level voxelwise analyses identifying positive and negative EV sensitivity, age and risk-preference effects, and feedback-related contrasts; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps with peak-voxel tables and figures. These analyses satisfy the requirement for condition-vs-condition/task contrasts (e.g., sensitivity to high vs low EV/riskier vs surer) and provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation evidence. The task and sample fall within eligible participant groups. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not rest-baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (categorizing happy vs angry faces with clear vs noisy images), fulfilling I4. It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (noisy > clear; hard > easy) relevant to perceptual DM, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses are reported (second-level t-tests with FDR correction and a table of activated regions), meeting I6 and I8. Participant characteristics are acceptable (healthy adults), satisfying I7. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not connectivity-only (E7), and does not report only task>rest contrasts as the sole decision-related contrast (E3). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making and is included.

The full text reports an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (risk-taking and gamble stages). The authors present condition-versus-condition contrasts (risk-disadvantageous vs risk-advantageous) and group comparisons (IGD vs HC) based on second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate tables/figures. Participant groups (IGD and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full article contains methods, results, and discussion (full text complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, only task>rest contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This study reports fMRI of human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) with within-task contrasts (risky vs safe) and reports voxel-wise group-level analyses and coordinates. The methods describe voxel-wise analyses and supplemental whole-brain activation patterns; results include risky > safe comparisons and within-group relationships. Participants include substance users and controls. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s fMRI, task-contrast, group-level voxelwise reporting, participant, and reporting-forms criteria.

Exclusion reason: This study conducted fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (meets I4) in human participants (adolescents and adults; meets I7). However, the imaging results are reported only as ROI-based analyses (ACC, VS, vmPFC) and discrete-state summaries, with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or whole-brain coordinate tables presented; thus it qualifies as an ROI-only study (meets exclusion E6). In addition, the reported contrasts are feedback/decision condition comparisons (PFB, NFB-Stay, NFB-Switch) rather than standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy), so it does not provide the required decision-making contrast form for the meta-analysis (fails I5 and I6). Therefore exclude under E6. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6.

This is a prospective fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making paradigm (Wheel of Fortune) with explicit probabilities. It reports within-task contrasts comparing high vs moderate and high/moderate vs equal risk/reward conditions and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons, with results described in text, figures, and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, scan acquisition, preprocessing, group analyses), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a sequential risk-taking task (participants open boxes with uncertain ‘devil’ outcomes), meeting risky decision-making criteria. It reports within-task contrasts (Context: Self vs Computer; Outcome: Optimum, Non-optimum, Devil) and parametric contrasts (gains, losses) rather than task>rest, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition comparisons. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM8 results with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds reported (tables/figures described). Participants are healthy human adults. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task vs baseline only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study used simultaneous EEG-fMRI with human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (meets I4). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results (meets I6) with acceptable participant sample (meets I7) and whole-brain results presented in text/tables (meets I8). However, it does not present at least one contrast that matches the meta-analysis’ required decision-making contrasts (I5) — e.g., there is no reported ‘risky > safe’, ‘high-risk > low-risk’, ‘high uncertainty > low uncertainty’, or perceptual ‘hard > easy’ contrast during the decision phase. The reported contrasts/regressors are outcome-locked parametric regressors for prediction-error valence and surprise (EEG-informed and model-based), not the decision-condition contrasts required by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore the study fails to satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and presents condition contrasts (anticipation vs. experience; gain vs. draw vs. loss; deck A/B/C/D comparisons and time-course by monetary value) rather than only task>baseline contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain activation maps and discussed with coordinates/figures. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (ring-size discrimination), and it contrasted stimulus/choice conditions, so it meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM) and I5 (within-task stimulus/choice contrasts). Participants were healthy adults (I7). However, the analyses are restricted to V1 (retinotopically defined ROI/population analyses) and the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; results are presented as ROI-based/region-specific analyses rather than whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it fails I6 and matches exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). On that basis the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a decision-making task that involves uncertainty about outcomes and feedback during learning. It includes within-task contrasts comparing high-uncertainty (exploratory) versus low-uncertainty (proficiency) phases and contrasts of gains vs. losses and correct vs. wrong feedback, i.e. condition-versus-condition comparisons relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain (SPM2) voxelwise analyses are reported with coordinates and cluster results. Participants are healthy adult females. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, coordinates) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET only, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This fMRI study does not meet the review's scope for decision-making under risk/ambiguity/perceptual uncertainty. Although it contains whole-brain group fMRI analyses and healthy participants, the scanned tasks involve incidental reward learning (a MID-like speeded response task) and a memory test for value; the explicit risky gamble manipulation (Experiment 4) was behavioral only (not scanned). Therefore key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis are not met: no fMRI scan during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task (I4), and no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe or ambiguous>non-ambiguous (I5). Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps while participants performed a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with volatile (high uncertainty) and stable (low uncertainty) decision-making conditions. The authors report within-task contrasts (learning-rate-modulation/volatile trials vs nonlearning/stable trials) and model-based regressors (RPE and learning rate) with whole-brain analyses and tables, satisfying condition-vs-condition contrast requirements analogous to 'high uncertainty > low uncertainty'. The task engages decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous/risky DM), and participants include healthy and schizophrenia groups (eligible populations). Whole-brain results are reported (tables/figures) and ROI analyses are supplementary. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of decision-making under maximum uncertainty (ambiguous DM) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reports of coordinates, but the critical decision-making contrasts are 50% probability condition > implicit baseline (task > implicit baseline). The paper does not report condition-versus-condition contrasts of uncertainty (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty) or task > active control task. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only contrasts vs implicit baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant groups), I8 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control decision-making contrast). Consequently the study must be excluded.

Exclusion E3 applies: the fMRI contrast of interest reported is decision > fixation (task > rest/fixation), and the paper does not report a condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast (e.g., risky>safe). Met inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — modified Iowa Gambling Task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mapping was performed via MEPM), I7 (participant groups acceptable — substance-dependent and controls), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-vs-decision or task-vs-active-control contrast; the primary reported contrast is against fixation). Because E3 excludes studies whose only decision-making contrasts are against an implicit baseline/rest/fixation, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite having whole-brain analyses. Full text appears complete and was used for screening.

This is an fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual decision-making (rapid evidence accumulation/Go–No-Go ‘‘baseball’’) task. The paper reports voxelwise GLM parameter estimates and whole-brain searchlight AUC/p-value maps and conducts within-task contrasts between decision conditions (Correct Go vs Correct No-Go; Correct No-Go vs Incorrect No-Go, etc.), satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making contrast. Participants (n=11) are humans and whole-brain task-evoked maps are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI experiment in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (synchrony/asynchrony judgments) (I4). The authors report condition-versus-control contrasts appropriate for perceptual DM (e.g., asynchrony and synchrony perception > auditory+visual unisensory conditions; i.e., perceptual task > control task) (I5). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses are described and reported (SPM second-level one-sample t-tests; activation maps and tables) fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Participants are healthy human adults (I7). Results are reported in text/figures/tables with coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (contrasts are not task>rest only; study is fMRI not PET; whole-brain maps are provided; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study acquired fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal-learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), and reports within-task contrasts (loseshift > winstay; final error > error) that compare decision-making conditions. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with multiple-comparison correction and reported coordinates/figures/tables. Participant groups (schizophrenia and controls) are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). Contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), it is not PET, and it provides whole-brain results rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly examined risky decision-making using a Roulette task manipulating reward probability (25% vs 75%), i.e. risky versus safe conditions. It reports within-task condition contrasts (high- vs low-probability gains and related probability-by-group contrasts) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain results and supplementary tables of activated foci are described). Participant groups are human (bipolar patients and healthy controls). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not resting-state/ROI-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI and should be included.

This is an fMRI study using a gambling (risky decision-making) task with within-task contrasts (risky vs non-risky and parametric effects related to risk) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with stereotactic coordinates and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making (I4, I5), provides whole-brain voxelwise group results (I6), and participant sampling is acceptable (I7); results are reported with coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

This study reports an fMRI task in human participants that involves decision-making under uncertainty (two-choice prediction task with 50% reinforcement), which qualifies as ambiguous decision-making. It includes an explicit task-versus-active-control contrast (two-choice prediction task > two-choice response task). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise regression, F- and t-maps, ROI analyses derived from whole-brain maps) and presents task-related whole-brain activation results. Participant group (methamphetamine-dependent subjects and matched controls) is an acceptable sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not task>rest only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

This empirical paper reports multiple fMRI experiments in which human participants made risky/ambiguous decisions (probability-weighting and regret experiments using probabilistic electric-shock lotteries and choice among lotteries/doors). The manuscript reports within-subject condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., different probabilities; high-regret > no-regret; rejoice vs regret interactions) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and tables of regions. Participants are healthy adults. Although the chapter also summarizes an intertemporal (dread) experiment (intertemporal choice is excluded if sole focus), the presence of the probability-weighting and regret experiments provides direct risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts suitable for the meta-analysis. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for methods and results reporting relevant contrasts.

This study reports an fMRI investigation in humans performing a decision-making task that manipulated uncertainty (odd–even–pass task: uncertain > certain). It includes a clear decision-making contrast (uncertain > certain, matching ambiguous/risky DM), reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with thresholding and reported activations/coordinates, and includes both clinical (IGD) and healthy control groups. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, and includes whole-brain task maps).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing an explicit risky decision-making gambling task with explicit probabilities and reward/punishment conditions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses and contrasts of task conditions against a neutral control (reward>neutral, loss>neutral), satisfying the required task-versus-control contrast form. Whole-brain results are reported (tables/coordinates) and ROI analyses are supplementary. Full article contains complete Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using the BART (risky decision-making) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, but the reported task contrasts appear to be event main effects (e.g., Inflate, Success, Win) and between-group comparisons of those events. The paper does not report a qualifying condition-versus-condition contrast (e.g., Inflate > Cash-In, risky > safe) or an experimental task > active control contrast in the provided full text; therefore the study’s only decision-related contrasts appear to be against implicit baseline, which meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), I8 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no explicit condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast reported). Exclusion criteria applied: E3 (only contrasts vs implicit baseline). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in humans that includes a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) and a rule-based decision task, collected during whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports condition-versus-control contrasts (task trials vs control trials; manipulations of difficulty/coherence and regressions on uncertainty levels), provides whole-brain statistical maps and thresholding, and reports coordinates/activation patterns. Participants are healthy human adults. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (task > control and difficulty/coherence/uncertainty contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not only baseline contrasts, not only ROI/connectivity, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study that implements a probabilistic (ambiguous) decision-making task (modified beads task) performed during BOLD fMRI in human participants (schizophrenia patients and controls). The paper reports within-task contrasts (lake reasoning > color naming; last fish with decision > preceding fish) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 random-effects, FWE-corrected results) with coordinates and tables/figures. Thus it meets the review’s requirements for an ambiguous decision-making task, an active task-versus-control contrast, whole-brain group-level activation maps, and participant groups within the eligible set. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

The study is excluded because it does not report group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked activation maps; analyses are ROI-based only. (a) Exclusion met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI with human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (contrast of ambiguous task vs control condition / within-task comparisons), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). (c) Inclusion not met: I6 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because failing I6 triggers exclusion under E6, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion: E6 and E7 apply. The study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (moving dots) and compared coherence levels (12% vs 50%), so I4 and I5 are met; participant criteria I7 is met. However, the paper reports ROI-based directed connectivity (spectral Granger causality among predefined ROIs) and net causal outflows, without presenting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map or whole-brain contrast maps (no voxelwise 'low coherence > high coherence' activation map or coordinates/tables indicating whole-brain task activations). Therefore it violates inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain results) and E7 (only effective/connectivity analyses without whole-brain task activation map). Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (and thus I8 not applicable). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans that used four perceptual decision-making tasks (face-house, happy-angry face, audio-visual synchrony/asynchrony, and random dot motion) with manipulations of difficulty/ambiguity (noise levels, coherence, asynchrony). The authors report within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., noisy > clear, low coherence > high coherence, asynchrony > synchrony) that match the perceptual-DM contrast forms in the inclusion criteria. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM8 voxelwise results with thresholding and tables of activations/coordinates reported. Therefore I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not only task>rest contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a sequential foraging task with probabilistic (risky) outcomes.
