It meets inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task with probabilistic/risky choices), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric effects comparing foraging vs waiting and value differences between choice options), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported with FWE correction and maps available), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables; supplementary data shared). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and contains within-task contrasts rather than only between-group effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (BART) (I4); it reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (Choose Inflate vs. Choose Win; Outcome Inflate vs. Outcome Explode) suitable for risky-DM contrasts (I5); analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level with cluster correction and reported in tables/figures (I6, I8); participant groups (high-risk and healthy youth, ages 10–14) are acceptable (I7). The task is a canonical risky-DM paradigm and contrasts are not against implicit baseline, results are not ROI-only or PET, and whole-text methods, results and figures are present, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a delayed matching-to-sample (perceptual) decision-making task (checking task) during scanning. It includes at least one within-task decision-making contrast (decision-making followed by checking behavior (DFCB+) > decision-making not followed by checking behavior (DFCB−)), reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects, FDR-corrected). Participant groups (OCD patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging acquisition, preprocessing and statistics), Results (whole-brain and ROI analyses) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts.

Although this is an fMRI study (Stoplight Task) of risky decision-making with whole-brain, group-level analyses, it does not report an explicit decision-making contrast of the required form (e.g., risky > safe or task > active control). The paper reports go and stop trials modeled versus implicit baseline and compares social-context conditions (mother vs adult) for those trial types, but no risky>safe (or equivalent) contrast is presented. Thus the study’s only decision-related contrasts appear to be against implicit baseline, which meets exclusion criterion E3.

This is an fMRI study in humans of risky decision making using mixed gambles and choices (P_max, G_max, L_min). The paper reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., P_max > magnitude-sensitive choices; G_max vs L_min) and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected maps). Participants are healthy young adults. Results include whole-brain activation maps and ROI/ connectivity analyses reported in text and supplemental materials. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making with whole-brain contrasts and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports an fMRI investigation of decision-making under uncertainty using a modified “beads” task (ambiguous decision-making). It includes an explicit task-versus-active-control contrast (DECISION > COUNTING), performed as whole-brain, group-level analyses (SPM5) with coordinates and figures reported. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. All required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no implicit-baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study (group, n=13) that administered a decision-making task under uncertainty (maze goal-search with partially observable states) and reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (subtraction goal-search > visuomotor and parametric regressions with HCP entropy and BT probability). The task manipulates uncertainty/ambiguity about current state (HCP entropy), matching the meta-analysis’ ambiguous decision-making domain. Active control (yoked visuomotor) and within-task contrasts/regressors were used rather than implicit baseline. Methods state whole-brain SPM random-effects analyses with thresholding and reported coordinates. Participants were healthy humans. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets inclusion I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with manipulated sensory evidence (high vs low coherence). The authors report within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual DM (High>Low and Low>High sensory evidence; sensory task vs baseline) and additional contrasts for motor preparation (eye/hand). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (mixed-effects FLAME1+2) voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction; results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (card-guessing/betting) task. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., self-selected vs. computer-selected trials; previous win vs. loss; interactions) at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinates/tables. The task and contrasts map onto risky decision-making contrasts and satisfy the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a decision-making task that manipulates risk, estimation uncertainty, and unexpected uncertainty (restless multi-armed bandit). The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (FWE-corrected) and provide coordinates and figures for parametric contrasts (e.g., phasic activation correlating with risk at cue: regions showing linear increases with risk), which constitute within-task condition contrasts equivalent to high-risk > low-risk or risker > surer. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is cited but not required. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not task>rest-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (the HiLo game). It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., 50% uncertainty vs 100% certainty; linear contrasts across uncertainty levels) that directly test ambiguity-related decision processes. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using FLAME with cluster correction (z>2.3, p<.05), and coordinates for significant clusters (ACC: x=-2,y=22,z=38) are reported. Participants are healthy adolescents and adults within the eligible age range. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI ambiguous decision-making, condition contrasts, and whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study with human participants performing a monetary risky decision-making task (gamble choices) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The authors used within-task parametric contrasts comparing neural responses across probability levels (linear p term and nonlinear deviation Δ(p)), and report whole-brain random-effects results (tables and figures) identifying regions (e.g., striatum) correlated with those decision variables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (experimental paradigm, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and fMRI results with tables/figures), and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced but not required. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

Excluded per E5: The task is a reinforcement-learning probabilistic reward/loss learning paradigm focused on prediction error signals, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported with FWE-corrected results), I7 (participant group qualifies: schizophrenia patients and controls), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in the text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (the task does not constitute one of the review’s target decision-making domains—risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM—as operationalized), and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast of the admitted forms such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; contrasts center on prediction-error regressors and gain>loss motivational context rather than the specified risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the meta-analysis criteria: (1) It acquired fMRI while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making (Gabor detection) task (I4). (2) It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., expectation-incongruent > expectation-congruent; unexpected > expected), satisfying the required decision-making condition contrasts for perceptual DM (I5). (3) Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise GLMs with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and reported peak coordinates (I6). (4) Participant sample consists of healthy adult humans (I7). (5) Whole-brain results are described in the text/tables/figures (I8). The full text supplied includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Given these points, the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is a human fMRI study that manipulated decision uncertainty (20–50%) during an active decision-making task and measured task-evoked BOLD responses. The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (including strict multiple-comparison correction) and parametric/condition comparisons of high versus low uncertainty (i.e., uncertainty-dependent activation), satisfying an ambiguous decision-making contrast. Participants were healthy humans. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study investigates free hand choice (Choice vs Instruct) and hand-specific motor planning, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and clearly describes results in the text, but it does not contain any of the required contrast forms for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual) and I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps) and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text). Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that explicitly investigates perceptual decision-making under high vs low visibility. It contains a whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analysis (searchlight decoding and random-effects GLM) comparing decision conditions (low visibility/guessing vs high visibility/perceptual) analogous to hard>easy or low-coherence>high-coherence contrasts. Whole-brain results are reported in the text and figures. Participants meet eligibility, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only) are violated. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete.

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in human participants performing a decision-making task that explicitly manipulates risk and ambiguity. Behavioral and fMRI analyses include condition-versus-condition contrasts (ambiguity > risk and main effect of condition), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported cluster coordinates/tables. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable per the review. Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures; contrasts are not against implicit baseline only. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, task>rest-only) are met. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI task (Balloon Analog Risk Task) administered during scanning to human participants (I4). It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions: choose win > choose inflate (choice-phase) and outcome inflate > explode (outcome-phase), which map onto risky decision-making contrasts (I5). The authors performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise permutation testing (group-level task-evoked whole-brain analysis is described), even though no clusters survived correction; this satisfies I6 (whole-brain analysis was performed and reported). The sample (youth with ADHD/DBD) is an eligible participant group (I7). Whole-brain analyses and their (null) results are described in the text, satisfying I8. Although significant effects were reported only in ROI analyses, the presence and reporting of the group-level whole-brain analysis means the study meets inclusion rather than being excluded under E6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in human participants that administered a perceptual decision-making task (visual motion direction discrimination) during task fMRI and reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps. The authors modelled parametric effects of motion coherence (20/40/80%) across trials, providing within-task contrasts equivalent to perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., low-coherence/hard vs high-coherence/easy via parametric modulation). Task-related whole-brain group analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected maps) and peak coordinates are reported. Participants are healthy humans. Although the paper emphasizes resting-state connectivity, the presence of whole-brain task activation maps and appropriate within-task contrasts meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choice between high-risk and low-risk options). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests) with thresholding and lists activation foci (Table 1, figures) for contrasts/ regressors related to decision variables (difference in weights/high-risk vs low-risk representation and reward prediction errors). The task and analyses therefore satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for (1) fMRI during risky decision-making, (2) condition-wise/task-vs-control-type contrasts via model-derived decision regressors (high- vs low-risk value difference and prediction error), (3) group-level whole-brain statistical maps, (4) an acceptable participant sample (healthy adults), and (5) reporting of whole-brain results in figures/tables. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion included). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that used a risky decision-making task (Modified Cups Task) during scanning and reports within-task contrasts comparing decisions after losses vs after wins (riskloss > riskwin and vice versa). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates. The task and contrasts directly probe risky decision-making and meet the meta-analysis focus. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than baseline). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study uses an abstract moral/social value word forced-choice task (individualistic vs collectivistic) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is moral/social decision-making, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual) and E3 (the main modeled decision contrast collapses all trials into one decision condition assessed against an implicit baseline; no qualifying condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results and peak coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and I5 (no qualifying decision-condition versus decision-condition or experimental task versus active control contrast). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (monetary lotteries). The authors present within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices (behavioral and BOLD contrasts) and examine modulation by regulation (Look vs Relax). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with FDR thresholding and tables/coordinates of regions (e.g., Table 2), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4–I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study uses an intertemporal choice (delay discounting) task (temporal discounting / Intertemporal Choice Task). The meta-analysis explicitly excludes delay discounting/intertemporal choice tasks (Exclusion E5). The paper does include group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and condition-vs-control contrasts (satisfying I6 and I8), and participant groups are acceptable (I7). However it does not examine risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (I4 not met) and therefore does not provide the eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts required (I5 not met). Full text appears complete. Accordingly the study must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house discrimination near threshold). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., HF > FH, FFhc > HHhc), and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected results, coordinates and figures). Participants are healthy adults. Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures. The full text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants (18–25 y) who performed an in-scanner reward/anticipation task with uncertainty and subsequent out-of-scanner risky choice, i.e. a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper includes within-task condition contrasts (e.g., possible win anticipation vs neutral; a parametric uncertain reward-expectancy regressor) that compare decision-making conditions rather than implicit baseline. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain multiple regression in SPM with FWE correction and reported peaks). Participant groups are acceptable per criteria and whole-brain results are described. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to implicit baseline contrasts, not PET, the task is risky decision-making (not excluded task types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the study is empirical fMRI task activation work. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making tasks (criterion comparison and signal detection) with explicit manipulations of difficulty/uncertainty (easy vs difficult; varying coherence/signal level). The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM and searchlight MVPA results (voxelwise analyses, cluster-corrected) and provide Talairach coordinates and figures. Contrasts compare decision conditions (parametric uncertainty modulation; difficult>easy/low coherence>high coherence-type effects) and include a task versus active control (categorization vs letter-identification) analysis. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study employed fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) and reports a risky > safe contrast, all reported fMRI analyses were conducted using an a priori ROI approach with small-volume corrections. The paper does not present unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making) and I5 (risky > safe contrast) and I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group maps). Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making task, with task versus active control block contrasts (experimental block vs control block). Group-level whole-brain one-sample and two-sample t-tests were performed and reported, and results are described in text, tables and figures. Participants were healthy adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI task contrasts and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This is an fMRI study in humans that directly manipulates risky and ambiguous decision-making (Social Context Decision Task) and reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (Risk > Ambiguity and Dangerous > Safe). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM8 results with FWE-corrected clusters reported in tables/figures. Participants are healthy human groups (adolescents and young adults). Although scenarios are social, the task explicitly manipulates risk and ambiguity, matching the meta-analysis focus. All inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in which human adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) in the scanner (meets I4). The paper reports within-task, condition-vs-condition contrasts involving decision types (go=risky and stop=safe) across social contexts (peer vs parent), i.e., comparisons of decision-making conditions (meets I5). Analyses were group-level, whole-brain random-effects maps with cluster correction and results shared on NeuroVault (meets I6 and I8). Participant sample falls within acceptable ages and groups (meets I7). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study does not rely solely on baseline contrasts, is not PET, reports whole-brain task activation (not ROI-only), and includes task contrasts beyond seed-based connectivity (so E3,E4,E6,E7,E8,E9 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making (animal detection) task with manipulated motivation. Relevant contrasts meeting the review definitions are reported (NEGATIVE > NEUTRAL, POSITIVE > NEUTRAL; task blocks also contrasted against an active arrow baseline). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and reported (FWE-corrected whole-brain tables and figures), and ROI results are supplementary — i.e., whole-brain results are available. The task is a perceptual decision-making paradigm (detection), so it fits the perceptual-DM category. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not PET, not rest-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion IDs met: E5 (task is dynamic reward-learning/exploration-exploitation rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation) and E3 (the reported contrasts are model-based regressors and event onsets rather than condition-versus-condition contrasts of the admitted forms). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI on human participants during a decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (participant sample acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no contrast matching required forms such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or perceptual hard>easy; no within-task condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast presented). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic (risky) monetary decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric correlations (EV vs RM, TD error, uncertainty) and conjunction analyses—i.e., condition-versus-condition effects rather than task>rest. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain/random-effects SPM results with voxelwise statistics and reported peak coordinates (with whole-brain and SVC corrections). Participants are healthy adults. Results and coordinates are fully reported in the main text and figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects that directly manipulates outcome probability (risk) within a decision-making task (options with differing probabilities and delays) and reports group-level whole-brain task-versus-control contrasts. The authors present a decision-making condition contrasted against active control tasks (summation and visual controls) and report voxelwise random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Although the paradigm also includes delay, the critical manipulation involves probabilistic (risky) choices and a parametric subjective-value regressor; thus it fits the meta-analysis scope of risky decision-making. Full text (methods, results, figures, tables, and coordinates) is available. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, implicit-baseline-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task, with analyses linking neural activation to increasing risk (balloon size/adjusted pumps). It provides a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map (correlation maps transformed to z-scores and t-tested at group level) and reports peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The neural contrast is a within-task parametric modulation of risk level (effectively high-risk > low-risk), satisfying the required decision-making contrast forms. Participants include adolescents with TBI and healthy controls (eligible sample types). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only, and within-task whole-brain effects are reported). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a decision-making task manipulating uncertainty (certain vs uncertain trials). The authors report a within-task contrast (uncertain > certain) that maps ambiguity-related activation and conduct group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, whole-brain thresholds) with results described in text, tables, and figures. Participants include clinical (alcoholic) and healthy groups, both acceptable. The task and contrasts directly match ambiguous decision-making criteria (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not only connectivity, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI study of human decision making under known probabilistic uncertainty (70% vs 30%) using a two-choice prediction task, meeting the meta-analysis focus on risky/uncertain decision-making. The experiment includes an active control task and reports within-task contrasts (prediction > control) for both age groups and group comparisons. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 results with corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, tables, figures, and discussion, so the report is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Excluded because the task is a value-based cost–benefit integration without explicit risk, ambiguity, or a perceptual decision-making manipulation. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (did not implement a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review) and I5 (the allowed contrast forms are specified for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM; the study’s contrasts are value-based comparisons and model-driven PPIs rather than the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making task (Stoplight) performed in the scanner, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts including Go > Stop (risky > safe) and other relevant contrasts (Crash > NoCrash), meeting I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with reported coordinates and cluster thresholds (tables and figures), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample (healthy adolescents) is an eligible group under I7. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not only task>implicit baseline), results include whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), and this is not PET or non-empirical. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used fMRI while human participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task) (I4). It reports task condition contrasts including advantageous versus disadvantageous decisions, win versus loss evaluations, and decision versus control trials (active control) (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (FLAME, cluster-corrected), with reported clusters/coordinates (I6, I8). Participant groups (heavy cannabis users and matched controls) are acceptable (I7). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it is complete. No exclusion criteria are met: not PET, not ROI-only, not rest/baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are reported. Therefore include for meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in humans that used a lottery decision task manipulating reward probabilities (prior and likelihood) and sample-size (uncertainty) during choices between lotteries. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (GLMs) with corrected statistical maps and coordinates (e.g., mPFC, striatum, occipital cortex) and contrasts/parametric effects comparing decision conditions (e.g., sample-size conditions, parametric regressors for prior/likelihood/posterior and likelihood uncertainty). Participants were healthy adults. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric comparisons across conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports event-related fMRI data collected while human participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task), satisfying I4. The authors created condition-versus-condition contrasts (win minus neutral; loss minus neutral) and modeled response and feedback phases, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses were performed (independent t-tests; results reported with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values, with small-volume correction noted), satisfying I6. Participant groups (ADHD and healthy controls) are acceptable per I7. Whole-brain results and coordinates are reported in the text/figures, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET modality, only ROI results, task>rest only contrasts, or only connectivity/resting-state analyses) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (Gain vs Loss trials) during whole-brain BOLD acquisition. The authors model a trial-by-trial parametric regressor (‘Gamble Risk’) and report within-task contrasts (risk parametric effects, Valence: Gain > Loss comparisons and related interactions), as well as ON vs OFF medication and group interactions. Imaging analyses are whole-brain (SPM5) with FDR correction and results are described in the text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only, not a review). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides whole-brain contrasts suitable for meta-analysis.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study of risky decision-making (sequential gambling ‘pig’ task) in healthy human participants. It reports within-task contrasts and parametric modulators (e.g., “continue” trials modulated by cumulative gambling, stop probability) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical maps (one-sample t tests, whole-brain thresholds, and cluster-level FWE), with coordinates and SVC results. Participants are healthy volunteers. Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures/tables described, discussion).

This is an empirical human fMRI study that administered a risky decision-making (mixed-gamble) task during scanning and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results. The fMRI analyses include parametric contrasts directly testing decision parameters (e.g., |p-0.5| reflecting high uncertainty > low uncertainty, EV-related correlations) and report cluster-level corrected whole-brain maps. Participants are healthy human volunteers. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, enabling assessment of task contrasts and whole-brain statistics. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study acquired whole‑brain group fMRI data during a task involving risk (detection probability) and reports Dis vs Hon contrasts at the outcome phase, it is a social/moral dishonesty paradigm rather than a canonical risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision‑making task. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is social/moral decision‑making (dishonesty) which the metaanalysis excludes. Moreover, the reported fMRI contrasts focus on outcome presentation (Dis vs Hon at feedback) rather than decision‑period contrasts of interest (e.g., risky > safe); therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one decision‑making contrast) is not met in this paper. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky/uncertain task), I6 (group-level whole‑brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole‑brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no decision‑period risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Given E5 is met, the study must be excluded from the decision‑making meta‑analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (a risky/probabilistic decision-making paradigm). It reports within-task contrasts decoding behavioral decisions (switch vs. stay) based on trial-wise neural activity, which constitutes a within-task decision-making contrast relevant to risky/uncertain decisions. The paper includes group-level random-effects analyses and whole-brain visualizations (Fig. 2B) and describes voxelwise analyses and preprocessing, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants were healthy humans, and whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in the text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-making task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrast — switch vs. stay), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (gambling) task. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decisions after Norisk vs Riskwin; Risk vs Norisk; RA > FG > RD) and analyzes decision-related and feedback-related BOLD responses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected, GRFT) with MNI coordinates and tables; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are present. The participants are healthy adults and results are clearly described in methods, results and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a naturalistic risky decision-making task). The analysis includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (prepump vs pre-cash out; i.e., risky vs safe) and univariate contrast maps, whole-brain searchlight and whole-brain classifier analyses at the group level. Results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The task directly assesses risky decision-making and meets the meta-analysis definitions for risky-DM contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study should be included.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task, with participants scanned while performing active-choice and passive-no-choice conditions. It presents within-task risk-level contrasts (parametric modulation of probability of explosion; effectively high-risk > low-risk comparisons) and an active-choice vs passive-no-choice contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise, with multiple-comparison cluster correction; results are reported as clusters/coordinates and figures. Participants are human young adults (twins), and whole-brain task activation maps are described and used for voxelwise genetic modeling. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans that investigates perceptual decision-making (categorization under sensory uncertainty). It reports within-task comparisons of decision-related conditions (radial vs concentric choices; analyses of stimuli near the category boundary/hard vs easier trials) and uses whole-brain, group-level searchlight MVPA with second-level t-tests (voxelwise maps reported; p<0.0001 cluster-threshold). The study includes full methods, results, and group whole-brain statistical analyses, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements for perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans using a gambling task that manipulates reward uncertainty (uncertain, probable, certain) during decision-making, i.e., a risky/ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., uncertain wins > probable wins; probable wins > probable losses) and examines outcome effects (wins vs losses). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (t-to-z maps, exploratory whole-brain contrasts) and ROI definitions derived from whole-brain contrasts. Participants were healthy adults. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous DM), I5 (condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/analyses). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only task>rest contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text is complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI collected while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (CUPS) and includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (risky vs non-risky and parametric modulators of risk and reward). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (FLAME random-effects, cluster-corrected maps, tables/figures with coordinates). Participants include casual methamphetamine users and non-users, which is acceptable per study population criteria. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and not task>baseline only). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains). It reports within-group and between-group, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses including a risky > safe contrast (risky vs safe choices) and reward vs punishment contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain analyses with tables/figures and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (risky fMRI task; appropriate contrasts; whole-brain group-level maps; acceptable participant group; coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents that implemented a risky vs ambiguous decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) during scanning, reported condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Risk Gamble > Ambiguity Gamble, Ambiguity Gamble > Risk Gamble, Gain > No Gain), and conducted group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE cluster correction and MNI coordinates. Participants are a healthy adolescent sample (11–24 yrs). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulates outcome uncertainty in a decision task (2-choice certain vs 4-choice uncertain reversal learning). It includes a within-subject contrast that directly tests uncertainty effects (4-choice > 2-choice) on responses to unexpected non-reinforcement relative to expected reinforcement, which maps onto ambiguous decision-making contrasts (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise (FSL/FEAT; Z-thresholding and cluster correction), and results are reported as coordinate tables and figures. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not baseline-only contrasts; not connectivity-only; not non-empirical; includes within-task condition contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making (mixed-gamble) task (I4). The paper includes condition-vs-condition contrasts and tests of decision factors (e.g., positive vs negative EV, high vs low uncertainty, high vs low urgency, and interactions)—satisfying the required decision-making contrasts (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM8 flexible factorial second-level analysis; voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction), and whole-brain results are reported (I6, I8). Participants are healthy humans (I7), which is an eligible group. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not rely solely on task>rest contrasts (it reports direct condition contrasts), is not PET, includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and is an empirical fMRI activation study. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI (BOLD) study in healthy human participants performing a gambling/guessing task with uncertainty. It includes task contrasts comparing predicting (guessing) versus reporting (an active control) and difficulty contrasts (suit > colour, hard > easy), analyzed with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM methods and reported as activation foci/figures. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (decision task > control and hard>easy contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (human participants; healthy sample), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, etc.). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study administering a probabilistic (beads) decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (ambiguous decision-making). It includes within-task contrasts suitable for the meta-analysis (lake decision > colour decision; last fish > all previous fish), including an explicit task-versus-control contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM8; FWE-corrected whole-brain results and coordinate tables) alongside ROI checks. Participant groups (ARMS patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. Results and coordinates are fully described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not only baseline contrasts; whole-brain maps reported; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans that administered a mixed gain–loss gambling task (risky decision-making) during scanning and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts of decision-related activity. The paper presents within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of decision phase by gain–loss ratio; linear and quadratic effects; within-group and between-group contrasts) rather than only task>baseline, and reports whole-brain SPM8 results with stereotactic coordinates and cluster-level inference. Participants include both pathological gamblers and healthy controls (acceptable per eligibility). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state/connectivity-only, implicit-baseline-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides usable whole-brain activation results.

This is an fMRI study using a probabilistic passive-avoidance task (70% reward/punishment contingencies) that involves decision-making under uncertainty (risky decision-making). The study models decision-phase (approach vs avoid) and feedback-phase (reward/punishment) with parametric modulators (expected value and prediction error), and reports both ROI and whole-brain group-level (voxelwise) analyses (whole-brain results reported in Table 4 and main-effect analyses within the nonmaltreated group). Within-task condition contrasts (approach vs avoidance; reward vs punishment feedback; EV/PE-modulated responses) are present, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Participants are human children (age 10–15), an acceptable participant group. The full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans performing the Iowa Gambling Task, which assesses risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2) and provides contrasts comparing decision-making vs an active control task and choices from risky versus safe decks (risky > safe), with coordinates and cluster statistics. Participants were healthy adult males. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a perceptual decision-making task (GO/NO-GO). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM) for parametric contrasts and categorical contrasts across levels of predictive information (within-task condition comparisons), including conjunctions and clusterwise/FWE-corrected inference. Results are reported in the text and supplemental tables/figures. Thus the paper provides whole-brain, task-evoked activation maps for perceptual decision-making contrasts (decision-related parametric and categorical contrasts), meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps (I6) and includes participant groups that are acceptable for the review (patients and controls; I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text/tables (I8). However, the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning/reward-learning paradigm and the reported contrasts are feedback-related (negative vs positive feedback; final reversal vs reversal error; final reversal error vs correct), not the decision-making contrasts required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrasts). It also does not unambiguously meet I4 as a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making manipulation per the meta-analysis definitions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are directly triggered, but because not all inclusion criteria are met (notably I5 and I4), the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney face detection) and a dual-task design that separates decision from motor response. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (voxelwise maps, RFX contrasts and tables of coordinates) and data-driven ICA corroboration. Relevant within-task contrasts compare decision-related regressors (Decision_response, Decision_color) against stimulus and motor regressors, providing condition-versus-condition contrasts that index perceptual decision processes. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, task, image acquisition, GLM/ICA analysis), Results (behavioral, GLM, ICA, event-related averages) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in humans that explicitly examined risky decision-making using a lottery choice task (risk manipulated via coefficient of variation). The fMRI analysis included a group-level whole-brain analysis testing how CV for chosen gambles modulated BOLD during the decision phase (reporting higher vs lower risk effects in bilateral anterior insula with FWE correction), which constitutes condition-vs-condition/riskier>safer contrasts (parametric modulation). Participants are human adolescents (eligible by I7). Whole-brain results and coordinates/ROIs are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and whole-brain group-level contrasts.

This is an fMRI study that includes a probability discounting task (risky decision-making) performed during scanning and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The authors computed contrasts/parametric regressors for subjective value separately for probability (PD) and delay (DD) trials, conducted comparisons between PD and DD (regions showing better correlations for PD than DD and vice versa), and conjunction analyses. Results are reported as whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with coordinates and figures (supplemental tables). The sample is healthy human participants. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analog Risk Task, a risky decision-making paradigm. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts comparing decision events to an active control (e.g., Pumps > Control), parametric modulation contrasts, and other task-versus-control contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FSL FLAME1; cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) with peak coordinates reported. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in human healthy adults using the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts (risky > safe; punishment feedback > risky; multiple punished-then-risky and risky-then-risky contrasts) and subject- and group-level analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (voxel-wise threshold P<0.001 with cluster correction; tables/figures and ROI results are provided). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., not PET, not task>rest only, includes whole-brain results beyond ROI).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing the Iowa Gambling Task (risky decision-making). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) and provides coordinate-based results and figures. Relevant contrasts include risk-related contrasts (bad > good deck; ‘risk effect’) and framed-message versus control comparisons (heightened-risk effect), which meet the accepted forms for risky decision-making contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied and the study should be included.

This is a human fMRI study in healthy adults performing a card gambling task manipulating risk (six risk levels). The analysis included within-task contrasts across risk levels (e.g., low-risk vs high-risk; regressors for each risk level; control > ketanserin contrasts for low-risk negative outcomes) meeting the risky-DM contrast formats. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed in SPM5 with FWE cluster correction and coordinates reported. Thus the study satisfies: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (condition contrasts comparing risk levels), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than only task>baseline, modality is fMRI (not PET), task is risky decision-making (not an excluded decision type), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and task activation maps (not only connectivity or only between-group contrasts) are provided. Full text is complete and includes methods, results and discussion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that manipulated probabilistic (risky) decision-making (Gambling blocks) and deterministic rule-based choices, and reports contrasts between decision conditions (e.g., low vs. high choice certainty; complex rule-based vs. high-certainty probabilistic). Group-level voxelwise analyses and activation foci are reported (tables and SPM analyses), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task and contrasts directly address risky/probabilistic decision-making relevant to the review. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (reports whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps/SPMs and group-level PLS maps), I7 (human participant sample; healthy volunteers allowed), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/maps). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks — NOT met: tasks are Recognition, Trail-Making, and Sustained Attention), I5 (no contrasts of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision conditions as defined — NOT met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making task manipulating outcome uncertainty. The task contrasts two-choice prediction (decision under uncertainty) with an active control (two-choice response task) and explicitly tests an uncertainty contrast (50% error rate vs 20%/80% error rates; contrast vector = high uncertainty > low uncertainty). The analysis is whole-brain, voxelwise (AFNI, Talairach normalization, cluster correction) with group-level mixed-model ANOVA and coordinates/figures reported. Participants include schizophrenia subjects and matched healthy controls. Reporting includes task-versus-control and uncertainty-related contrasts, and whole-brain maps/tables/figures. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving game). It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (Go > Stop) and outcome contrasts (Pass > Crash), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) with reported peak coordinates. Participants are healthy humans and whole-brain results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a human fMRI study in which participants performed a two-alternative instrumental choice task with probabilistic action–outcome contingencies (decision-making under uncertainty). The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts showing BOLD covariation with task-derived decision variables (parametric modulators for relative advantage P and value difference D) with SPM group one-sample t-tests and FWE cluster correction, and provide peak coordinates and statistical thresholds. These constitute within-task, condition-wise comparisons (parametric high vs low P/D bins and related contrasts) rather than task>rest baselines. The paper also includes whole-brain chosen-value contrasts and reports results in tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults (n=20). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text is complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that directly probes risky decision-making using monetary gambles (high-probability small payoff vs low-probability large payoff). The paper reports within-task and between-task contrasts (parametric regressors for intradimensional vs unidimensional differences; preferential choice vs judgment-based choice paired t-tests), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5; cluster-corrected results, reported peak MNI coordinates). Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates and figures. Subjects are healthy adults. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition and task-vs-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that directly contrasts decision-making under ambiguity and risk, reporting condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > risky, risk effects) during the decision phase. The analysis used group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise statistics with cluster and voxel thresholds reported, and results are described in the text and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods (imaging and behavioral), results, and discussion, so the full article appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task). It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (disadvantageous decks vs advantageous decks — corresponding to risky > safe) as well as decision > baseline contrasts, and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group and between-group statistical maps (whole-brain corrected thresholds reported). Participant samples are acceptable per inclusion criteria. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making with whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (the study does not rely solely on implicit baseline contrasts, is not PET, includes whole-brain maps beyond ROI or connectivity-only results, and reports within-group task effects).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a multi-attribute decision-making task where trials systematically varied the variability (ambiguity) of value predictions. The authors explicitly decoded variability (sorted into four groups) and tested where in the brain variability/ambiguity information was represented, performing group-level, voxelwise second-level statistics on whole-brain searchlight accuracy maps and reporting MNI coordinates. This constitutes a condition-vs-condition (high vs low variability/ambiguity) analysis appropriate for ambiguous decision-making contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports whole-brain coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements.

This study used task-based fMRI in human participants performing an anticipation task with an 'uncertain event' versus 'certain reward' contrast (meets I4 and I5). Participant sample and reporting (healthy adults) are acceptable (meets I7), and peak coordinates are reported (meets I8). However, the reported analyses were restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction (SVC) within those regions; there is no evidence of an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map. Because the paper reports only ROI-based voxel searches/SVC without whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This article reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a monetary guessing task with uncertain outcomes (decision-making under uncertainty), satisfying the risky decision-making domain. The study includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports task contrasts (gain > loss; feedback and reward-relevant trials versus reward-neutral control trials are modeled), with cluster-corrected whole-brain results presented in figures and tables. Participants are human (healthy young adults). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision task), I5 (within-task contrast comparing decision-making conditions and task vs control), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses, PET, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) during scanning, and it reports the critical contrast of risky > safe choices. The authors performed group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (one-sample t-tests on contrast images, with cluster correction) and report coordinates and ROI results; thus whole-brain task-evoked maps are available. Participant groups (suicide attempters, affective controls, healthy controls) are acceptable under the review’s participant inclusions. The contrasts and task directly map onto the meta-analysis objective of risky decision-making. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only, and is empirical). Full text is complete (includes methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used the BIAS financial decision-making task (stocks vs bond) manipulating uncertainty/risk and measured BOLD while participants made choices. It reports task contrasts relevant to the review (neural representation of uncertainty as a parametric modulation, and comparisons preceding bond vs stock choices — i.e., risk-avoidant vs risk-seeking), at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported clusters, tables/figures). Participants include clinical (violent offenders subgroups) and healthy controls, which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (with tables/figures referenced). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study reports an fMRI experiment (BART) involving risky decision making in human participants, with within-task contrasts distinguishing risky versus safe choices and parametric modulators (e.g., ChooseInflate*P(explode), ChooseWin*P(explode)) and planned contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (with FDR and cluster correction) including coordinate tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, task>rest-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic decision-making task that manipulates risk. The authors modelled trial-by-trial risk prediction and used GLM parametric regressors to produce group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster- and voxel-level corrected) identifying regions correlating with risk prediction; they report and correlate these maps with behavior and personality. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric modulation indexing risk prediction across conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state-only; not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic multi-cue decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty and time pressure. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (parametric modulation by subjective and objective sum of evidence, phase contrasts HighP>LowP, conjunctions) with corrected voxelwise cluster results and tables of clusters. Task contrasts compare decision conditions (low vs high time pressure) and parametric contrasts indexing uncertainty/evidence (high vs low SoE), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (mixed gambles) and includes healthy participants, but it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map or coordinate tables. The analyses are ROI-based univariate regressions and PPI/DCM effective connectivity across predefined ROIs. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results and is effectively an ROI/connectivity-only report.
(a) Exclusion IDs met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E7 (reports effective/seed-based connectivity without reporting a whole-brain task activation map). 
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I7 (healthy participants). 
(c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no explicit admitted form contrast such as risky>safe or similar categorical decision-making contrast reported as voxelwise map), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map), I8 (no whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures/tables). 
Full text completeness: fulltext appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given E6/E7, exclude from the meta-analysis.

The study includes an fMRI experiment in human participants that manipulated decision difficulty via manual bistability (ambiguous posture selection) and modeled a parametric predictor of bistability (a within-task decision-making contrast analogous to hard>easy). The analysis produced group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps of the parametric effect, reported in text/tables/figures. Participants were healthy adults. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, not only baseline contrasts). Hence it meets inclusion criteria for perceptual/ambiguous decision-making fMRI studies.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used fMRI (I4) while human subjects performed a risky decision-making task (choices between risky gambles and certain outcomes), it includes within-task contrasts comparing gamble versus certainty decisions (I5), reports group-level whole-brain searchlight MVPA maps with a group one-sample t-test and cluster correction (I6), uses an eligible participant sample (healthy adults) (I7), and presents whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>rest), it is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is an empirical fMRI task study. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (I4), reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked results with cluster-level FWE correction (I6), included an eligible participant sample (I7), and presented whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). However, it does not report any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Instead, the fMRI analysis used model-derived parametric modulators for reward prediction errors (RPEcue and RPEoutcome) and between-group comparisons of those parametric effects; no within-task contrast of risky vs safe or ambiguous vs non-ambiguous (I5) is provided. Because I5 is not met, the study does not satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Exclusion criteria met: none of the explicit exclusion items (e.g., PET only, ROI-only) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans using a risky decision-making task (modified Balloon Analog Risk Task) with both active (choice) and passive (no-choice) conditions. It includes within- and between-task contrasts (e.g., active risk vs. passive risk; active inflation vs. passive inflation; active loss vs. passive loss) that directly compare decision-making conditions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects GLM results (normalized to MNI space, reported with whole-brain FDR-corrected thresholds and cluster tables), and results are presented in figures and tables. Participants are healthy humans. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the report is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a Risky-Gains decision-making task (risky vs safe choices). The manuscript includes within-subject contrasts comparing risky > safe and risky > punished conditions, and reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with threshold/cluster correction and Talairach normalization, with coordinates and figures. Personality correlations are ancillary but do not affect eligibility. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (subjects, task, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, voxelwise analysis), Results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging results with tables/figures), and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in humans that collected whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps while participants performed a probabilistic decision-making/learning task involving uncertainty. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., rounds where choices followed System 1 vs System 2, correct vs incorrect choices, parametric value and uncertainty regressors) and random-effects whole-brain analyses (thresholded maps, Talairach normalization). These contrasts qualify as condition-vs-condition decision-making comparisons (within-task). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) with within-task contrasts (rewarded vs nonrewarded; directional probability contrasts). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with statistical maps and tables of coordinates, including t-maps and corrected peaks. Participants are healthy humans and full article includes methods, results, and discussion. These elements satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and do not violate any exclusion criteria.
