This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that directly examines ambiguous decision-making (internal vs external subjective color choices) with within-task contrasts (ISD vs ESD, ISD vs EVD, ESD vs EVD). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM2, FDR-corrected voxelwise results, tables/figures), and contrasts are against an active veridical control (EVD) rather than rest. The paradigm therefore meets criteria for ambiguous decision-making, provides task-versus-task and ambiguous-versus-control contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not PET, not ROI-only, and not resting-state/connectivity-only.

This study acquired fMRI while human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task involving decisions under probabilistic (uncertain) outcomes. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses of task-evoked signals (model-derived reward prediction error (RPE) parametric modulators) with family-wise error correction, and conducted within-task comparisons (RPE modulation; exploratory binning of negative/neutral/positive RPEs) and group comparisons. The task constitutes decision-making under uncertainty (probabilistic/ambiguous learning), and the contrasts (parametric RPE effect and binned RPE comparisons) are within-task decision-related contrasts that are reported at the whole-brain group level. Participants are human and within accepted age range. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only, not resting-state-only, empirical fMRI with whole-brain maps). Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that explicitly examines decision making under risk (explicit probabilities and incentives), using blocked task conditions. It reports a within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise contrast comparing the information-based risk decision condition (A) to an active high-level control condition (B) and provides group-level random-effects results with coordinates. Participants are healthy elderly adults. Whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates).

This is an empirical human fMRI study of reinforcement-based decision making using a probabilistic Paper-Scissors-Rock task that manipulates uncertainty across trials. The authors report within-task contrasts (early trials vs late trials reflecting higher vs lower uncertainty) and group-by-decision-time interactions. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (LME across all voxels with cluster correction) and results (and coordinates) are reported in text, figures, and supplements. Participants include occasional stimulant users and controls (eligible participant groups). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task with uncertainty/risk), I5 (within-task contrast comparing decision conditions: early>late / late>early), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This longitudinal fMRI study used the Wheel of Fortune risky decision-making task and reports a risky vs. safe selection contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (AFNI 3dANOVA3) with cluster correction and results reported in tables/figures (Table 2, Figures). Participants include adolescents who became binge drinkers and matched controls (acceptable participant groups). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no baseline-only contrasts, not PET, task is risky-DM, reports whole-brain results beyond ROIs, not only connectivity, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that implemented risky and ambiguous decision-making tasks during scanning and reports direct condition-vs-condition and condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Gamble Risk > Gamble Ambiguity; Gain > No Gain) as well as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with FWE-corrected inferences and MNI coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task design, MRI acquisition, GLM), Results (whole-brain contrasts, conjunctions, regressions), Discussion, and tables of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human adults performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task). The authors report a within-task contrast 'risky decisions minus safe decisions' (risky > safe), performed at the group-level using random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (statistical parametric maps, voxel- and cluster-level thresholds) and report coordinates/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets fMRI task (I4), appropriate decision-making contrast (I5), whole-brain group-level analysis (I6), participant eligibility (I7), and reporting of coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making paradigm). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing high-risk (decks A/B) versus low-risk (decks C/D) selections (i.e., high-risk > low-risk), and present group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (FSL group analysis, MNI registration, Z-thresholding and cluster correction). Participant groups (pathological gamblers and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only).

This is an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky mixed-lottery decision-making task (lottery choice task) with within-task contrasts and parametric modulation of probability and magnitude. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and model-based one-sample tests), thresholding, and ROI analyses derived from whole-brain results. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and condition-versus-condition/parametric contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Participants are healthy human adults; results include within-group task effects and between-group (age) interactions. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because its decision-making task does not match the meta-analysis focus (Exclusion E5). The paper investigates offline replay and revaluation in a multi-step RL/planning paradigm rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making per the meta-analysis definitions. Although the task includes noisy rewards (uncertainty) and contrasts between revaluation and control conditions, it does not implement canonical risk (e.g., risky > safe) or ambiguity (high uncertainty > low uncertainty) or perceptual difficulty contrasts (hard > easy) required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (human participant sample within acceptable populations), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (did not conduct fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as defined), I5 (does not present one of the admitted decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The manuscript reports an fMRI experiment in which human subjects made risky and ambiguous choices (I4 satisfied) and models condition-specific parametric regressors for risk and ambiguity (within-task contrasts; I5 satisfied). Participant sampling is acceptable (human subjects; I7 satisfied). However, the paper is a methods-oriented JoVE article that presents representative single-subject activation maps and descriptions of the analysis pipeline; it does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map required by the review (I6 NOT met). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not PET, and not task>rest only). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it lacks clearly reported group-level whole-brain results.

This study collected fMRI data while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles), with within-subject contrasts between decision contexts (threat vs safe) and parametric modulation by expected subjective value. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and coordinates are reported; exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected results and ROI results are provided. Participants were healthy adults. Thus the paper provides whole-brain task-evoked maps comparing decision-making conditions (within-task contrasts), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making fMRI studies. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, PET, rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (animal detection) with within-task motivational manipulation (motivated vs neutral) — addressing I4 and providing a condition-versus-condition contrast (motivated > neutral) that qualifies as a decision-making contrast (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (second-level random-effects, whole-brain FWE-corrected results) satisfying I6. Participant groups (medicated schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable per I7. Results are described in full text (tables/coordinates and ROI follow-ups), meeting I8. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., contrasts are not only versus implicit baseline, whole-brain maps are provided, not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study of decision-making under risk and ambiguity that reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (ambiguity > risk and risk > ambiguity) and a random-effects whole-brain analysis. The manuscript describes task design with risky and ambiguous conditions, GLM analyses, and voxelwise group-level results reported in figures and supplementary tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants include healthy subjects (with additional lesion behavioral work that does not negate the fMRI eligibility). All relevant inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, no ROI-only reporting, contrasts are not against implicit baseline only, and it is an empirical fMRI activation study). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but that is acceptable. Therefore, include this study in the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because its decision task is value-based (pleasantness/reward) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (exclusion E5). The paper reports fMRI in humans and contains appropriate contrasts and whole-brain group maps, but the domain of the decision (judging pleasantness of odors / reward-based choice) does not match the meta-analysis target domains. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task contrasts: correct vs error, decision vs rating; ΔI regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain SPM analyses with coordinates reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results/coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task per the meta-analysis scope). No other exclusion criteria applied. Confidence reflects clear domain mismatch based on full text.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants (primary care physicians) performing diagnostic decision-making tasks that explicitly manipulate diagnosticity (high vs low diagnosticity → maps to certainty/uncertainty). It includes within-task condition contrasts comparing diagnostic information of differing diagnosticity and task contrasts (diagnosis vs naming; diagnosis vs prescription), matching the required contrast types (e.g., high uncertainty/low diagnosticity vs low uncertainty/high diagnosticity). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps (SPM12) with peak coordinates and FWE correction reported. Participants are an acceptable human group. Results and maps are reported in the main text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as an ambiguous (uncertainty) decision-making fMRI study.

This fMRI study (wheel-of-fortune risky decision task) meets inclusion criteria I4 (task-based fMRI in humans), I5 (risky > safe contrast: 10/30 vs 70/90), and I7 (healthy participant groups). However, the primary neuroimaging analysis was restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and reported ROI peak coordinates; the paper does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I6. Because the report presents only ROI-limited results (no whole-brain voxelwise maps), it falls under exclusion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group map) and I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables—no qualifying whole-brain results were provided). Therefore the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a two-choice prediction decision-making task with three manipulated error-rate conditions (20%, 50%, 80%). The main contrasts compare error-rate conditions (e.g., 20% vs 80%), meeting the requirement for a within-task decision-making contrast (analogous to high- vs low-uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and cluster-corrected results are reported (voxelwise thresholding, cluster size, Talairach labels; Table 3, figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participant groups (stimulant users and controls) are appropriate per inclusion criteria, and whole-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the study fits the meta-analysis scope of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that directly examines risky decision making (pairs of monetary bets) while scanning (meets I4). The paper reports within- and between-task contrasts (preferential choice vs trade-off instruction choice), and reports task effects (RMANOVA, task main effects and task-based voxelwise connectivity differences), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise activation and connectivity analyses are reported (second-level one-sample t-tests, conjunction analyses, voxel-wise RMANOVAs with FDR/FWE corrections and cluster reporting), meeting I6. Participants are healthy adults (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported with cluster coordinates and figures (meets I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not resting-state/seed-only without whole-brain maps (E7), not solely task>baseline contrasts (E3) because between-task contrasts are reported, and it is an empirical fMRI study (not E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human adults using a risky monetary decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). It reports within-task contrasts (monetary selection > control selection; high-reward/risk > low-reward/risk) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with tables/figures of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI risky DM), I5 (task vs control and high-risk>low-risk contrasts), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion). It reports condition contrasts of interest (low coherence > high coherence), matching the perceptual-DM contrast types in I5. Authors performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses and present group maps/statistics (permutation testing and cluster correction), satisfying I6. Participants are healthy adults (I7). Results and whole-brain maps are reported in the main text and figures (I8). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a monetary gambling task (risky decision-making) and therefore directly addresses the review objective. It includes within-task contrasts comparing levels of risk (a linear gambling-risk contrast and high-risk > low-risk outcome contrasts), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrast requirements. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (second-level SPM8 ANOVA) with reported cluster results and MNI coordinates and FWE correction; ROI-restricted corrections were also used but whole-brain results are present. Participant sample (healthy twins at familial risk) is an allowed subject group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered.

Full text is complete and reports an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain analyses (I6), includes healthy human participants (I7), and reports whole-brain results in the text (I8). However, the task is a social feedback-based person-perception learning paradigm (predicting ‘yes’/‘no’ responses of others) and is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. The study’s contrasts (e.g., incorrect vs. correct feedback; parametric modulation by learning state; yea-sayer vs. naysayer) do not match the required risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and does not meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Excluded on that basis.

This study reports fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion), with detailed methods and results (introduction, methods, results, discussion) present — full text appears complete. The authors report group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses: (1) univariate parametric contrasts relating BOLD to motion coherence (including low-coherence > high-coherence effects), and (2) whole-brain searchlight multivariate classification with group repeated-measures ANOVA and reported peak coordinates/figures. These provide condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual DM (e.g., low coherence vs high coherence) and whole-brain, group-level statistical maps reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy humans performing an explicit risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains Task). It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., +80 vs +40 high-risk > low-risk, and regressors for safe [20] vs risky [40/80]) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (LME) with cluster-corrected results and tables of coordinates. Results are presented in the main text/tables/figures. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts: high-risk>low-risk and safe vs risky regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation with whole-brain analyses in healthy participants (adolescents and adults) and reports whole-brain results; however, the task is a reward-processing Card Guessing Task that the authors explicitly state is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Contrasts are reward vs. no-reward (reward receipt/consumption), not risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy perceptual contrasts. Therefore it fails the required scope for decision-making tasks in this review. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study in human smokers using the Wheel of Fortune, a probabilistic (risky) decision-making task. The paper reports task-versus-control contrasts (money > control) during selection and anticipation phases and win>no-win during outcome, modeled and reported at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables/figures). Participant group (nicotine-dependent smokers) is acceptable. Reporting includes coordinates, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are against an active control (not implicit baseline), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts without within-task effects. Full text is complete.

Full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making card prediction task manipulating outcome uncertainty (uncertain vs. certain). The paper includes an explicit Uncertain > Certain (Uncertain–Certain action selection) contrast, computed voxelwise and tested at the group level with whole-brain analyses and cluster correction; significant clusters and coordinates are reported in Table 2. Participant groups (stimulant users and controls) are acceptable per review scope. The manuscript contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI study of ambiguous/risky decision-making with a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast and reported coordinates.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making task (BART) in human participants, with within-subject contrasts examining risk-related activity and active>passive choice comparisons. Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses were performed (SPM8; Monte Carlo cluster correction) and results are reported in text/tables/figures (VMPFC, dorsomedial PFC, striatum, insula, etc.). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making (I4, I5), provides whole-brain statistical maps/voxelwise results (I6, I8), and uses an eligible participant group (I7). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that includes probabilistic (risky) decision trials and directly contrasts probabilistic versus intertemporal valuation (reports R>D and D>R contrasts). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results with cluster-corrected maps and tabulated local maxima, satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Although the task also includes intertemporal (delay) trials (which alone would be excluded), the presence of risky/probabilistic trials and explicit risk versus delay contrasts makes the study relevant to risky decision-making. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) with within-task contrasts (bad deck > good deck; framed vs control risk effects). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected maps and peak coordinates), and results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates. Participant groups include substance-dependent and non-substance-dependent individuals (eligible per I7). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only ROI/connectivity, not task>rest only, includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This single-case study reports task-based fMRI during decision-making and reports a condition contrast (A>B) and whole-brain voxelwise results, but it is a single-subject (n=1) study rather than a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. Inclusion criterion I6 requires group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) maps; that criterion is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous DM), I5 (explicit condition contrast A>B, task>control), I7 (participant group is acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis are triggered. Because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I6 is not met), the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making card gambling task (meets I4). It reports explicit condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky DM (risk scaled linear contrast; high-risk wins > low-risk wins) matching accepted risky-DM contrast forms (meets I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level maps with reported cluster coordinates and corrected p-values (meets I6). Participants are healthy humans (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and clearly described (meets I8). No exclusion criteria are violated: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not only task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results provided, not ROI/ connectivity-only, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task with stochastic rewards (decision-making under uncertainty/risk). It includes within-task contrasts and model-based regressors that compare decision conditions (e.g., switch > stay, prior-correct/value contrasts, and direct model comparisons state-based vs RL). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates and thresholding, satisfying the meta-analysis reporting requirements. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than task>implicit baseline). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/uncertain decision-making.

This fMRI study (beads/JTC probabilistic inference) involved human participants performing a decision-making task (I4) and included an active control condition (control blocks) allowing task-versus-control comparisons (I5). Participants were healthy adults (I7) and results are described in the full text (I8). However, the analyses are ROI- and multivariate-pattern-based (Harvard-Oxford masks, voxel-selection within ROI masks) and the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; rather, results focus on ROI statistics and selected-voxel patterns. Therefore the study meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map). Because failing any required inclusion criterion and meeting E6 mandates exclusion, I exclude this paper from the meta-analysis.

Exclusion rationale: The study employed fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (a decision-making paradigm), but the reported primary contrasts are outcome valence contrasts (reward > punishment) and positive>neutral picture viewing, not contrasts that manipulate or compare levels of risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty as required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task/contrast does not match risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI with human participants performing a decision-making task — probabilistic reversal learning), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported and described). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (required decision-making contrast comparing risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty was not provided). Full text appears complete.

Although this study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, the analyses reported and emphasized in the paper are limited to the feedback/outcome phase (Win vs. No Win). The meta-analysis requires at least one contrast that compares decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty) or a decision-making task vs an active control (I5). This study does not report or focus on any decision-phase contrasts of risk vs. safe (selection/choice-phase contrasts); instead the primary contrast is reward receipt vs reward absence, which is an outcome/feedback contrast rather than a decision-making contrast of interest. Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) were triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making task (gambles) during scanning. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Decoy > Filler, Decoy > Baseline) and a parametric modulation of decision activity with model-predicted choice probability, satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making contrast. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses were conducted using FSL/FLAME and whole-brain cluster results are reported, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy humans and results are reported in the main text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contrasts are not only versus rest). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and should be included.

Excluded because the fMRI data were acquired during a working-memory (n-back) task and not while participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task) and I5 (a decision-making contrast/task-versus-control). The study does satisfy I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the 2-back>0-back WM contrast), I7 (eligible participant groups: patients and healthy controls), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study tested risky decision-making (child-friendly cake gambling task) during scanning with healthy human participants, reporting contrasts comparing decision conditions (high-risk > low-risk; negative > positive feedback). It includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain section, tables of activations and figures) and reports coordinates and ROI results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. All inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no contrasts only versus baseline, no PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This study meets inclusion for the meta-analysis because it used fMRI while human participants made mixed gambles that included a prospective risk manipulation (prospective risk mixed gambles), and reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and parametric contrasts relating neural activation to prospective risk magnitude. Although the paper also examines effort-based choices (which would be excluded), the presence of a well-specified risky decision-making task with whole-brain analyses (parametric risk levels analogous to high-risk > low-risk) satisfies the review’s scope. Participants were healthy adults and results/maps are available and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study reports ROI-based fMRI analyses and forward-model reconstructions in early visual areas rather than providing a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task) and I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast of the accepted forms such as hard>easy or low-coherence>high-coherence in the main fMRI experiment; coherence was fixed per subject) and I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group activation maps reported; analyses focus on selected ROIs and reconstruction performance). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults performing risky decision-making tasks (lotteries) and social strategic games involving uncertainty. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., risky/B-choice vs sure/A-choice; entry games > lotteries/stag-hunt; non-threshold vs threshold) and group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with reported MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Results are presented in text, figures, and coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain analyses are reported; contrasts are condition-versus-condition, not task>rest; modality is fMRI). Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a two-choice prediction task (uncertain/ambiguous) contrasted directly with a two-choice response task (certain), meeting the requirement for a decision-making vs active control contrast. The methods describe voxelwise, group-level, whole-brain analyses (mixed-model ANOVA, cluster correction, Talairach normalization) and report task-related whole-brain activation results. Participant groups (schizophrenia and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. The paper provides full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of ambiguous/perceptual decision-making with whole-brain contrasts.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a probability (risk) discounting task (probabilistic rewards) and a delay discounting task. The probability discounting task constitutes a risky decision-making paradigm. The main reported contrasts include free vs. forced choice (decision vs. an active, matched control), meeting the requirement for a task-versus-control contrast. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM; coordinates and FWE-corrected results reported), and results are reported as coordinates and figures. Participants include clinical and non-clinical groups (allowed). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study uses a value-rating/social influence task (participants rate products, view others' reviews, and update ratings). Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is social/value updating rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in the text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (does not contain the required decision-making contrasts comparing risky/ambiguous/perceptual conditions of the types listed). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis because it fails to meet the core task-domain inclusion criteria (E5).

This study meets the review inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal-learning task that manipulates outcome uncertainty (risk/ambiguity). The primary imaging contrasts compare punished (probabilistic error) versus rewarded correct responses (a within-task condition-versus-condition contrast relevant to decision-making under uncertainty). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM, cluster-level FWE correction) with results reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Participant groups (ADHD persisters/remitters and matched controls) are acceptable per eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI-only analyses, only connectivity, only PET, or only task>baseline contrasts — it reports whole-brain task activation and within-group contrasts. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Accordingly, include the study.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in humans performing two risky decision-making tasks (ART and BART), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and direct between-task contrasts (ART vs. BART). It therefore meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision tasks), I5 (includes between-task contrasts—ART vs. BART—and within-task parametric contrasts of risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported and thresholded), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (results clearly reported in text/tables/figures). It does not violate exclusion criteria (not limited to implicit-baseline contrasts only, not PET, includes whole-brain results beyond ROIs, not connectivity-only, empirical fMRI study). Full text is complete.

This is a within-subject fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probability-discounting risky choice task during scanning (meets I4). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts indexing decision variables (subjective value, decision conflict) and presents decision-conflict effects (equivalent to hard > easy) and value-related contrasts (meets I5). Analyses were conducted and reported at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise SPM random-effects analyses with thresholds and clusters reported (meets I6). Participants are healthy adult males (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures (meets I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; sufficient detail is present to assess eligibility. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulated risk and ambiguity during a decision-making task (bowling-ball gambles) and acquired BOLD images during task performance. The paper reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (ambiguous > nonambiguous; parametric effect of second-order entropy; other contrasts related to outcome range and risk probability) rather than task>rest, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 RFX one-sample t tests with cluster- and voxel-level corrections) with tables/figures of results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social influence using two-alternative forced choice tasks but the tasks are social decision-making with deterministic reward functions based on choice history rather than risky (probabilistic), ambiguous (unknown probabilities), or perceptual (difficulty/coherence) decision-making. Therefore it does not meet the core domain requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults), I8 (whole-brain results presented/described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task), I5 (no qualifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is social rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a canonical risky decision-making task (Risky Gains). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing risky versus safe responses and punished versus non-punished outcomes, and presents both a-priori ROI and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (with cluster correction), with results described in text, tables, and figures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used a risky decision-making task (modified Lane risk-taking task) performed during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices and feedback conditions (risky > safe; win > safe; loss > safe), and both within-condition and condition-by-task interactions (alcohol vs placebo). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded with cluster correction; results are reported with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy social drinkers. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a two-choice prediction task manipulating error rates (20%, 50%, 80%), which operationalizes risky and ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of significant clusters/coordinates and corrected thresholds. Analyses included comparisons across error-rate conditions and interoception states (e.g., effects during 80% punishment vs other conditions and Group x ER x Interoception interactions), providing within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts rather than only task>implicit-baseline contrasts. Participant groups include methamphetamine users and healthy controls, which is acceptable. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply based on the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (tactile grating orientation) with simultaneous confidence ratings. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (cluster-level FWE correction) and provides contrasts that qualify (perceptual task > motor-control trials, easy vs difficult, correct vs incorrect, and parametric modulation by confidence). Results are presented as figures and tables. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (perceptual task > control and difficulty contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment (3T scanner) collected while healthy human participants performed a risky gamble decision-making task with explicit probabilities (risky > safe equivalence manipulated across trials). The authors conducted group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses and report condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., interactions of decision: gamble vs sure combined with CS effects) rather than task>rest comparisons. Whole-brain results and MNI coordinates are reported (with both an a priori amygdala mask and post-hoc whole-brain exploratory maps). Participants are healthy volunteers. Therefore the paper meets fMRI during risky decision-making (I4), contains decision-condition contrasts (I5), provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (I6) and reports coordinates (I8), and uses an eligible participant group (I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face gender categorization) with manipulation of stimulus coherence (phase noise) and morphing to change difficulty. It reports within-task contrasts comparing noise-present (low coherence) versus noise-absent (higher coherence) and versus control, matching perceptual-DM contrasts (e.g., low coherence > high coherence). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates (Table 1) and conjunctions; ROI analyses are supplemental but do not replace whole-brain maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Although this study used fMRI in human participants performing a risky lottery task (I4) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (I6) with results described in the text and figures (I8), it does not provide at least one accepted risky-decision contrast as required by I5 (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, or experimental risk task > control task). The reported fMRI contrasts focus on social versus private contexts and outcome valence (social gain/loss) and connectivity, not on contrasts that isolate risk level or task-versus-control risk activity. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune). It reports within-task contrasts suitable for risky decision-making (risk/reward 25/75 vs control; high-risk 25% vs low-risk 75%) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (whole-brain analysis conducted and MNI coordinates reported, with ROI/SVC follow-up). Participants are human adolescents (healthy), and whole-brain results are reported in tables/coordinates. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only rest contrasts, ROI-only without whole-brain results, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts) are met. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human adults performing a modified Iowa Gambling Task (decision-making under ambiguity/risk) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. It includes within-task condition contrasts (disadvantageous > advantageous, advantageous > disadvantageous; win > loss; EV-modulated outcome contrasts) satisfying condition-versus-condition contrast requirements. The authors ran whole-brain permutation-based group analyses and report clusterwise results and coordinates, meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Participant group (healthy adult males) is acceptable. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplemental material noted but core article content present). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a 3T fMRI study with human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) while inside the scanner. The authors report within-task contrasts comparing biased versus neutral cue conditions (bias vs neutral), conduct group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using FLAME (cluster-corrected maps and conjunction analyses), and report whole-brain results in text/figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts: bias vs neutral), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (human participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (certainty-equivalent gambling), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and condition-vs-condition contrasts (low-probability vs high-probability; low-value vs high-value). The manuscript reports whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables and links activation differences (notably in ACC) to behavioral parameters (Prelec α). Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports fMRI during a probabilistic reward-learning task (MIL) that entails decision-making under uncertainty (risky DM), satisfying I4. It provides within-task contrasts related to decision outcomes (positive vs. negative prediction errors and parametric prediction-error regressors) and condition comparisons (gain vs nongain in MID), meeting I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, tables/figures), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample is human adults (healthy), and participant groups are acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not PET, not only ROI, not only connectivity, not task>rest only, and the paper is empirical. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Thus the study qualifies for inclusion in a meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. Note: although the MID task is a nonlearning reward task, the MIL learning task provides the required decision-making contrast under uncertainty.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (n=8) that directly tests decision making under uncertainty (probabilistic reasoning tasks: balls-in-a-bottle and personality survey). It reports a condition-vs-condition contrast comparing decision making under uncertainty to decision making under certainty (ambiguous > non-ambiguous), using whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses with corrected voxelwise statistics and tables/figures of coordinates. Participants are healthy; results are reported in figures and a coordinate table. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and references and appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of ambiguous decision-making and should be INCLUDED.

Although this fMRI study clearly scanned human participants during a risky decision-making task and reports group-level whole-brain contrasts and coordinates, it does not report any qualified decision-making contrast of the types required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or perceptual hard > easy). The reported neuroimaging contrasts focus on incidental CS cue processing (Touched_CS > Shocked_CS; Shocked_CS > Touched_CS) prior to gamble presentation rather than contrasts that directly compare decision-making conditions (e.g., risky vs safe choices or task vs control). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) with participants scanned during decisions. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (Risk vs. No-Risk; Risk > No-Risk and No-Risk > Risk) that match admissible risky-DM contrasts (risk > certainty). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FLAME) are reported with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of whole-brain activation coordinates and contrasts of interest for the meta-analysis.

This study meets the review’s inclusion criteria: (I4) it collected fMRI data while human adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (BART); (I5) it reports condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky DM (Pumps > Control (color pumps vs. white control pumps), Cash Outs contrasts); (I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinates; (I7) participant group (healthy adolescents from Mexican backgrounds) is acceptable; (I8) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contrasts include task-versus-control rather than only implicit baseline. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore include for meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (framing task) with choices between a sure option and a gamble, satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision types (e.g., sure vs gamble within gain/loss frames and the framing-effect contrast [(Gsure + Lgamble) − (Lsure + Ggamble)]), satisfying I5. Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise maps (with thresholding and reported peak coordinates), satisfying I6 and I8. Participants were healthy volunteers (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so is complete. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and task is a risky decision-making task. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (odd/even with certain vs uncertain trials), includes within-task contrasts (Uncertain > Certain), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics (random-effects 1-sample and between-group t-tests; FWE-corrected maps and coordinate tables). The paper includes methods, results, and discussion describing whole-brain activation and task contrasts, meeting the meta-analysis requirements for ambiguous decision-making studies. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI study in which human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning decision-making task (uncertain/probabilistic rewards and punishments), meeting the review’s domain (risky/ambiguous decision-making). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted in SPM5: parametric first-level regressors (learning rate, expected value, prediction error) and second-level 1-sample t tests and full-factorial ANOVAs (including comparisons across trial types: correct/wrong × rewarded/punished). These provide task-evoked whole-brain maps (not ROI-only) and within-task contrasts (via the 12-regressor model and ANOVAs), not solely task>implicit baseline contrasts. Participants and methods are fully reported. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual detection decision-making task (animal detection) and reports within-task condition contrasts (Pos > Neut-P and Neg > Neut-N) that directly compare decision-making conditions. Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses are reported (FWE-corrected clusters, coordinates provided) alongside ROI analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the listed exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps while participants performed a probabilistic classification task (weather prediction task) with uncertainty/predictive-value manipulations and an explicit control task. The methods report whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables of coordinates for task-related activations (presentation and feedback phases) and within-group task activations, satisfying the requirement for task-versus-control and condition-versus-condition contrasts related to uncertainty/predictive value. Participants include stroke patients and controls (eligible participant groups). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI of ambiguous/risky/perceptual decision-making and provides whole-brain, group-level results.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (sparse vs dense categorization with an uncertainty opt-out), includes within-task condition contrasts (e.g., uncertainty > correct categorization, correct > uncertainty, and parametric distance-to-bound modulators corresponding to difficulty/hard>easy), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with coordinates and cluster statistics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies fMRI during perceptual decision-making (I4), includes relevant condition-vs-condition contrasts (I5), provides whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (I6), has an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required (Exclusion E5). The tasks are value-based/affective decisions about pleasantness of thermal and olfactory stimuli (reward-based choice) rather than risky/uncertain or perceptual-coherence decisions targeted by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task condition contrast: easy vs difficult), I6 (group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task category — not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=23) who performed a probability-learning and gamble-choice task (risky decision-making). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., active decision phase > control phase; parametric modulation by stimulus probability, outcome and choice entropy) and voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates, thresholds, and corrections (FDR/FWE). Methods, results, and statistics for whole-brain maps are provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts such as active > control and parametric contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not ROI-only, not rest-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, empirical data present). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic classification task that manipulates uncertainty (entropy) — an ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper includes condition-vs-condition and parametric contrasts relevant to decision-making (e.g., negative feedback vs positive feedback, and BOLD correlated with increasing entropy/high vs low uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM99 second-level analyses, with FDR and cluster corrections), and coordinates/tables are provided. Although the entropy effect was significant within a predefined midbrain ROI rather than surviving whole-brain correction, the study did perform whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain results for other contrasts, and therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete in the provided content.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that implemented a risky/ambiguous decision-making task and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper includes condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to the meta-analysis (e.g., Uncertain > Certain; a100 > a0; a80+a100 > a0+a15; parametric linear and quadratic ambiguity regressors; high- vs low-ambiguity; wins vs losses; expected vs unexpected wins). Whole-brain GLM results are presented with cluster correction and Talairach coordinates (tables and figures), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain evidence be available. Participants are human and within eligible age range. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and contrasts are condition-vs-condition rather than task>baseline only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic classification (category learning) task with informational feedback, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined for this meta-analysis. It does not report any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). It does, however, report group-level whole-brain analyses and includes healthy participants. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are met, but I4 and I5 are not met. Exclusion criterion E5 (task not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) applies.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a decision-making task (four-armed bandit) with probabilistic rewards (risk), and thus addresses risky decision-making. It includes task-based, within-task contrasts via model-based parametric regressors (baseline prediction error and novelty-bonus-related prediction error) and contrasts comparing choices of novel versus familiar options, which qualify as decision-making condition contrasts. Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise, whole-brain SPM5 random-effects analyses (with results reported and small-volume correction for a priori regions), and participants were healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles) with within-subject condition contrasts. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., Play > Pass, Gain > Loss, and their interaction), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with cluster- and FWE-correction, and provides coordinates in tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Roulette Betting Task) with explicit manipulation of win probabilities and bet magnitudes. It reports within-task contrasts (active-choice vs no-choice; parametric modulation by probability and bet size) and group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses including whole-brain results (coordinates/tables and exploratory whole-brain analyses are described). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI risky DM task), I5 (condition-vs-condition decision contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic object-reversal decision-making task (pORT) with explicit uncertainty/probabilistic outcomes. The authors report group-level, voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (used to identify ventral striatal voxels at P<0.001 uncorrected and report coordinates x=12,y=16,z=-5) and then parametric contrasts comparing decision-making conditions ("learned" vs "not yet learned") and modulation by uncertainty (inverted U-shaped response with maximal activation at ~50% learning). These constitute within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to ambiguous/risky decision making. Whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate reporting are present (and used to define ROI), and participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (e.g. PET, only ROI/no whole-brain, only baseline contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision task (reporting painful vs. non-painful detection), meeting the review's perceptual-DM definition. The paper reports condition-wise GLM contrasts (pain vs. no pain during anticipation and stimulation) and whole-brain group-level analyses. It additionally provides whole-brain MVPA results including FWE-corrected voxelwise maps and group-level permutation tests. Participants are human and results are presented in standard whole-brain formats. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting/connectivity-only; not ROI-only; contrasts are condition-vs-condition, not baseline-only). Full text appears complete.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study of decision-making under uncertainty using a probabilistic deck task with clearly defined "certain" (100:0) and "uncertain" (80:20) sequences. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., certain vs. uncertain sequences, increases vs. decreases in objective certainty) in addition to task-versus-baseline maps, provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with cluster correction and peak coordinates, and reports results in tables and figures. Participant groups include OCD patients and controls (acceptable per eligibility). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

Exclusion E5 met: the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm probing cognitive flexibility, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision/choice task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the study does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). The reported contrasts focus on phase (acquisition vs reversal) and accuracy (correct win vs incorrect loss) and diagnostic group interactions rather than risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis’ required decision-making contrast types and must be excluded.

This is an empirical human fMRI study that directly investigates risky financial decision-making (BIAS task) during event-related fMRI with group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript reports voxelwise group maps and condition contrasts (e.g., stock gain > loss, market relative gain > loss, stock vs bond choice) with thresholding and Talairach coordinates, and also describes prediction analyses relating anticipatory activation to subsequent risky vs riskless choices. Participants are healthy volunteers. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, fMRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only).

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic (uncertain) decision-making task where choices had known reward probabilities (A/B 80/20; C/D 70/30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (SPM, AlphaSim thresholds) with coordinates and figures, and condition-versus-condition contrasts (positive vs negative feedback; correct (high-probability) vs alternative (low-probability) rules; rule × valence contrasts; shift vs stay). These contrasts constitute within-task comparisons of decision-making conditions (high vs low probability choices) that map onto risky decision-making contrasts (high- vs low-probability outcomes). Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported. Participants are healthy human subjects. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not baseline-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a four-armed bandit gambling task involving decision-making under uncertainty (exploration vs exploitation), which qualifies as risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports a within-task contrast classifying trials as exploratory versus exploitative (a decision-vs-decision comparison). Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM with whole-brain voxelwise statistics and report whole-brain-corrected activations and peak coordinates (figures and coordinates are provided). Participants are healthy humans. Therefore the study satisfies I4 (fMRI + human decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (within-task decision contrasts: exploratory > exploitative), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with corrections), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, discussion, and coordinates (supplementary methods referenced but core content present).

This study uses fMRI in human participants performing a risky lottery task (inclusion I4). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates and random-effects statistics (I6, I8) and uses healthy participants (I7). However, the reported fMRI contrasts focus on outcome-related contrasts (wins vs losses, boosted vs normal wins) and do not report any decision-making contrasts of interest for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, or choice-based contrasts such as trials where participants chose 25 versus 5). The predictors listed and reported results are outcome-phase regressors rather than explicit decision-phase risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts, so criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet I5.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the Decision-Reward Uncertainty Task examining risky and uncertain decision-making and reward outcomes. It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (behavioral risk > reward risk/no-risk; reward > no-reward) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and tables/figures. The full text includes Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. None of the exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), task is risky/uncertainty decision-making (not excluded task types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), connectivity/resting-only criteria do not apply, and within-group/main-effect maps are reported (not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Given these points, I include this study in the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during an affective picture-judgment task and correlated brain activity with behavior on the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT), but the IGT was not performed in the scanner. The fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task, and the reported contrasts (affective judgment vs picture viewing, expected vs unexpected) are not risk/ambiguity/perceptual decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe or ambiguity>non-ambiguous). Therefore it does not meet the key inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and I5 (an appropriate decision-making contrast). The full text is complete and the paper does report group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates and healthy participants, so it meets I6, I7, and I8. Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied (E5).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic (ambiguous) decision-making task (Box Task). It reports within-task contrasts including conclusion > draw and, critically, a high-uncertainty versus low-uncertainty contrast (60:40 > 80:20), satisfying the ambiguous decision-making comparison. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM with reported activation maps/tables and PPI connectivity; whole-brain task-evoked results are presented in tables/figures/text. Full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Exclusion: E5 — the task is moral/social decision-making, which is explicitly excluded (not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group acceptable—healthy children/adolescents). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (no fMRI of a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task), I5 (contrasts reported are moral > nonsocial baseline rather than one of the admitted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms), I6 (uncertain whether a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task map is reported because full text is incomplete). Because E5 is met, the study is excluded.

This is an fMRI study that used a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) with contrasts comparing decision > no-decision and risky > safe. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses were performed (SPM2) with FWE-corrected maps reported and ANCOVA group comparisons. Participant groups (controls, substance-dependent, substance-dependent with gambling) are acceptable. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study (Experiment 4) in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (accept/reject lotteries). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., gain > loss; accept > reject) and parametric contrasts for risk (variance) and EV, and tests interactions—i.e., condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 results with cluster-level FWE correction, and coordinates/tables of activations are provided. Participants are healthy adults. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (condition contrasts such as gain>loss, risk parametric effects), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not a PET-only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline-only). Full text is complete. Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study (3T, SPM8) in healthy human participants performing a multiple-choice task that manipulates internal uncertainty about answers. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts directly comparing decision-making conditions (Uncertainty > Certainty, Certainty > Uncertainty; LC > OE and related contrasts) with coordinates and thresholding detailed in tables and figures.
