Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during decision-making under uncertainty/ambiguity), I5 (condition-vs-condition contrasts appropriate for ambiguous decision-making), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the review are met.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (biased vs. unbiased decisions on vocal emotions) in healthy human participants. It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing two decision-making conditions (unbiased > biased and biased > unbiased) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (SPM flexible factorial, thresholded maps) with ROI-masking applied to whole-brain results. The study therefore provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps (reported within predefined ROIs) and also reports functional connectivity (PPI) but not exclusively. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not only connectivity, not only between-group effects). Full text appears complete with Methods, Results, and Discussion. Hence it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (delayed match-to-category) task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (searchlight) voxelwise statistical maps (t tests on cross-decoding accuracy with TFCE correction) that compare decision-related conditions (category discriminations across modalities), which constitute condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual decision making. The participant sample is healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM task), I5 (condition-vs-condition decision contrasts via decoding maps), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI during a rewarded antisaccade (inhibitory control) task but does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (human participants; age groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (contrasts are reward vs neutral/incentive cue and preparatory/saccade epochs, not one of the admitted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis for not meeting I4 and I5.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that implemented risky, ambiguous, and a novel "conflict" decision-making task during scanning (Materials & Methods). The paper reports condition contrasts including ambiguity > risk and parametric effects of ambiguity/conflict level, and correlations of activation with behavioral attitudes (Results). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLMs and whole-brain searches are described and reported (Statistical maps, Monte Carlo cluster correction), with results presented in figures/tables. The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not only baseline contrasts; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study measured brain activity while human participants performed perceptual decision-making tasks (visual contrast detection, auditory tone detection, motion discrimination) and reports condition contrasts and whole-brain group-level maps. It includes within-task contrasts (e.g., signal+noise vs. noise) and choice-related contrasts, not only task>baseline; it provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and searchlight decoding results. Participants are human (healthy/typical adult samples). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study of effort-based decision-making (sequential presentation of effort and reward) and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps. However, the review is limited to risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making tasks. The study’s task is effort-based, which is explicitly excluded (E5). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (human participants; healthy sample), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual), I5 (no eligible contrasts like risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded under E5.

The study uses a delay discounting / intertemporal choice task (delay discounting, Intertemporal Choice Task), which falls outside the review scope. Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM — delay discounting/intertemporal choice excluded) is met. The paper does report whole-brain, group-level fMRI activation maps and voxelwise contrasts (hard>easy, hard>no, easy>no), so inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures) are satisfied. However I4 (task must be risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) is not satisfied, and I5 (contrasts appropriate to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) is not applicable for the review domains. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task probing cognitive flexibility and feedback processing, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis. Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and figures/tables (I6, I8) and includes healthy human participants (I7), it does not employ an accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm or contrasts (e.g., 'risky > safe', 'ambiguity > non-ambiguous', 'hard > easy'). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study had human participants performing a tactile perceptual decision-making task (vibrotactile pattern discrimination) with manipulated decision difficulty (intact/partially/fully scrambled) and immediate vs delayed response conditions. The analysis included group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM and parametric modulation by difficulty (i.e., hard > easy type contrasts), and reported task-related whole-brain activation (ROIs derived from corrected voxelwise results). Participants were healthy volunteers. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI with perceptual DM), I5 (decision-related contrasts/parametric difficulty modulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not baseline-only contrasts; not ROI-only reporting; not connectivity-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans that implements a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination with graded difficulty including noise trials) and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., FaceDecision > HouseDecision, parametric contrasts across signal strength/hard>easy manipulations and decision vs instructed responses). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (with cluster correction) including whole-brain reward-network activations; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are present in the text/figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded (E5): The task is probabilistic association learning (Weather Prediction Task), a learning paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable: healthy controls and schizophrenia patients), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) is not satisfied because the WPT is an associative learning task rather than a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm; I5 (required decision-making contrasts) is not satisfied in the sense required by the review (risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy, or analogous uncertainty/risk contrasts). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study in human participants that used a perceptual two-alternative forced-choice task (judge stimulus as more speech vs more non-speech). The experiment manipulated stimulus ambiguity/difficulty (pure vs blended stimuli) and modeledcondition-wise BOLD responses (Speech: speech vs non-speech; Correctness; Time), and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and reported peak coordinates. Thus it provides within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making and reports whole-brain group activation maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

The study reports fMRI data (Experiment 2) collected while human participants performed a probabilistic reinforcement-learning decision-making task (choices between options with differing reward probabilities), which constitutes decision-making under uncertainty/risk. The paper includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-task contrasts and regressors relevant to decision processes (chosen vs unchosen outcomes; relative outcome; relative value prediction error). Participants were healthy adults and whole-brain results are reported in the main text/figures. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky/uncertain decision-making and whole-brain contrasts.

This study does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. While it uses fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (I6) and includes a healthy participant sample (I7), and presents whole-brain results/coordinates in text (I8), the critical decision-making manipulation (valence ratings of surprised faces) was performed outside the scanner. In the MRI session participants freely viewed faces (passive viewing) and performed an emotion regulation task (reappraise vs maintain), which is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast comparing decision conditions or task vs control) are not satisfied. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study’s in-scanner tasks are not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. Consequently the study must be excluded.

Exclusion IDs met: E6 and E7. Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — BART) and I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy human participants across ages). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no clear reported contrast comparing decision-making conditions or task>control contrast in the paper text), I6 (no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map presented in the manuscript). Although the manuscript focused on fMRI data and reports ROI-based connectivity (GIMME) and extracted timepoints for “risky decisions,” the primary analyses are ROI-based effective/connectivity models rather than whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts. The paper does not provide clear, unmasked whole-brain task activation maps or within-task contrasts in the full text; therefore it meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E7 (only effective/connectivity analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete, but lacks the required whole-brain activation contrast for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study reports whole-brain fMRI collected while human participants performed a probabilistic (uncertainty-manipulated) reinforcement learning task with monetary outcomes (50%, 69%, 100% predictability). The authors report voxelwise, group-level contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (predictability-related contrasts: 100%<69%<50%, within-group and between-group comparisons) with whole-brain statistical maps and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision task with uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrasts across uncertainty levels), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets inclusion for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI. It used fMRI while participants performed a risky gambling (accept/reject mixed gambles) task (I4). It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., parametric contrasts of losses vs gains, emotional vs non-emotional decision trials) rather than only baseline contrasts, satisfying the requirement for a decision-related contrast (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with clusters surviving correction and anatomical coordinates (I6, I8). Participant sample is healthy adults (and would be acceptable per participant inclusion; I7). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This is an fMRI study acquired while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (face vs car categorization with color discrimination control) with manipulated stimulus coherence. The design includes condition-wise manipulations (high vs low coherence and task type) that yield condition contrasts interpretable as perceptual difficulty (e.g., low coherence > high coherence) and task-vs-control comparisons. Analysis is whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise mixed-effects GLM with cluster correction; results are reported as voxelwise activation maps and region summaries. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI evidence.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants that used a perceptual decision-making task (difference judgment) during scanning and reports task-versus-control contrasts (judgment > passive viewing/blank) and within-task contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects) are reported, with coordinates and figures (Talairach coordinates, Table 1, and group maps). The task falls squarely within perceptual decision-making. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only rest contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This fMRI study uses a risky decision-making lottery task (choices between a lottery and a sure amount) performed by human participants, meeting the review scope. It provides within-task contrasts via trial-by-trial subjective-value (SV) parametric regressors and a high-vs-low SV comparison through cross-modality MVPA (train-on-one-modality, test-on-the-other), which constitutes an eligible within-task comparison (analogous to high-risk > low-risk). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (FDR-corrected maps, MNI coordinates) and a whole-brain searchlight MVPA was performed. Participants are healthy adult humans. Results (coordinates, figures, conjunctions) are clearly described in the text. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state/connectivity-only; contrasts are not only implicit baseline given the within-task high-vs-low analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in which human participants (n=10 healthy adults) performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task) inside an fMRI scanner. The analysis includes within-subject contrasts of IGT > active control task, group-level voxelwise statistical maps (t-maps with Bonferroni correction) and whole-brain surface/volume results. Participants are an eligible group (healthy adults). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (3D heading discrimination) with explicit contrasts comparing decision difficulty (EASY vs HARD) across two stimulus manipulations (COH and FOE). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects t-maps, conjunction analysis) are reported with thresholding and coordinates; results are presented in text, figures, and ROI follow-up. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates none of the listed exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a gambling task that manipulates risk levels (high- vs low-risk choices) and analyzes outcomes. The methods describe event-related fMRI, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses and report group- and risk-level contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk for positive outcomes; group×risk interactions). Results include whole-brain coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. Participant sample (healthy first-degree relatives and controls) is acceptable per the review scope. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (task-based fMRI of risky decision-making; relevant decision contrasts; whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps; acceptable participant group; clear reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria apply.

Although this study used fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps (satisfying I6), recruited healthy human participants (I7), and reports whole-brain results described in the text (I8), it does not meet the review’s decision-making task requirements. The experimental paradigm is a probabilistic learning/inference task probing estimation and confidence about transition probabilities, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. It does not present contrasts of the accepted forms (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, hard > easy) and instead reports parametric/model-based regressors (confidence, surprise, update). Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in human participants performing a probabilistic object reversal task (reward-based decision making under uncertainty). It includes a within-task decision-making contrast (Decision making: “learned” vs. “search”) and reward-processing contrasts, all analyzed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with peak coordinates reported. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. These facts satisfy inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports empirical fMRI data from 143 healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (gain/loss framing). It includes within-task condition contrasts (frame-consistent vs frame-inconsistent choices) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (unthresholded framing contrast deposited on NeuroVault). Methods, results, and discussion are present and detailed. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) fMRI during risky decision-making, (I5) at least one condition-vs-condition contrast, (I6) whole-brain group-level maps, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) clearly described whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., contrasts are not against implicit baseline, not PET, not ROI-only, etc.). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision making (object recognition) with human participants. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures mixed-effects ANOVA), contrasts across decision conditions (recognition time TR3–7, comparisons of correct vs. TR8, and static vs. shuffle trials), and presents whole-brain maps and ROI coordinates. These meet inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only baseline contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports whole-brain fMRI results from a two-step sequential reinforcement-learning task and provides group-level voxelwise contrasts (model-based vs model-free prediction-error regressors) and full methods/results/discussion. However, the meta-analysis specifically targets risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. The two-step task is a model-based/model-free reinforcement-learning paradigm and does not constitute a risky, ambiguity, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review; therefore it fails the task-domain inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (does not report contrasts in the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual forms). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed an ambiguous decision-making task (valence judgments of sounds with manipulated consonance/dissonance). Relevant contrasts compare ambiguous vs less-ambiguous conditions (intermediate dissonance > consonance; strong > intermediate), meeting the required condition-vs-condition contrasts for ambiguous-DM. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level one-sample t-tests) are reported, with cluster and voxel-level thresholding and coordinates presented. Participants are healthy human adults. Results and coordinates are reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-task contrasts rather than only task>rest). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

Full text lacks necessary fMRI methodological/results detail to confirm inclusion. The paper presents EEG and behavioral data from a sequential stock-buying (uncertainty) task and references an fMRI dataset, but the provided full text does not include fMRI acquisition, whole-brain group-level contrasts, or voxelwise task activation maps required for meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met / could not be verified: I4 (fMRI scan while performing risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) — fMRI is only referenced, not reported here; I5 (at least one condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control fMRI contrast) — no fMRI contrasts presented; I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task map) — not provided. No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis (E3–E9) are explicitly met based on the supplied text. Because core fMRI details and contrasts are missing from the provided full text, I cannot confirm this study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Marking fulltext_incomplete=true to indicate the supplied full text is insufficient to determine eligibility.

Exclusion(s) met: E3. The fMRI analyses reported use task-versus-baseline contrasts (200 ms vs baseline; 400 ms vs baseline) and subsequent regressions/conjunctions derived from those maps; the study does not present a within-task contrast or a task>active-control contrast of the type required. Inclusion(s) met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results described in the text/tables/figures). Inclusion(s) not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as hard>easy, low coherence>high, or task>active control; only task>baseline and parametric correlations based on those baseline contrasts). Full text appears complete and not truncated.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the probabilistic “weather prediction” task (decisions under probabilistic uncertainty), with task-versus-control contrasts (weather prediction > perceptual-motor control) and group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses reported (tables and figures). The task constitutes decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous DM), the admitted contrast form (task > control) matches I5, whole-brain voxelwise maps and second-level analyses are present (I6), participant groups (patients and healthy adults) are acceptable (I7), and results are reported in text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting baseline contrasts only; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a human fMRI study that manipulated risky and ambiguous gambles and tested neural correlates of belief updating, value updating, and expectancy violation. The task clearly involves risk and ambiguity (Ellsberg-style urn gambles), and fMRI data were analyzed with whole-brain, group-level GLMs producing voxelwise statistical maps (parametric modulators for belief updating, value updating, and expectancy violation) with cluster-level FWE correction. The study reports within-task contrasts/parametric effects (e.g., value updating, belief updating adjusted for expectancy violation), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Participants were healthy adults. Whole-brain results are reported in the main text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore this empirical fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study with human participants (N=19 analyzed) performing a multi-option decision-making task involving probabilistic rewards (uncertain/risky outcomes). The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLM results and contrasts (parametric modulators of decision variables such as best unchosen probability, chosen probability, prediction errors) with coordinates, figures, and mixed-effects group analyses. These constitute within-task decision-making contrasts (decision-related parametric effects) relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. Whole-text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Participants are healthy volunteers. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not rest-only contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a two-alternative perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with manipulated stimulus coherence. It reports within-task contrasts comparing difficulty levels (hard > easy) and DR>RT, uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction and reports MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Behavioral modeling and DDM-informed analyses are included. The study therefore satisfies perceptual-decision criteria, provides condition-vs-condition contrasts (hard>easy), and supplies whole-brain group-level results (maps/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a predictive-inference decision task in the scanner (subjects placed a bucket to infer a hidden helicopter location under uncertainty). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (searchlight RSA and group t-maps, cluster correction) linking neural patterns to model-derived decision variables (relative uncertainty, change-point probability, learning rate) — i.e., within-task comparisons and parametric effects akin to high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty. Results are reported as whole-brain maps/figures and tables. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies fMRI during a decision task under uncertainty (I4), contains within-task contrasts/parametric comparisons of decision variables (I5), provides whole-brain group-level maps (I6), participants are an acceptable group (I7), and whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision task (face/house discrimination) with concurrent metacognitive (confidence) reports. It includes a within-task condition contrast (Report > Follow) that contrasts an active metacognitive report vs a yoked control, which constitutes a task-versus-control comparison relevant to perceptual decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with corrected clusters and tabulated coordinates. Participants and methods are fully described and the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants making risk-related decisions in driving (urgent braking vs. risk evaluation). It reports within-task condition contrasts (urgent > evaluative and vice versa) that are directly relevant to risky decision-making, uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM12, AlphaSim correction) and reports cluster coordinates/tables and figures. The tasks constitute risky decision-making (braking to avoid hazards), satisfying the meta-analysis scope. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>baseline only), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), and the paper is empirical. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that used an event-related risky decision-making (gambling) task during scanning and reports multiple within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Risk_DisAdv > Risk_Adv; Risk_DisAdv_Win > Risk_Adv_Win; Risk_DisAdv_Lose > Risk_Adv_Lose). The paper describes voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM5, second-level random-effects, cluster-level FWE correction) and reports regional activations and correlations. These contrasts are condition-versus-condition risky decision contrasts (comparable to allowed forms such as high-risk > low-risk or riskier > surer). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning decision task (I4 met) in human participants (I7 met), but the neuroimaging analysis was constrained to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and no unmasked whole-brain task-activation map is reported, i.e. only ROI-based results are presented (meets exclusion E6). Consequently the required whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map is not available (I6 not met), and the reported contrasts (win, lose-stay, lose-shift) do not match the explicit risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms required (I5 not met). Qualifying whole-brain results are not provided in tables/figures as whole-brain maps (I8 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) administered in the scanner. It reports within-task condition contrasts including Go > Stop (risky > safe) and Good > Bad outcomes (i.e., risk vs safety and positive vs negative outcomes), satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected results, tables, and NeuroVault uploads), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are a human sample (adolescents) and thus acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met: it is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts rather than only task>rest, and is an original empirical fMRI activation study. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore this study should be INCLUDED.

This article reports an fMRI study in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (the BART) during scanning, includes within-task contrasts (parametric risk modulation; experimental green (risk) > control orange balloon; decision contrasts cash > inflate), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and coordinate tables. The sample and methods are fully described in the full text. Thus all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making paradigm, with participants scanned during task performance. The analyses include within-task, parametrically-modulated contrasts (inflation choice * P(explode); successful inflation * P(explode)) that constitute condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts, and second-level, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses reporting peak coordinates and cluster statistics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an economic decision-making task with uncertainty about option values (learning from noisy samples), satisfying the meta-analysis domain of ambiguous/risky decision-making. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., commit > defer; rule x decision x value interactions) and parametric value regressors, i.e., condition-versus-condition contrasts. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLMs with clusterwise correction and reported peak coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; contrasts are not only vs implicit baseline; whole-brain task activation maps are reported).

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between gambles) with concurrent BOLD acquisition and event-related analysis. The paper reports within-task condition comparisons and parametric contrasts (e.g., choices of one gamble vs another, parametric modulation by context-dependent desirability and weighting-function differences, high- vs low-gain and high- vs low-probability control trial contrasts), satisfying the requirement for decision-condition contrasts. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM results with reported MNI coordinates and cluster statistics (tables/figures/SI). Participants are healthy adults. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, only baseline contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a value-based stock-buying task with probabilistic outcomes and manipulated cue validity (compensatory vs noncompensatory environments), i.e., decisions under uncertainty. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with parametric contrasts (EV, RPE, decision conflict, strategy selection) and trial-type comparisons (ALL vs AUD trials, DCM analyses separating trial types). Whole-brain results are reported with peak coordinates/tables. Although contrasts are parametric rather than a simple "risky>safe" label, the within-task condition contrasts and model-based comparisons meet the meta-analysis requirement for condition-vs-condition/task-vs-control contrasts. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are applicable.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a monetary decision-making task varying reward probability and magnitude (uncertainty/risk), satisfying I4. The authors report within-task contrasts modeling reward uncertainty (e.g., 50% vs 100%), reward magnitude and value, and prediction error contrasts, satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM second-level analyses with FDR/FWE correction and coordinate tables, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults, satisfying I7. The manuscript includes full introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a matching-pennies competitive decision-making task involving uncertainty about an opponent’s choices. The task probes decision-making under uncertainty/ambiguity (subjects did not have explicit probabilities and the study examined opponent-related uncertainty and block-wise winning rates). The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric analyses (entropy-related effects; high/medium/low entropy blocks) and a human vs. computer condition; these constitute condition-versus-condition comparisons (e.g., high-entropy > low-entropy and human > computer). Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain maps with ROI and whole-brain thresholds) and significant activations (e.g., bilateral anterior insula) are described. Participants were healthy humans. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for ambiguous decision-making fMRI studies and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house detection). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects) with statistical contrasts that compare task conditions (e.g., Fin vs Nin; In vs Out; Fin+Hin > Nin), not merely task>baseline. Whole-brain activation maps, figures, and coordinate tables are reported. The task is clearly a perceptual DM paradigm and includes condition-versus-condition contrasts appropriate for inclusion. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that measured BOLD responses while subjects performed a perceptual decision-making task under ambiguity (face emotion morph judgments). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing ambiguity levels (e.g., increasing ambiguity and decreasing ambiguity effects) and identify whole-brain group-level activations using SPM random-effects analyses. Thus the paper provides eligible ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (ambiguous > non-ambiguous and related contrasts) and whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (E5). Although the paper used fMRI with group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (I6), included qualifying participant groups (ASD and controls) (I7), and reported whole-brain results in tables/figures (I8), it did not implement a decision-making task nor report contrasts that compare decision-making conditions (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). The fMRI contrasts are stimulation (texture) > rest (baseline) and within- and between-group texture effects, not decision-making condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrasts; thus I4 and I5 are not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task).

Only the article abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract it is clear this is an fMRI study in human participants performing a categorisation task of prosodic expressions (meets I4) and the authors report contrasts involving ambiguous versus typical tokens (consistent with an 'ambiguous > non-ambiguous' contrast, suggesting I5). Participant inclusion criteria are broad (I7) and results are described in the text (I8). However, the available content does not include the full methods or results needed to confirm that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps were reported (I6) or to verify the exact contrasts and their masking/statistical thresholds. Because core article content (methods/results) is missing, I cannot confidently verify all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis were clearly triggered by the abstract alone. Therefore I exclude on the basis of incomplete full text preventing confirmation of required whole-brain, condition-vs-condition contrasts.

Exclusion (E5, E6) — This is an fMRI study of category learning (rule-plus-exception) and does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis (E5). The imaging analysis is focused on high-resolution, anatomically defined MTL and striatal ROIs rather than reporting unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps, so it reports ROI-restricted results with no qualifying whole-brain task maps (E6). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group qualifies: healthy human participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (contrasts are exception vs rule-following in a category-learning task, not the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts), I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete and was evaluated in full.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in which participants performed explicit monetary decision-making tasks under risk (probability discounting and 50-50 gambles). Group-level, voxelwise analyses (one-way ANOVAs and exploratory whole-brain analyses) are reported, with parametric regressors for subjective value, magnitude, and probability; results are presented in the main text and supplementary tables. The study thus (a) acquired fMRI during risky decision-making (I4), (b) reported within-task parametric contrasts relating neural activity to subjective value/potential gain/potential loss (acceptable forms of decision-related contrasts, satisfying I5), (c) conducted and reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (I6) and provided results in text/tables (I8), and (d) included clinical and healthy participant groups (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to task>rest only, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task effects are reported. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (visual shape discrimination with easy vs hard trials). The study reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected) and condition-versus-condition contrasts including decision-related contrasts (decision to continue vs quit after negative feedback) and feedback contrasts (positive vs negative). These constitute within-task decision-making contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making. Whole-brain results are described in the text and supported by ROI and gPPI connectivity analyses. Participant sample, methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study used event-related fMRI with group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy humans and reports coordinate-based results (I4, I6, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm examining reversal learning and responses to negative feedback, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). The reported contrasts (final reversal errors vs correct responses, probabilistic errors vs correct, etc.) do not match the required decision-making contrasts (I5 not met). Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded (E5). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement that participants performed a decision-making task (Exclusion E5). Although the task manipulates uncertainty (reward vs. no-incentive anticipation) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps, it is a passive slot-machine paradigm with no behavioral choices or decision-making component; thus inclusion criteria I4 (decision-making task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast/comparison) are not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (contrast comparing decision-making conditions or task vs active control for decision-making). Full text is complete and sufficient for this determination.

This is a human fMRI study in which cocaine-dependent participants performed a Paper-Scissors-Rock reinforcement-learning task during fMRI. The task manipulates uncertainty/probability (preferred 90%, even 50%, worst 10%) and the authors model decision-phase contrasts of early (high uncertainty/learning) versus late (low uncertainty/execution) trials, which maps onto an ambiguous-DM contrast (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (AFNI GLM, AlphaSim correction) with cluster tables and Talairach coordinates. Participants are a substance-using clinical sample (acceptable). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Instead, one of the tasks is a delay discounting task (intertemporal choice), which is explicitly excluded (E5). Although the study includes whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (satisfying I6), reports results in the main text (I8), and uses an eligible participant group (healthy adults; I7), it does not meet the core inclusion requirements for task type (I4) nor the decision-making-contrast requirement for the allowed DM domains (I5). Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulated ambiguity in a decision-making task (ambiguous, unambiguous, incongruent sequences) and implicitly biased choices. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts including ambiguous > unambiguous and ambiguous > incongruent, and order (2-1 > 1-2) contrasts that directly compare decision-making conditions (matches ambiguous-DM contrast types). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with FWE cluster correction and reported coordinates/parameter estimates. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E7 — the paper reports ICA-derived networks and component betas (a connectivity/ICA approach) and does not report a standard group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast required for coordinate-based activation meta-analysis. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — fMRI was collected while participants performed a perceptual decision-making (two-choice RT) task; I7 — participants are human healthy adults (young and older) (participant groups acceptable); I8 — MNI coordinates for ICA component maxima are reported. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — no reported contrast of decision-making conditions (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high, or task>active control); the paper averaged across verbal and numerical blocks rather than presenting within-task condition contrasts; I6 — no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrast map (e.g., task>control or condition>condition) is provided. Because I5 and I6 are required and not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescent females that implements a decision-making task with explicit risk manipulation (high-risk vs low-risk sexual decisions) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. The manuscript includes within-task contrasts (high-risk > low-risk and Boys (high-low) vs. control conditions), reports whole-brain cluster results in tables and figures (voxel p<.001, cluster extent threshold), and provides full methods and results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is an fMRI study in humans that used two-choice perceptual decision-making tasks (numerical and verbal) during scanning, with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses linking task activation to behavioral parameters. The paper reports between-task comparisons (numerical vs. verbal) and task-related contrasts, and performs whole-brain random-effects analyses and multiple-regression voxelwise maps (thresholded and reported with coordinates). The task is a perceptual decision-making paradigm and whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, only baseline contrasts without task-vs-task comparisons) are met. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing life–death framing tasks (risky decision-making). It reports within-task contrasts comparing positive (gain) vs negative (loss) framing and large vs small group contexts (condition vs condition), with group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables of MNI coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present, and whole-brain results are reported (Table 2, figures). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is a human fMRI study in which participants performed a risky decision-making task (rating risk of physical activities) manipulating likelihood and severity. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; high-harm > low-harm; Risk x Format interactions) rather than only task>baseline. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans using a risky decision-making task (accept/reject mixed gambles with 50% win/loss probability). The paper reports within-task, condition-vs-condition contrasts and parametric contrasts (e.g., anticipation/activation for losses vs gains, bidirectional responses, acceptance > rejection) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM8; thresholds reported). Methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making paradigm) during scanning, with within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (pump decisions following negative feedback/explosion vs following positive feedback/cash-out). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (tables of coordinates, cluster-corrected maps, NeuroVault link). Participant sample and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of the Trust Game (risky social decision-making) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (GAME>CONTROL, INVESTOR>CONTROL, TRUSTEE>CONTROL) and coordinates/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. However, all reported neuroimaging results are between-group comparisons (high-Mach > low-Mach) of the task contrast, and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain within-group/task main effect map (e.g., task>control within a single group or the overall sample). Therefore it falls under exclusion E8 (reports only between-group contrasts with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports an fMRI study in humans that manipulated outcome uncertainty/error rate during a two-choice decision-making task (20%, 50%, 80% error rates) and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., low-error vs high-error, uncertainty-related effects) with voxelwise whole-brain analyses and cluster correction. The paper therefore matches the review scope (risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making via uncertainty manipulation), includes appropriate condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., high uncertainty [50%] vs more predictable conditions and 20% vs 80%), and provides group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported and described in the text. Full article includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-only contrasts) apply.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a probability-discounting task that manipulated risk (choices between certain smaller rewards and larger probabilistic rewards). The paper reports within-task contrasts (probabilistic/risky > fixed/certain) and between-group comparisons ((IGD possible − IGD fixed) − (HC possible − HC fixed)). Analyses were conducted at the whole-brain group level using SPM5 with cluster-level FWE correction and reported cluster coordinates (Table 1 and figures). Participant groups (IGD and healthy controls) are acceptable per review criteria. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the content is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an event-related gambling (guessing) task that manipulates uncertainty/risk during the anticipation phase. It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Anticipation $4 vs No-change; Ant $4–No-ch $4 and Ant 50c–No-ch 50c) rather than task>rest, satisfying risky/ambiguous decision contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM8, voxelwise thresholding with cluster reporting) with results presented as clusters/coordinates and parameter estimates. Participants are healthy humans in a crossover design. Therefore I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion (E5): The study uses a probabilistic reinforcement-learning/episodic memory task and investigates prediction-error-related activity and memory, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results are reported/mentioned), I7 (human participant groups qualifying by age/health), I8 (whole-brain results referenced in main/supplemental materials). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM tasks required), I5 (no accepted decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Because I4 and I5 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded under E5.

This study is excluded because its task does not meet the meta-analysis domains. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the task is a two-step sequential reinforcement-learning task probing model-based vs model-free control, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review). Additionally, the study includes PET imaging (F-DOPA PET) alongside fMRI, which falls under the meta-analysis exclusion of PET studies (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results are reported), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (whole-brain results are described in the text and figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not performed while participants engaged in a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined), and I5 (no contrast of the types specified for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude under E5 (and E4).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that scanned participants while they performed a risky decision-making task (gambling) and reported within-task condition contrasts. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (High-Variance > Low-Variance; Skewed > Symmetric; Positive-Skew > Negative-Skew) that correspond to risky-DM contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (AFNI preprocessing, whole-brain corrected thresholds, cluster criterion), with reported localization and timecourse VOI verification; whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures. The sample (N=19) and methods are detailed and the full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets the review criteria. It acquired fMRI while human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), satisfying I4. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (parametric PE regressors and group contrasts), satisfying I6 and I8. The paper includes between-condition contrasts comparing decision-making contexts (reward-seeking vs punishment-avoidance) and stimulus-domain conditions (faces vs abstract), which are valid within-task decision-making condition contrasts for the meta-analysis (satisfying I5). Participants are a healthy human sample (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only task>baseline implicit contrasts (they include between-condition contrasts and parametric contrasts), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study (3T scanner, SPM5) in healthy human participants performing a gambling/decision-making task manipulating prior outcomes (WIN, LOSS, CONTROL). It reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts during the decision-making phase (WIN vs CONTROL, LOSS vs CONTROL, WIN vs LOSS) at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates, and includes behavioral–ROI correlations. The task models risky decision-making with independent random outcomes and the risk level held constant; contrasts are not against implicit baseline. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging, analysis), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a monetary probability task (cues with 0,25,50,75,100% chance) that manipulates decision-making under risk/uncertainty. The authors report within-subject condition contrasts (linear contrasts across five expectation conditions and outcome regressors contrasting positive vs negative prediction error), computed at the group (second) level with voxelwise SPM analyses and whole-brain FWE correction. Participants are healthy humans and whole-brain results are described in text/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8).

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART) during whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses to examine covariance between risk level (parametric modulation of explosion probability) and brain activation, comparing post-win vs post-loss decision events. It reports voxelwise random-effects analyses (2x2 ANOVA) with whole-brain cluster correction and within-group maps, satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-condition contrasts (risk-level parametric effects and after-loss vs after-win comparisons). Participants are human adolescents (IGD and HCs). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

Exclusion: E5 met — the task is an erotic Go/NoGo response-inhibition task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (participant group is acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm), I5 (contrasts are NoGo vs Go and Male vs Female motivational contrasts, which do not match the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the review’s decision-making domains.)

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (subjects bluffing in a domino game) and includes condition contrasts (nonmatch [risky] vs match [safe]) with healthy human participants. However, MRI acquisition used a small number of slices centered on the amygdala (partial brain coverage) and analyses focus on anatomically defined ROI and small-volume/group GLMs restricted to the amygdala; no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported. Therefore the study does not provide whole-brain results required for inclusion and meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only / no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI while participants performed a spatial memory retrieval task in morphing virtual environments, not a canonical risky, ambiguous economic, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Although participants made memory-based placement choices in ambiguous contexts, the paper’s analyses focus on MVPA pattern similarity (sigmoidal vs linear models) and hippocampal remapping rather than standard decision-making contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous) or univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps appropriate for the meta-analysis. Exclusion ID E5 applies (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during task), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (reporting of coordinates/whole-brain results in text/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no standard contrast comparing decision conditions or task > control as required), I6 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps presented for the decision contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART) during task-based fMRI, providing within-task contrasts based on risk level (parametric 'risk level' pump regressor) and reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds). The manuscript includes methods, results, and discussion (full text present) and reports whole-brain results in the text (with supplemental materials referenced). Although the paper also presents resting-state connectivity analyses, it also provides task-evoked whole-brain contrasts appropriate for risky decision-making (high-risk > low-risk type parametric contrast). Participant sample (nicotine-dependent smokers) is an allowed population. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest only, or only connectivity without task maps) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making task fMRI and whole-brain reporting.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (lotteries) inside the scanner. The authors performed group-level GLM analyses including parametric modulators (ΔU, ΔMin, ΔEV), compared task conditions (Self vs Other; Comp filler), and report whole-brain activation results (with summary tables) and ROI analyses. Thus it provides within-task contrasts/parametric task effects relevant to risk decision-making, and includes group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results. Participants are healthy university students. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI or connectivity results, contrasts only vs baseline) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This fMRI study is excluded because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or canonical perceptual decision-making contrasts (Exclusion E5). The task is a sequence/pattern-learning paradigm where subjects identify gradually revealed images to detect patterns; the reported contrasts (pattern vs no-pattern, RT drops, entropy regressors) index structure learning and uncertainty rather than established perceptual difficulty contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence) or risk/ambiguity manipulations. The paper does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported using SnPM and cluster-level FWE correction), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). However it does not meet I4 (study must be an fMRI of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined) nor I5 (contains an admissible decision-making contrast such as perceptual hard>easy or equivalent). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED (E5).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It acquired fMRI while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (the cups task) (I4), and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., risky > safe; win > loss; parametric risk/reward contrasts) (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise maps with reported MNI coordinates and GRF-corrected thresholds (I6) and results are reported for eligible participant groups (IGD and healthy controls) (I7). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an event-related fMRI study in which human participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task) during scanning. The authors modeled and tested trial-type regressors (positive, negative, zero outcomes) and carried contrast files into group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (cluster-level inference with FWE correction). Thus the paper provides within-task contrasts comparing decision-related conditions (responses to wins vs losses) and reports whole-brain group results in the text and figures. Participants include both patient and healthy groups (allowed). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Please note: the primary contrasts are outcome-evaluation (win/loss) rather than explicit “risky > safe” decision-phase contrasts, but outcome contrasts are valid within-task decision-making contrasts for the IGT and were reported at the whole-brain group level.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used the Cups task (risky decision-making) during fMRI (meets I4). The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., ADV Risk > DIS Risk and other EV contrasts) that directly compare decision-making conditions (meets I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise FLAME results with cluster correction and reported activation tables/figures (meets I6 and I8). Participant groups (healthy adolescents and adults) are acceptable (meets I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion (E5): The study’s task is a working-memory / DMN paradigm contrasting memory-guided (1-back) versus immediate perceptual (0-back) spatial judgments; it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or the kinds of perceptual decision-making contrasts targeted by the meta-analysis (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, risk>safe). Inclusion satisfied: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures). Inclusion not satisfied: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or clearly defined perceptual decision-making manipulation as required), I5 (the reported contrasts do not match the accepted decision-making contrast types for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that manipulated reward probability (risk) within an economic decision task and analyzed task-evoked BOLD responses. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM) with task-versus-control contrasts (DM > C2) and regression analyses using entropy; results are reported as clusters/coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision task), I5 (decision task vs active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using an instrumental probabilistic (80% vs 20%) reinforcement-learning task (choices between stimuli with probabilistic reward/punishment), satisfying the review’s focus on decision-making under uncertainty (risky DM). The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (rewarded > non-rewarded; punished > non-punished; reward > punishment) and parametric prediction-error regressors, with standard random-effects whole-brain analyses and ROI/whole-brain results reported. Participants include clinical and healthy groups. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (within-task condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a perceptual/predictive-inference decision task manipulating uncertainty (high vs low noise) and surprise. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts (CPP, RU, reward) and pairwise contrasts (e.g., CPP>RU), perform whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses with appropriate correction, and present conjunction and contrast maps. These analyses constitute condition-vs-condition and parametric decision-making contrasts rather than task>baseline. The task maps onto perceptual decision-making (noise/coherence-like manipulation) and meets the meta-analysis objective. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, includes whole-brain task activations, not only connectivity, not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans that directly examines neural responses to risk and ambiguity in a task contrast relevant to decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) SPM analyses with second-level RFX contrasts including ambiguity > risk and ambiguity > ignorance, and provides tables/figures of coordinates and clusters. The experimental manipulation and reported contrasts match the meta-analysis inclusion forms (e.g., "ambiguity > ignorance"). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and includes within-group whole-brain task contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and is complete for screening.

This fMRI study uses a two-stage sequential reinforcement-learning task probing model-based vs model-free evaluation, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. It does not report contrasts of the form required for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, or hard > easy). The paper does include group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses present), I7 (human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not categorized as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) and I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (direction-of-motion discrimination) with two coherence levels. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and condition-versus-condition contrasts (high-coherence vs low-coherence; conjunction analyses across response modalities), and provides coordinates and statistical maps. The methods and results include mixed-effects whole-brain GLM analyses and thresholded Z-statistic images, satisfying the review’s requirements for task-evoked whole-brain results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a stochastic monetary decision-making task with probabilistic outcomes (risk/uncertainty). The experiment includes Test (decision-making with rewards) and active Control blocks, and the authors report Test > Control contrasts and regression analyses masked by Test-Control, satisfying a task-versus-control contrast. Analyses were conducted using SPM with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results reported (coordinates, corrected p-values, figures, and tables). Participants were healthy adults.
