Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (decision task vs active control), I6 (group whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses an fMRI trust/reciprocity (social) task and contrasts human versus computer interaction; this is social decision-making rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy; primary contrast is human>computer). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Exclusion IDs met: E5 (the fMRI task is an emotional go/no-go impulse-control paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E7 (the primary reported analyses are pseudo-resting-state/functional connectivity and multivariate prediction of “brain age,” not whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation maps or task contrasts). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (the participant group is within eligible populations). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no fMRI performed during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no reported contrasts of the form risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; the paper does not report decision-making task-versus-control-task contrasts relevant to the review), and I6 (the target analyses are connectivity/prediction rather than group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps). Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given these points, the study does not meet the required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is primarily moral/social decision-making (allocating financial harm/help to a charity vs self), which the meta-analysis explicitly excludes. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI results reported with corrected cluster thresholds and coordinates), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/coordinates and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is framed as social/moral decisions rather than a canonical risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm targeted by the review), and I5 (no contrast matching the admissible risk/ambiguity/perceptual forms such as "risky > safe" or "high uncertainty > low uncertainty"; condition contrasts focus on self vs charity and gain vs loss rather than risk vs safe or ambiguity contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study used an n-back working memory fMRI task (0-back vs 2-back) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Thus it does not meet I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) nor I5 (no decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity contrasts, or hard>easy). The paper does report group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps and within-group results (satisfying I6) and includes relevant participant groups (I7) and clearly describes whole-brain results in the text (I8). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI during a monetary reward-learning task emphasizing reward prediction error (RPE) and connectivity (gPPI). However, it did not manipulate or contrast risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making conditions (no contrasts such as “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”). The task and reported contrasts focus on RPE/RE/OE and seed-based connectivity; activation analyses were constrained to a reward-related mask rather than presenting an unmasked whole-brain task activation map relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement that the fMRI task be a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm (Exclusion E5). Met inclusion criteria: I7 (participant group acceptable) and I8 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). Not met: I4 (task is not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts), I6 (no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked activation map for a qualifying decision-making contrast).

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans during a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game) with explicit risky vs. cautious choices and decision-periods (I4). It uses an active control condition (Directed Trials) and reports the key contrast (Decision Trial – Directed Trial) and separate analyses for risky vs. cautious deliberation, satisfying the allowed decision>control and within-task contrasts (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM8 maps with cluster-level FWE correction and reported cluster/tables/figures, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements (I6, I8). Participant groups include adolescents with conduct/substance problems and matched comparisons, which are acceptable per eligibility (I7). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing reversal learning tasks that explicitly manipulate outcome uncertainty (four-choice task) and compare neural responses to unexpected non-reinforcement at reversal versus expected reinforcement. The four-choice condition represents decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguity), and the primary contrasts are condition-vs-condition (non-reinforcement vs expected reinforcement) rather than task>rest. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FSL Randomize with TFCE) and reported. Participants include clinical and control groups, which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI of ambiguous decision-making with whole-brain group maps and condition contrasts.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a decision-making task that involves risk (choice to take a challenge with probabilistic shock) and a perceptual discrimination challenge (vowel vs consonant). It includes within-task condition contrasts (Discouragement vs Control; Discouragement-successful > Control-successful) at the group random-effects level, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported MNI coordinates and cluster corrections. Results include activation maps (insula, striatum) and psychophysiological interaction analyses, but critically also GLM whole-brain activation contrasts. Participants are healthy adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: E6 (only ROI-masked/striatum analyses reported; no whole-brain, unmasked voxelwise group-level task activation maps provided). Included criteria met: I4 (fMRI collected during a probabilistic loss-learning decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrasts/model-based contrasts for positive vs negative prediction errors and C− vs C+ drug-state contrasts), I7 (participant group acceptable—clinical substance-using sample), I8 (whole-brain-style results and coordinates/cluster statistics are described in the text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no whole-brain, unmasked group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps; analyses were masked to the striatum and therefore constitute ROI-restricted results). Because E6 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study that used a perceptual decision-making task (backward-masked majority function task) manipulating task difficulty/information rate (hard > easy) and exposure time. It reports within-subject condition contrasts (main effects of information entropy, reciprocal of ET, and their interaction) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults using a risky decision-making investment task with probabilistic outcomes. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Buy – Did Not Buy, Obedient – Not Obedient) that qualify as risky > safe and other decision-making contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 results with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level correction, and results are reported in text and figures. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not rest contrasts only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

The study employed an fMRI Stroop cognitive-control task and contrasts (incongruent vs neutral, blocked/event-related Stroop effects) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses reported using FLAME and whole-brain thresholding), I7 (participant groups are acceptable — healthy adolescents and adults), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not performed during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making contrasts of the admitted forms such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore excluded for not addressing the review’s decision-making task domain.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human volunteers performing a risky decision-making task (risky £1 vs safer 10p choices) inside the scanner. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses identifying neural correlates of decision-related parametric modulators (choice temperature βm and learning rate αm) and contrasts comparing ketamine vs placebo sessions (paired t-tests). These constitute within-task, condition-related task contrasts (trial-wise high vs low decision-related signals) and not task>rest contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps (cluster-corrected) and described in the text. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only, and includes within-group whole-brain effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI and whole-brain group analyses during a probabilistic reversal learning task, but the task is a reinforcement/reversal-learning paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. The reported contrasts focus on negative vs positive feedback, reversal errors, and history effects (e.g., FINREVERR vs REVERR, NEG+2 vs NEG+0), not on risk (e.g., risky>safe), ambiguity (e.g., ambiguous>non-ambiguous), or perceptual difficulty (e.g., hard>easy) contrasts required by I5. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task not in targeted DM categories). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps present), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM per the protocol) and I5 (no qualifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the task is a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement-learning) paradigm and the reported analyses focus on parametric PE regressors rather than contrasts that match risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making comparisons. Specifically, no contrasts of the form risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses were performed) and I8 (results reported with coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined for this meta-analysis) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts are presented). Exclusion criterion invoked: E5 (task does not fit the risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM categories required). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a choice reaction-time task that manipulates uncertainty/entropy (high vs low entropy) during decision-making. It reports within-task contrasts (entropy/response-alternative and reversal contrasts), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM and single-trial analyses, and presents whole-brain results (maps/tables). Participant sample is healthy adults. The task contrasts include high- vs low-uncertainty comparisons consistent with ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

While the study acquired simultaneous EEG–fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (I4) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results (I6) with healthy participants (I7) and whole-brain results/tables described in the text (I8), it does not present any eligible decision-making contrast as required by I5 (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, or hard>easy). The reported analyses focus on parametric regressors (signed and absolute RPEs), EEG-informed fMRI associations, and DCM rather than contrasts comparing decision conditions or a task vs active control. Therefore I5 is not met and the study is excluded.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain task-evoked activations during value-based choices between snack items, but the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is value-based choice, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), I7 (healthy human participants included), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making — NOT met), I5 (at least one accepted decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, high uncertainty>low, or hard>easy — NOT met). Full text is complete. Therefore the study does not satisfy the core eligibility for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This fMRI study used the weather prediction probabilistic category-learning task (prediction > perceptual-motor baseline), so it involves decision-making under uncertainty and includes an active task>control contrast (I4 and I5). Participants are human and groups are acceptable (I7), and whole-brain results are described in the text/figures (I8). However, the authors performed an ROI-based SPM factorial ANOVA (analyses were restricted to anatomical ROI masks from the AAL library) and report only ROI-focused activation results. They did not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map; thus the study reports only ROI analyses and lacks whole-brain voxelwise task maps (violates I6) and meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house categorization with asymmetric costs), satisfying I4. The paper contains condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., cost > neutral, FV > HV, HV > FV, and uncertainty-related contrasts), satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and inference are reported (whole-brain FWE cluster correction and coordinates; SVC also used), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample is healthy human adults, which is acceptable per I7. None of the exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are not only versus baseline/rest (E3), the modality is fMRI not PET (E4), the task is a perceptual decision-making task (not excluded by E5), whole-brain results are provided (not E6), and the study is empirical with original fMRI data (not E9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, include this study in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (BART) in adolescents with group-level whole-brain results and relevant ROIs, but it reports the main effect of risk decisions (pump events) relative to an implicit baseline. The paper does not present a condition-vs-condition contrast (e.g., risky > safe or pump > cash-out) nor a task > active control contrast. According to the review criteria, studies whose only decision-making contrasts are against an implicit baseline must be excluded (E3). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion I5 (required condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded due to E3.

This study used fMRI and whole-brain group analyses of a probabilistic reversal-learning task (feedback: positive vs negative; loss/switch vs loss/stay), but it does not probe the meta-analysis’ target domains (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) nor report the specific decision-making contrasts required. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level whole-brain maps were reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results described). Inclusion not met: I4 (task is reversal learning/feedback-guided learning, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM paradigm as defined by the review), I5 (no accepted risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as “risky>safe”, “ambiguity>non-ambiguous”, or “hard>easy”; primary contrasts are reward vs. punishment and switch/stay). Exclusion applied: E5 (decision-making task is not one of risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM per the review criteria). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a temporally-extended probabilistic categorization task (perceptual decision-making with uncertainty). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts (categorical evidence, confidence, and their modulation by urgency — effectively high vs low evidence states) and compares models, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM analyses, FWER/topological FDR corrections) presented in figures and tables. Participants are healthy adults. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (I6) and tests uncertainty-related contrasts (e.g., variance/inverted-U; consistent with “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”) and thus meets I5, and the participant sample is acceptable (I7) and results are clearly reported (I8), the scanned task was a passive conditioning/imperative task (participants pressed a button indicating stimulus quadrant) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task performed during fMRI. The authors explicitly state they used conditioning “to study the processing of economic parameters independent of choice.” Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (task must be a decision-making task performed during fMRI). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This is an fMRI study of human risky decision-making (choice between certain amount and gamble) with 21 healthy participants, meeting I4. The analyses include condition contrasts comparing risky versus non-risky choices and other task-based contrasts (e.g., risky > certain; amount-related contrasts), satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level voxelwise GLMs and second-level one-sample t-tests with reported MNI coordinates and voxelwise inference (with Small Volume Correction applied to ROIs), indicating availability of whole-brain, group-level statistical maps or coordinate-based whole-brain results, satisfying I6 and I8. Participant sample are healthy adults, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only without whole-brain results, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a behavioral/structural MRI study of decision-making in MS using the Game-of-Dice Task and 2-D ventricular width measures. It does not include any fMRI data or task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Exclusion rationale: No fMRI scanning during the decision-making task (failed I4), no within-task or task-vs-control whole-brain contrasts reported (failed I5 and I6), and no whole-brain activation coordinates/ maps provided (failed I8). The study does include a human participant group that would otherwise qualify (I7). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E3–E9) are directly met. Therefore the study must be excluded from the fMRI meta-analysis because it lacks fMRI task-based whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study (n=15 and n=14) in which participants performed a two-stage decision-making task involving foraging and gamble choices with explicit probabilities (Stage 2 probabilities 20–90%). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses (SPM8) with parametric contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., relative foraging value vs. engage; choice difficulty regressors; high vs. low value similarity), and presents whole-brain t-statistic maps and ROI analyses. These satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: (I4) fMRI during risky/decision-making (probabilistic gambles), (I5) condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., relative value, difficulty, chosen vs unchosen), (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps, (I7) acceptable participant group (healthy humans), and (I8) results reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, online methods).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a risky decision-making task (Modified Cups Task) and tests contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., decision after loss vs decision after win; feedback risk win vs risk loss). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded with cluster correction; peak coordinates and cluster tables are reported. Participants include healthy controls and frequent poker players. The task is a risky DM paradigm and the reported contrasts are within-task condition comparisons, thus meeting the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making contrasts. Full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and imaging), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult humans using a gambling task that manipulates risk and counterfactuals (regret). The authors report within-subject contrasts comparing decision-making versus control computer-chosen conditions (IP minus IF; OP minus OF), which qualifies as task > control (risky > control). Data were analyzed with whole-brain, group-level random-effects SPM analyses, conjunctions, and reported activation coordinates and thresholded maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, participants, fMRI acquisition and whole-brain analysis), Results and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants investigating perceptual decision-making (high visibility, low-visibility perceptual guessing, and free decisions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (searchlight decoding and univariate GLM) with reported cluster statistics and MNI coordinates. It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g. FDC > PGC) and cross-condition classification between perceptual-guessing and free-decision conditions, satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast. The work is not PET, not ROI-only, and not resting-state/connectivity-only. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (fMRI-adapted BART) with a clear active vs passive task contrast (active>passive). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects) with cluster-corrected results, tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (task vs active control contrast), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). None of the exclusion criteria apply (not a PET, not only ROI or connectivity, contrasts are task vs control not baseline, and contains within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables referenced).

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that used a probabilistic choice task (participants chose higher vs lower than 5 for cues with 85% vs 65% predictive probabilities). The task involves decision-making under differing levels of uncertainty (easy = low uncertainty; hard = high uncertainty), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM statistical maps and coordinates (random-effects SPMs) with contrasts that include cue difficulty (easy > hard / high uncertainty > low uncertainty) and learning-type contrasts. Thus the study provides within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts mapping onto ambiguous decision-making (high uncertainty > low uncertainty), meets whole-brain reporting, and includes appropriate participant sampling. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making under uncertainty), I5 (condition contrast: hard vs easy/high uncertainty vs low uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (results reported with coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy humans (n=30) using a perceptual decision-making task (bistable motion) and presents within-task contrasts (incoherent > coherent) comparing perceptual decision conditions. Group-level, whole-brain RFX-GLM voxelwise results, statistical maps, and coordinates are reported, and methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment using the BART (a risky decision-making task) with parametric modulation of risk and an active > passive decision-making contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed (2×2 ANOVA) with cluster correction and coordinates are reported. Within-task contrasts (active vs passive; risk-related modulation within groups) are presented and post-hoc tests reported. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during a risky decision task), I5 (decision-making contrasts: active>passive and risk modulation analogous to high-risk>low-risk), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (Cups task) with an explicit risky>safe contrast (I4, I5). Participants are humans and age range fits (I7), and results/coordinates are reported in detail (I8). However, the paper's reported group-level task activation results for the risky>safe contrast were analyzed/thresholded within an a priori anterior insula ROI rather than presented as a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. While the study does report whole-brain PPI (connectivity) results, it does not provide a whole-brain group-level task activation map for the decision contrast, so it effectively reports ROI-only task activation (violates inclusion I6) and thus meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only, no whole-brain task results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic feedback decision task (choices between high/low with 83%/67%/50% reward probabilities) performed during scanning. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (with cluster correction) and provide coordinates/tables for activations. They model and test trial-by-trial uncertainty (a parametric modulator) and other decision-related contrasts (action values, action-dependent and action-independent prediction errors), which correspond to contrasts of high vs low uncertainty / action-dependent decision signals. Participants were healthy adults. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a decision task with uncertainty), I5 (decision-related contrasts via parametric modulators, e.g., uncertainty/high vs low), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans performing perceptual decision-making (visual motion coherence and auditory detection). The authors report within-task decision contrasts (hits vs misses, correct rejections vs false alarms; hit>false alarm) that probe perceptual outcomes, and they present group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported maps and cluster-level statistics) in addition to ROI analyses. Participants are healthy adults and the full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (orientation discrimination of Gabor patches with manipulated discriminability/contrast). The analysis included within-task comparisons that index perceptual difficulty/discriminability (high- vs low-contrast trials, implemented via trial-by-trial parametric regressors and model comparisons), and reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM2 random-effects ANOVA with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates). Participants were healthy adults. The paper therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing risky decision-making (social trust and matched non-social gamble) with explicit risk probabilities (meets I4). The design includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (risky vs certain; social vs non-social) and group-level ANOVAs (meets I5). The paper reports group-level voxel coordinates and peak activations (e.g., ventral striatum, amygdala) and references whole-brain contrasts/tables alongside ROI analyses, indicating whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results are available (meets I6 and I8). Participants are healthy adults (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), task is risky decision-making (not excluded social-only without uncertainty), and whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI to measure BOLD responses to passive viewing of random-dot motion while participants performed an orthogonal fixation task; it did not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task about the motion stimuli, nor did it report decision-making contrasts. Analyses focus on retinotopically-defined ROI averages rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps. Therefore it fails the key inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it did not perform functional MRI during task performance and did not report task-evoked whole-brain fMRI contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant group acceptable — MS patients and healthy controls). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (no fMRI scan conducted while participants performed the decision-making task — only structural MRI (DOC, FA, MD, volumetry) was acquired), I5 (no fMRI task contrasts such as risky>safe or analogous fMRI condition contrasts were reported), I6 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or voxelwise fMRI results), I8 (no whole-brain fMRI results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria from the review checklist (E3–E9) are directly triggered, but failure to meet I4/I5/I6 mandates exclusion. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although this fMRI study reports group-level, whole-brain, decision-phase contrasts and clearly manipulates uncertainty in a trust game (FAIR/INDIFFERENT/UNFAIR partners), it is a social decision-making (trust) task. The review’s exclusion criterion E5 explicitly excludes social decision-making tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous decision-like task), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing partner decision conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I4–I8 satisfied). Primary exclusion: E5 (task is social decision-making and therefore outside scope). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDE under E5 despite meeting the technical fMRI and contrast requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between sure wins and lotteries) while scanned. The paper reports within-task contrasts (presence vs absence of advice; parametric modulators for offer magnitude and certainty equivalents indexing safe vs risky valuation) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-level corrected t-maps, reported coordinates and brain maps). Participants include adolescents and adults (healthy), and results are presented in main text and supplementary materials. Thus it meets all inclusion requirements for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is an ultimatum/dictator social fairness task (decision to punish/accept unfair offers), which is social/economic decision-making, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task contrasts reported: UG (unfair–fair) and UG−DG contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) — the task does not involve risk/uncertainty or perceptual difficulty as defined by the review. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (feedback processing and behavioral adaptation) rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. The reported contrasts compare error versus correct responses or switch versus nonswitch errors, not the canonical contrasts required for risky (e.g., risky>safe), ambiguous (e.g., high uncertainty>low uncertainty), or perceptual (e.g., hard>easy) decision-making. Although the study provides group-level whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates and includes healthy human participants, it does not meet the required task/contrast definitions for inclusion. Therefore it is excluded under E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (coordinates and whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM by the review definitions), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports whole-brain fMRI in healthy human participants performing a sequential investment task that involves risk/uncertainty (risky decision-making). It provides group-level, voxelwise task-evoked analyses: parametric contrasts for fictive errors and temporal-difference (TD) errors within Attend and Regulate conditions, and direct Attend vs Regulate comparisons (including reported activations and tables). The task is a canonical risky decision-making paradigm (investment under market uncertainty), and results are reported as whole-brain maps/coordinates (not ROI-only). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) during scanning and included risk/ambiguity manipulations (easy, hard, ambiguous trials and shock anticipation linked to performance). The analyses include within-task contrasts and parametric modulators relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., coherence modulation, a 2×2 RepHigh/RepLow × Easy/Uncertain ANOVA, and parametric conformity/dissent contrasts), and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM8 second-level random-effects analyses; FDR and SVC corrections) with coordinates/tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic decision-making (beads/JTC) task that manipulates uncertainty. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (with FWE correction) as well as ROI results, and includes contrasts comparing the decision task to an active control task (JTC blocks > control blocks) and event-related contrasts (last fish > preceding fish) that index decision-making under uncertainty. Participants are healthy humans. Results are reported with coordinates and whole-brain statistical inference. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not only ROI; not resting-state/connectivity-only; not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing an investment task involving risk (I4). It includes condition contrasts/parametric task regressors related to decision variables (DJONES and MKT) and a between-condition contrast comparing human partner vs computer control (human>computer) relevant to the decision context (I5). Group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses are reported (t-tests), with at least one whole-brain FWE-corrected result and whole-brain reporting (figures/tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6, I8). Participant sample is appropriate human subjects (I7). Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants that includes a risky decision-making Control task (a probabilistic one-armed bandit) performed during scanning and model-based, within-task parametric contrasts (reward probability and prediction errors) that probe decision variables. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses with coordinates/tables and figures (satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting). Participants are healthy human subjects (n=36). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/decision task), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric decision-related regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply: contrasts are not only against implicit baseline, modality is fMRI (not PET), task includes risky DM (control task), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and this is an empirical study with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

Although this fMRI study used a probabilistic (65% vs 35%) reward-learning task (meets I4) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets I6) with results described in the text/tables (meets I8) and an eligible participant sample (meets I7), it does not include any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the review (e.g., “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “risk > certainty”, or an explicit decision-task > control-task contrast). The reported analyses focus on parametric RPE and value regressors and emotional (fearful vs neutral) modulations, not on between-condition decision-making contrasts of risk/ambiguity or hard>easy perceptual difficulty. Therefore Inclusion Criterion I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are directly met, but failure to meet I5 mandates exclusion.

Excluded under E5: the task is a probabilistic category-learning (weather prediction) nondeclarative learning task rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. The study does meet several methodological inclusion criteria: I5 (it reports a task > active control contrast: weather prediction > perceptual-motor control), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM99), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). However I4 is not met because the experimental task is a category-learning/memory task, not a risky, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty decision-making task per the meta-analysis definitions. Full text appears complete and was reviewed in detail.

Excluded because the task is social/moral decision-making (truth-telling under asymmetric information) rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual; it is social/moral). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as required), I5 (no contrast matching the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts — the main contrast is true advice > false advice, a social honesty contrast rather than risky>safe or ambiguity contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This study used an intertemporal delay discounting task (choices between smaller-sooner and larger-later rewards), which is explicitly excluded by criterion E5 (delay discounting/intertemporal choice is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The full text reports within-task contrasts versus an active control (SS vs CON; LL vs CON), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and participant details, so it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, and I8 but fails I4 (task type). Full text appears complete. Exclusion: E5.

This fMRI study used a rewarded gambling (wheel-of-fortune) task that manipulates win probability (25/50/75%), i.e. a risky decision-making paradigm, and acquired task-evoked BOLD data during decision, anticipation, and outcome phases. The authors report group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (with whole-brain correction for non-ROI effects and ROI small-volume correction) and provide coordinates/figures of activations. Relevant contrasts include gambling vs control (rewarded vs non-rewarded), anticipation (rewarded > non-rewarded), and outcome (wins > losses), satisfying condition-vs-control and within-task contrasts. Participants were healthy human volunteers. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dynamically adaptive motion prediction). The authors report within-task condition contrasts (errors with negative feedback vs correct trials with positive feedback), which reflect comparisons between decision-making conditions (errors correspond to more difficult/uncertain perceptual decisions), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (voxel-wise one-sample t tests, z-maps, tables/figures), and coordinates/activations are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic two-armed bandit decision-making task (uncertain/risky reward learning). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps) for a decision-related parametric contrast (chosen expected value Q at time of choice) and for outcome-related RPE regressors, satisfying the requirement for a within-task, decision-related contrast. Participants are healthy human adults (younger and older). Whole-brain results are presented with coordinates and figures. Although the study also collected PET, it is not a PET-only paper and includes unmasked, whole-brain fMRI activation maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a decision task involving explicit probabilistic outcomes (risk) while deciding whether to transfer a point (altruistic/helping under risk). The paper reports within-task contrasts and factorial comparisons (no self-risk vs high self-risk; low vs high other-need), parametric modulators of self-risk and other-need, and group-level whole-brain GLM results (voxelwise thresholds and cluster FWE correction). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Although the paradigm has a social/altruistic element, the decision variable is explicit probabilistic risk and thus fits the risky decision-making category. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study uses a reward-learning task contrasting choice versus no-choice and reward versus no reward; analyses are whole-brain and reported at the group level. However, the primary task manipulation probes the intrinsic value of personal choice and reinforcement learning rather than decision-making under risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. The paper does not report contrasts of the form required for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, hard > easy). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrasts) and does not clearly meet I4 as a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (results reported in text/figures). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts for perceptual decision-making and does not report whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps. Specifically: Exclusion criteria met: E3 (decision-making contrasts are task > rest/implicit baseline, e.g., JLO vs Rest). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI was collected during perceptual tasks such as the Judgment of Line Orientation) and I7 (healthy human participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no eligible decision-making contrast such as hard>easy or perceptual task>active control; contrasts reported are primarily task vs rest), and I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps; analyses are component/ICA-based and component-wise GLMs rather than unmasked voxelwise maps). Full text appears complete so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because failure to meet I5 and I6 and presence of E3 disqualify the study from inclusion in the meta-analysis, I exclude it.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (E5). This is a value-based food vs. nonfood purchasing task (BDM auction) and thus falls outside the meta-analysis domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported with second-level GLMs and coordinate tables/figures), I7 (human healthy participants), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (the reported contrasts compare food vs nonfood valuation and sleep states rather than the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms required by the review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

This study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (exclusion E5). It instead examines statistical learning and prediction of symbolic sequences (prediction task), and though it contrasts structured vs. random sequences, the task is a learning/prediction paradigm rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM. The paper also emphasizes ICA-based component and connectivity analyses and reports task effects as component β changes rather than providing a standard group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrast map; thus it effectively reports component/ connectivity results without the required voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps, fitting exclusion E7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (there is a contrast between two task conditions: structured vs. random), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (spatial maps/peak coordinates are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm), I6 (no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map appropriate for the meta-analysis). Therefore the study should be excluded.

Excluded because the task is social bargaining (Ultimatum Game) rather than a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social decision-making, which is listed as an example of tasks to exclude). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions, e.g., slightly selfish > fair and fair > selfish), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported), I7 (healthy adult participants; participant groups are acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review; it is social/fairness-driven UG proposing). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite having whole-brain fMRI contrasts, because the decision-making domain does not match the review focus (E5).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a probabilistic (stochastic) classification task (weather prediction task) — a decision-making task under uncertainty (ambiguous/probabilistic). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects, FDR-corrected) with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster tables. It contains at least one task-versus-active-control contrast (WPT > control task during presentation and feedback periods) and within-task contrasts relevant to uncertainty (high > low predictive value). Participants are healthy humans. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision task under uncertainty), I5 (task > control and within-task contrasts), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only baseline contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses an fMRI trust game (human vs computer counterparts) that is a social decision-making task focused on betrayal aversion. The review’s exclusion criterion E5 explicitly excludes moral or social decision-making tasks. Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level SPM results and contrasts that include a risky > safe style comparison (trusting > not trusting) and provides coordinate tables, the task is fundamentally social/trust-based rather than the non-social risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making targeted by the meta-analysis. Therefore it fails the inclusion requirement about task domain (I4) and must be excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI study of shogi problem-solving (generation of next-move) with whole-brain group analyses and contrasts versus an active sensory-motor control. However, the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making: its task is rule-based problem-solving/strategy evaluation rather than risk/ambiguity/perceptual DM. Therefore it fails the domain-specific inclusion criterion and must be excluded. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task vs active control contrast present), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (human participant groups), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Full text appears complete.

This study conducted 3T fMRI while participants performed two-arm bandit decision-making tasks with probabilistic rewards and changing reward probabilities (social: faces smiling; non-social: houses open/locked). The fMRI analyses modeled volatility (uncertainty), prediction errors, and value expectation and tested whole-brain voxelwise encodings, reporting cluster coordinates and t-values (group-level whole-brain results). Thus it satisfies: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (parametric contrasts/analyses of uncertainty/volatility and decision-related computations consistent with ambiguous/risky decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not PET, does not report only ROI or connectivity, and includes within-task computational modulators rather than only task>rest contrasts. Although one task was social, a non-social bandit was also acquired and modeled, and volatility/uncertainty-related regressors map onto ambiguous/risky DM constructs. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling (risky decision-making) task during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts that separate outcomes by risk level (e.g., aversive outcomes following low-, medium-, and high-risk choices), parametric risk-level analyses (linear effects across odds), and pharmacological challenge interactions; these constitute condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results (FWE-corrected clusters reported, peak MNI coordinates provided), and additional ROI and ASL checks are supplementary. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making with whole-brain task-evoked maps.

This study used event-related fMRI of probabilistic reversal learning in Parkinson's patients, focusing on feedback-related and reversal-related activations (e.g., final reversal errors > correct responses). Although it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I6), includes a clinical participant group (I7), and provides whole-brain results in text/figures/tables (I8), it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis. The experimental contrasts (final reversal errors vs correct responses; nonswitch errors vs correct responses) index reversal-learning and feedback processing rather than formal risky/ambiguous choice contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task per the meta-analysis definitions. Full text appears complete. Hence EXCLUDED.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) (I4). It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (risky vs safe decisions) and reports group-by-decision analyses (risky > safe / risky vs safe contrasts are analyzed) (I5). Second-level, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (AlphaSim) are performed and reported (I6). Participant groups include substance-using and comparison subjects, which are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to baseline contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, and the report includes within-task condition contrasts rather than only between-group effects. The provided full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI and reports whole-brain group results (meets I6) in a healthy sample (meets I7) and provides whole-brain results/coordinates (meets I8), the behavioral paradigm does not constitute a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as required by the review. The gambling task contrasts focus on reward vs. punishment (value) and salience (reward+punishment vs neutral) rather than condition contrasts that manipulate risk/uncertainty levels or compare risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy perceptual conditions. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that experimentally manipulated decision difficulty and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making. The task required subjects to decide whether a presented probe color matched one or more memorized colors; sample–probe similarity (match, similar non-match, dissimilar non-match) and memory load (1 vs 3 items) produced condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., similarity main effect; high vs low load), which map onto perceptual decision-making contrasts (hard > easy). Analyses were whole-brain SPM random-effects ANOVAs with FDR correction and peak coordinates/tables reported. No exclusion criteria were triggered: contrasts are not baseline-only, the modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and the task fits within the perceptual decision-making domain as argued by the authors. Full text is complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (category judgments based on perceptual features) that manipulates uncertainty. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Far > Flanking, Flanking > Far, Training > Far) and parametric contrasts (distance from decision bound, distance from prototype), satisfying the requirement for decision-making condition comparisons. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs conducted with SPM8 and corrected for multiple comparisons; results are reported as statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Participants are healthy undergraduates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not contrasts only vs implicit baseline). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using probabilistic choice tasks (displayed reward probabilities in planning trials; learned probabilistic rewards in trained trials), constituting risky decision-making with known probabilities. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (planning > trained, trained > planning, mixed PE and EE contrasts) and parametric value contrasts, i.e., within-task comparisons rather than task>rest. Group-level whole-brain analyses are reported (whole-brain parametric and categorical contrasts; FWE-corrected results and ROI analyses). Participants are healthy adults. Results and maps/statistics are described in the main text and tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task vs baseline only) are violated. Note: although the paper frames decisions as model-based vs model-free rather than explicitly as “risky” in label, the use of known probabilistic reward contingencies satisfies the review’s risky decision-making domain. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Excluded because the study does not report any qualifying decision-making contrast (I5) required for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, or an experimental risk task > control task). The paper reports an fMRI probability-discounting (risky) task (I4) and provides whole-brain, group-level parametric maps of subjective value (I6) with coordinates reported (I8), and includes eligible participant groups (gamblers and controls; I7). However, the primary reported analyses are seed-based PPI connectivity contrasts (between-group connectivity effects) and a model-based subjective-value map; there is no within-task contrast that matches the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts (I5). Therefore it cannot be used for the required task-contrast meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human healthy adults using a risky decision-making task (the Cups task) with immediate feedback. It reports task contrasts of interest (e.g., Risky > Safe and Win > Loss), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-based correction, and provides coordinates and figures for significant activations. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (relevant decision-making contrasts such as risky > safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents that used a risky decision-making task (the Social Analogue Risk Task) during scanning and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps. The authors modeled knock, cash-out, and slam events and used a parametric modulator (cash-out PM) indexing increasing risk (number of knocks) and conducted whole-brain group analyses (including cluster-corrected results). Results (main effects and regressions) are reported across the whole brain in the text and figures. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast via parametric modulation of risk/cash-out), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (human adolescent sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (two-option lottery Selection task) with fMRI acquisition and group-level whole-brain analyses. Reported task contrasts include within-task decision contrasts such as riskier > surer, gains > losses, and choice-determined value contrasts, satisfying the required risky-DM contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates reported in tables/supplementary materials. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents using the Decision–Reward Uncertainty task that manipulates behavioral risk and reward risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., behavioral risk > reward risk + no risk; reward > no reward) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for (I4) fMRI during risky decision-making, (I5) condition-versus-condition contrasts, (I6) whole-brain group-level maps, (I7) acceptable participant group (healthy adolescents), and (I8) reporting of coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines risky decision making using a framing task (sure vs gamble under gain/loss frames) with healthy human participants. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., the framing-effect interaction: (Gsure + Lgamble) − (Ggamble + Lsure) and its reverse), and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests, whole-brain regression, cluster correction, and tables of activations). Behavioral and imaging results, methods, and discussion are present in the provided full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion), and activation results are presented in tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., contrasts are not only vs implicit baseline, not PET, task is a risky decision-making paradigm, whole-brain results are reported, and it is an empirical report). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving simulation) with human adolescents. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe decisions (Go > Stop and Stop > Go) and feedback contrasts (Crash vs No-Crash). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (voxelwise threshold p = .001, cluster thresholds; tables of coordinates and figures provided). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making whole-brain activation contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion coherence) with response-signal manipulation. The analyses include condition-wise (motion coherence × duration) GLMs, parametric contrasts for motion coherence (equivalent to 'low coherence > high coherence' / 'hard > easy'), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (spatial maps normalized to MNI) and ICA-derived whole-brain components. Results are reported at the group level with spatial maps and ROIs; whole-text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition contrasts/parametric comparisons relevant to perceptual DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic wheel-of-fortune task (risky decision-making). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts of decision task versus non-reward control trials (e.g., anticipation [AR1, AR2, AR3] > AnRn; outcome contrasts versus OnwRn), satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-control contrasts. The full text includes methods, results, and tables of coordinates and description of whole-brain findings, meeting whole-brain evidence reporting. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion summary: E5 applies — the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm but a visuomotor/sequence-statistics finger-tapping task assessing entropy and surprise in stimulus/action sequences. Included criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses were conducted and reported), I7 (healthy adult participants were tested), I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and supplementary material). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (there is no eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrast of the forms required by the review; the main contrast is choice vs specified action related to sequence regularity, not risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded under E5.

The study used fMRI while participants performed perceptual decision-making tasks (spatial comparison and shape comparison), with active baseline target-detection trials and contrasts of interest (spatial comparison > baseline; within- vs between-image comparisons). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise activation and contrasts are reported in the text and figures. Participants were healthy adults. Thus it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI (I4, I5) and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps at the group level (I6). Reporting in figures/text meets I8, and participant population is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting-state/ROI-only; contrasts are against an active control rather than implicit baseline). Full text appears complete.

Although the study used fMRI during a reinforcement-learning choice task (three-armed bandit) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and reported coordinates, its reported contrasts focus on novelty-bonus and reward prediction error (model-based parametric modulators) rather than contrasts that map onto risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high uncertainty > low uncertainty, hard > easy). The task manipulates stimulus novelty and reward learning rather than explicit risk or ambiguity levels, and no accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast (I5) is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast per the meta-analysis definitions). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (coordinates/results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic guessing task involving monetary rewards and penalties (risky decision-making), and reports contrasts comparing high- vs low-loss probability during number presentation and loss > win outcomes (meets I4 and I5). Participant groups (MDD and healthy controls) are acceptable (I7). However, the MRI acquisition was limited to 23 oblique slices centered on the epithalamus (not whole-brain), and all group-level statistical analyses were conducted on beta coefficients averaged within manually defined habenula ROIs; the paper does not report unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore the study fails the whole-brain requirement (I6) and reports only ROI analyses (violating E6), so it must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not provide task-evoked, whole-brain fMRI results for a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the behavioral paradigm is a time-perception/interval estimation task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E7 (the neuroimaging data reported are resting-state seed-based connectivity analyses rather than task-evoked whole-brain activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant group is acceptable; healthy volunteers were tested). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan performed while subjects completed a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrast comparing decision-making conditions such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), and I6 (no group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Only the abstract/full text excerpt is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract we can confirm fMRI was used during a decision-making task (I4) and participant type is acceptable (I7). However, the full text is not available to verify critical inclusion criteria: there is no clear description of the specific task contrasts meeting I5 (e.g., risky>safe or equivalent) nor confirmation that group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps were reported (I6). It is also unclear whether results are reported beyond summary activations (tables/coordinates) as required (I8). Because the full text is incomplete and these mandatory inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study must be excluded pending access to the full article.

This study uses fMRI but investigates social valuation of equality in choice opportunity (number of options, equality between self and other) rather than manipulations of risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. It does not implement risky vs safe, high- vs low-risk, ambiguity contrasts, or hard vs easy perceptual decisions as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported, including exploratory whole-brain FWE-corrected results), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (reported contrasts are about option number and equality, not the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI study with human participants performing a decision task that explicitly manipulates ambiguity (ambiguous context vs. generalization context) and examines neural correlates of ambiguity during choices. The task contrasts high-ambiguity and low-ambiguity conditions and uses a model-based (Shannon entropy) regressor indexing ambiguity, which was tested at the group level. Analyses include whole-brain SPM second-level results with cluster-level FWE correction and ROI analyses; whole-brain activations for ambiguity (right hippocampus/amygdala, fusiform/precuneus) are reported. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI human ambiguous decision-making), I5 (condition contrasts: high vs low ambiguity / ambiguity parametric regressor), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (healthy participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a social/prosocial reinforcement learning fMRI experiment (learning to benefit self, another person, or no one) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is social decision-making, which the meta-analysis excludes).
