Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the paper contains within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions, e.g., prosocial vs self, prosocial vs no one), I6 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (human participant sample appropriate), and I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the fMRI task examined prosocial/microlending (charitable lending) decisions rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making, thus meeting exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study contains a within-task contrast: choices to lend vs not lend), I6 (reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the fMRI task was not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task required by the review objective). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused specifically on risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making.

This study is excluded because the fMRI data were collected while participants passively viewed celebrity faces and performed a simple luminance-detection button-press (an attention task), not while they performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. The actual choice behavior (voting between two celebrities) occurred after scanning outside the scanner. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, hard>easy, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or task>control) are NOT met. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses were performed via searchlight MVPA with second-level one-sample t-tests), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported in the text). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (the decision-making task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task — it is a social preference task). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (moving-dots). The analyses include within-task contrasts comparing cue conditions (reliable vs. neutral and moderate vs. neutral) that index decision-making processes (prior/probabilistic cues) and a conjunction analysis; these are condition-versus-condition contrasts rather than task>rest. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects maps are reported with cluster correction and Talairach coordinates; results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8).

The study used fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic two-armed bandit (decision-making under uncertainty) and reports group whole-brain analyses; however it does not include any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the meta-analysis (e.g. risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguity > non-ambiguous, or perceptual hard > easy). Instead, analyses focus on model-based parametric modulators (R(t), Q(t)) and reward prediction errors rather than contrasts comparing levels of risk/ambiguity or task > control. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that implemented a risky decision-making task (the Risk-Taking Task) with clear risky and guaranteed reward conditions. The paper reports within-task contrasts (low-penalty vs no-penalty; high-penalty vs no-penalty; no-penalty vs motor control), and group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster correction. Participant groups (substance-dependent patients and controls) are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an event-related fMRI study (3T) in healthy human participants performing a game-theory-based risky decision task (iterated game of Chicken) involving risky/aggressive vs safe/reconciliatory choices. The design included within-subject contrasts (selection: risky vs safe) and opponent contrasts (human > computer), and a 2×2 factorial analysis; group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses are reported (whole-brain FDR-corrected results and tables/figures). Full article contains methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, and task involves risky decision-making rather than purely social/no-uncertainty paradigms). Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied.

Exclusion: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). This fMRI study examined clinical reasoning using vignette-based MCQs (answering vs reflection) in experts and novices. It meets several inclusion items: I5 (within-task contrast: answer > reflection), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with FWE correction), I7 (human participant groups; healthy physicians/interns), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). However it fails I4: the decision-making task is clinical diagnostic reasoning (MCQs), not one of the meta-analysis target paradigms (risky-DM, ambiguous-DM, or perceptual-DM). Because the primary exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task not of the targeted types) is met, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI while participants performed a perceptual phoneme categorization task (auditory post-tests) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects maps (satisfies I4, I6, I8). However, it does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast as required by I5 (e.g., hard>easy, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or a task>active control). The primary whole-brain contrasts presented are audiovisual exposure blocks > baseline and a behaviorally weighted parametric modulation of exposure-block activation predicting later perception; no explicit within-scan contrasts directly comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., ambiguous vs less-ambiguous post-tests or hard vs easy perceptual trials) are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criterion E3 applies because the study’s main whole-brain task contrast is versus baseline and no appropriate condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast is provided. Full text appears complete.

EXCLUDED because the study does not provide a qualifying decision-making contrast per the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5). Although this is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a two-choice perceptual discrimination (color) task (meets I4), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures (meets I6 and I8), and participants qualify (meets I7), the critical requirement I5 is not met: the reported contrasts examine temporal expectancy (good vs bad clock) and accessory (vibration) effects, and task>rest contrasts, but do not include perceptual difficulty or perceptual decision contrasts of the accepted forms (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>active control) nor ambiguity/risk contrasts (high uncertainty>low uncertainty in the decision dimension). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) were triggered. Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study where human participants performed a mixed-gamble (risk) decision-making task (50/50 gains/losses) during T2*-weighted EPI scanning (I4 satisfied). The authors report within-task contrasts (neural gain sensitivity and neural loss sensitivity parametric modulators) and group-level ANOVAs/ T-maps (within-task, condition-based contrasts) suitable as decision-making contrasts (I5 satisfied). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (including whole-brain checks and NeuroVault deposition), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I6 satisfied). Participant groups include patients and healthy controls (I7 satisfied). Whole-brain results are reported in text/figures and made available online (I8 satisfied). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not only task>rest, whole-brain maps present, not only connectivity/ROI). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reward-learning task (Salience Attribution Test) that manipulates reward probability (high vs low) and includes ambiguous 50% probability conditions. It reports within-task condition contrasts (adaptive reward prediction: high-probability cues > low-probability cues; aberrant reward prediction: subjective high > low on task-irrelevant 50% cues) and random-effects, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected results and stereotactic coordinates. The task therefore probes decision-making under risk/uncertainty and ambiguity, the contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not baseline), and whole-brain group maps are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI during passive viewing of food images (fattening vs. non-fattening) and an ad libitum eating paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and E6 (analyses are ROI-focused with no reported whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participants; healthy adult sample qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), I6 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; results are ROI-based). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making task (50/50 monetary gambles), meeting the review topic. The study reports within-task contrasts (gain > loss and neural loss aversion parametric contrasts) and performs group-level random-effects SPM8 analyses with whole-brain voxelwise results reported as MNI coordinates and tables. Both within-group (shared gain>loss activations across groups) and between-group NLA contrasts are presented. The task is a risky DM paradigm, not a baseline-only contrast, and whole-brain maps (reported via coordinate tables and figures) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports a human fMRI experiment in which participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task manipulating reward probabilities (HP 90% vs LP 75%), i.e., decision-making under uncertainty. The paper includes within-task and between-condition (HP vs LP) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., REVERR − ALLPOS within conditions and paired t tests comparing HP vs LP; parametric prediction-error regressors and HP–LP comparisons). These contrasts directly map onto an ambiguity/uncertainty comparison (high uncertainty [LP] vs low uncertainty [HP]) and therefore satisfy the meta-analysis contrast requirements. Whole-brain results are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds. Participants are healthy human volunteers. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task outside risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM, baseline-only contrasts) apply.

This study reports human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making (trajectory prediction go/no-go) task and provides within-task contrasts that index perceptual difficulty (fast > medium stimuli, analogous to hard>easy). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using FSL with third-level mixed-effects (FLAME1+2) and results are reported as Z maps/clusters in text/tables (i.e., whole-brain evidence). Participants are human (healthy and expert athletes), which is acceptable. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral and fMRI), Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts, and includes within-task contrasts). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in human participants (n=22) using a perceptual decision-making task (trajectory endpoint estimation) with parametrically manipulated stimulus noise/precision (hard vs easy perceptual conditions). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, cluster-corrected Z-maps) linking brain activity to trial-wise perceptual precision, statistical-model precision, accuracy, and disparity measures. These constitute within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of decision difficulty/precision akin to hard>easy or low coherence>high coherence) and thus meet the required decision-making contrast criterion. The manuscript contains full Methods, Results, and Discussion and clearly reports whole-brain activation maps and tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts of feedback-related activation and cycle-phase interactions, but it does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy) specified by the meta-analysis. Instead, reported contrasts are feedback-based (positive vs negative) and cycle-phase interactions. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrast) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-related task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses), I7 (participant group acceptable — healthy humans), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were directly triggered; exclusion is based on failure to meet all inclusion criteria (I5). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (Social Context Decision Task) during scanning. The authors report within-task condition contrasts that compare risky versus neutral outcomes (e.g., Regret [risky negative outcome] > Disappointment [neutral negative outcome]) and other decision-related contrasts (Regret>Relief, Relief>Elation, Disappointment>Elation), which serve as condition-versus-condition task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise GLM results with clusters reported in the text/tables and ROI time series derived from significant whole-brain peaks. Participants are healthy human subjects (late adolescents and young adults). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning (gambling-like) task but the reported contrasts are reward > punishment, punishment > reward, and final reversal error > baseline. None of the contrasts correspond to the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy) required by inclusion criterion I5. The paper does provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates/tables, and it clearly describes the task and methods. However, because it lacks an eligible decision-making contrast quantifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, it does not meet I5 and is therefore excluded.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task involving uncertainty/probabilistic outcomes (i.e., risky decision context). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted: RPE-related parametric modulators were tested with one-sample and two-sample t-tests and whole-brain cluster- and peak-level FWE-corrected results (RPE network) are reported. The paper does not rely solely on ROI analyses and includes within-group task effects in healthy controls and patient subgroups. Although the task is framed as reinforcement/reversal learning rather than explicitly labelled “risky” or “ambiguous,” the probabilistic (80/20) choice structure entails risk/uncertainty and qualifies under the review’s risky/ambiguous decision-making domain. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in humans that directly investigates perceptual decision-making using ambiguous and unambiguous trials, meeting the review scope. It reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (FWE-corrected results) and model-based parametric contrasts relating trial-by-trial prediction variables to BOLD activity. The design includes within-task contrasts and parametric modulators that assess perceptual decision processes (e.g., conditional probabilities, prediction errors) and separate modeling of ambiguous vs. unambiguous trials for ROI definitions, which fulfill the requirement for a decision-related contrast (ambiguous/perceptual decision conditions vs. others) rather than only task>baseline. Participants are healthy adults. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

(a) Exclusion met: E5 — the task is semantic matching (language/semantic decisions), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the meta-analysis. (b) Inclusion met: I5 — contains decision-making vs active control contrast (semantic > perceptual matching); I6 — reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses (SPM maps) and coordinates; I7 — participant group acceptable (healthy adults); I8 — whole-brain results and coordinates are described. (c) Inclusion not met: I4 — the scanned task is NOT a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (it is semantic/language decision-making). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because the decision-making domain is outside the meta-analysis scope.

While this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level analyses and a clear decision-making contrast (Chosen vs Specified), the task probes voluntary action selection / internal choice between motor responses rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task decision contrast present), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), I8 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criterion I4 (task is risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) is NOT met. Therefore the study is excluded under E5 (task not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete.

This peer-reviewed fMRI study acquired whole-brain BOLD data while participants performed a speeded shooting decision task under threat of shock (high vs low threat), a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing high vs low threat (risk > safe) during preparation and draw-locked analyses, and shoot vs withhold contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are reported (FWE-corrected peaks; coordinates and SI tables referenced). Participants include healthy civilians and police recruits. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

Full text is complete. This study used fMRI during a number-selection (stimulus–stimulus association and selection-conflict) task and reports group-level, whole-brain activation maps and within-task contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analysis reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable: healthy adults and patient sample), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguity/uncertainty, or canonical perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review — it probes associative learning and selection/conflict rather than risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty), I5 (contrasts do not correspond to the review’s accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Therefore exclude because the experimental paradigm does not match the meta-analysis target decision-making domains (risky, ambiguous, perceptual).

This fMRI study used human participants performing a perceptual task (2IFC orientation detection) and healthy subjects, so inclusion criteria I4 and I7 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report any eligible decision-making contrast (e.g., hard>easy or perceptual task>control) for voxelwise task activation — the main fMRI analyses focus on MVPA/ROI-based decoding of spontaneous (rest) reactivation and retinotopically defined ROI results rather than condition-versus-condition task contrasts (I5 not met). Crucially, the study does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map; analyses are ROI-based (retinotopic and anatomical ROIs) and MVPA, so I6 is not met and exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results) applies. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (visual object categorization) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; degraded > intact; interactions of congruency and sensory reliability) and trial-specific RT regressors. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses are reported (voxelwise results with cluster correction). Participants were healthy human volunteers. Results and contrasts are reported in the main text and tables. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans using a risky decision-making gambling task with variable winning probabilities (meets I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts (decision-for-self vs decision-for-other and vice versa) and parametric modulation contrasts of value models, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts (meets I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses are described and whole-brain contrast maps/coordinates are reported (with supplementary tables and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I6 and I8). Participants are healthy human adults (meets I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, includes within-group task contrasts).

This study reports fMRI during a sentence–picture verification task (a semantic/verification decision), not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. The reported voxelwise SPM contrasts shown in the paper are task > fixation (implicit baseline) rather than condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrasts required by the review. Therefore it fails the content inclusion requirements for decision-making type and uses baseline contrasts excluded by the review.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is an instruction-based learning/outcome-integration paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level whole-brain contrast maps were computed), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates described). Inclusion not met: I4 (the task is not a decision-making task under risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty), I5 (no appropriate decision-making contrast such as ambiguous > non-ambiguous or risky > safe was reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study used human participants (n≈27) performing a perceptual categorization task with parametrically varied uncertainty (entropy levels 3, 7, 8.5 bits/dot), directly manipulating perceptual decision difficulty (hard > easy). The analyses include contrasts assessing increasing activation with categorization uncertainty (parametric modulation/high uncertainty > low uncertainty), training-related contrasts (untrained > trained), and feedback-valence contrasts. Imaging was whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with FDR correction; results are reported in tables/figures with coordinates. Thus it meets: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts reflecting uncertainty/hard>easy), I6 (group whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI collected while participants performed a modified trust game that explicitly manipulated risk (high =65% vs low =35% detection probability) and examined decision-making (cheating vs benevolent choices) across risk levels. The paper includes within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., low-risk cheating > benevolent; comparisons of low vs high risk; composite risk-adaptive contrasts) reported as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinate data and thresholds and also reports SVC ROI results. Participant groups (MDD and controls) are acceptable per eligibility. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no E3–E9 apply).

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with whole-brain, group-level analyses and reported coordinates, but it does not report any of the decision-making contrasts required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, high uncertainty > low uncertainty, or hard > easy). The reported fMRI contrasts are feedback-related (negative vs. positive feedback) and parametric prediction-error correlations, rather than contrasts that directly compare decision conditions (risk vs. safety or high vs. low ambiguity/difficulty). Therefore criterion I5 is not met, although I4, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered and the full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examined perceptual decisions about grating orientation and used fMRI during task performance (meets I4). However, the reported analyses focus on ROI-based MVPA and regressions within retinotopically-defined visual areas (V1–V3) and do not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or standard task contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, low-coherence>high-coherence) required by the meta-analysis. The paper therefore fails to meet I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast reported) and I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise task maps); because only ROI analyses are reported with no whole-brain results, it falls under exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete. Consequently the study must be excluded.

This study uses fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement learning task (60% vs 40% reward contingencies) and reports whole-brain RPE (reward prediction error) activation maps. However, it does not present any of the decision-making contrasts required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty; or equivalent ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Instead, the reported contrasts focus on outcome-related RPE signals (win RPE, loss RPE) and emotional (versus neutral) modulations, not explicit risky-versus-safe or uncertainty-based choice contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrast form) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (task is not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast for the meta). The full text is complete and provides whole-brain group maps, so other inclusion criteria (I4, I6, I7, I8) are met.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I4. Although it is an fMRI study with a within-task contrast against an active control (PCLT > PMCT; meets I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (meets I6), involves human participants (meets I7), and provides whole-brain results described in the text (meets I8), the task used (Probabilistic Category Learning Task / Weather Prediction Task) is a category-learning feedback task and is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which human participants performed a lottery task manipulating outcome uncertainty and expected value. It tests neural responses to uncertainty (OU) and includes contrasts/parametric tests equivalent to “high uncertainty > low uncertainty” during curiosity induction and condition comparisons at outcome (Curiosity Relief–Yes > Curiosity Relief–No). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinate tables reported. Participants were healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous task), I5 (within-task contrasts reflecting uncertainty/risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

Although this study used fMRI in human participants on a gambling task (risky context) and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts, it does not present a qualifying decision-making contrast as required (I5). The primary reported contrasts are outcome-based (wins > non-wins; near-miss > full-miss; interaction of near-miss by personal control) rather than contrasts comparing decision options by risk or ambiguity (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, or hard > easy). The selection-phase (participant-chosen vs computer-chosen) is not an explicit risky vs safe or ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrast. Therefore I5 is not met, so the study must be excluded. Exclusion criteria: none met. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is a task fMRI study of value-based decision-making in adults with ADHD (I4 satisfied). The paper includes within-task comparisons (e.g., difficulty/hard>easy-like regressor, trial accuracy) and reports results in text and supplemental tables (I5 and I8 satisfied). Participants and groups are acceptable (I7 satisfied). However, the report centers on ICA-based component/time-series analyses, node variances, and network (edge) connectivity and presents voxel-wise within-node connectivity maps derived from component spatial maps. It does not provide unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, hard>easy) in the conventional sense required by the meta-analysis. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. This matches exclusion criterion E7 (studies reporting only connectivity/ICA-focused results without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps). Because not all inclusion criteria are met (I6 missing), the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in human adults implementing a perceptual decision-making task (nonsymbolic numerosity comparison) with an active, matched control task (brightness comparison). The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise ANOVA and parametric contrasts (cluster-corrected), and reports task > control and task-by-difficulty interaction effects identifying rIFG. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) during scanning (I4). The analysis includes within-task parametric modulators related to motion coherence (absolute coherence) and decision difficulty/value-related regressors (bias, RPE), which satisfy the required form of perceptual decision contrasts (e.g., low coherence > high coherence / hard > easy) and other within-task comparisons (I5). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster-corrected) for these regressors and contrasts (I6), and participants are healthy young adults (I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described and visualized (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (model-based prediction-error regressors) and includes eligible participant groups, the experimental task is a probabilistic reversal-learning reinforcement task focused on reward prediction errors rather than explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. The paper does not present any of the required decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4 (task is not one of risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast). It does satisfy I6 (whole-brain maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (results clearly reported). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reinforcement learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (satisfying I4, I6, I7, and I8). However, it does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts comparing two decision-making conditions as specified in I5 (e.g., high uncertainty > low uncertainty, risky > safe, hard > easy). The imaging results focus on parametric learning-related effects, stimulus vs feedback epochs, and between-group differences rather than explicit within-task contrasts between uncertainty/risk levels; therefore the study’s reported task activations appear to be contrasts against baseline/epochs and group comparisons rather than the condition-versus-condition contrasts required. This places the study into exclusion under E3 (only decision-making contrasts against implicit baseline/task epochs rather than condition-vs-condition contrasts) and fails I5. Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E3.

The study used fMRI in human subjects performing a foraging-style stay vs leave task that probes reward-trend-guided value-based choice. While it reports whole-brain group analyses and explicit stay>leave contrasts, the task is not a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review (e.g., risky vs safe, ambiguity vs non-ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty/coherence contrasts). Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion requirement I4 (task must be risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) and thus should be excluded under E5. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (contains a decision contrast: stay vs leave), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy humans), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Not met: I4 (task is foraging/value-based, not clearly risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task not in risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM categories). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI during a perceptual task (texture discrimination) and reports whole-brain task-evoked activation, but it does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast of the forms required (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence, perceptual task > active control). The fMRI analyses derive and compare task-induced activation maps (averaged across conditions) and report group differences and pre/post session effects; the reported effects appear to be task > implicit baseline and between-group differences rather than a within-task condition contrast or task > active control contrast. Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (only contrasts against implicit baseline/task activity) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition contrast).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a risky instrumental decision-making task (Go/NoGo with monetary wins/losses). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reward vs neutral, punishment vs neutral), model-based regressors (Q values, prediction errors), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with family-wise error correction using SPM5. Results include voxelwise activations, time courses, and correlations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core content is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It uses fMRI during an olfactory intensity-rating task combined with a memory (cognitive load) manipulation. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), I7 (healthy adult participants qualify), and I8 (whole-brain results and cluster/coordinate information are described). Not met inclusion criteria: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task performed during fMRI) and I5 (no decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete and sufficient to determine eligibility.

This study collected fMRI during a risky decision-making task (shell-game style) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and healthy adult participants, and reports whole-brain results in text and figures. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported). However, the reported fMRI contrasts are parametric effects against implicit baseline (e.g., RP > 0, LP > 0, RPE > 0, LPE > 0) rather than condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk, risky > safe). Because the study’s decision-making contrasts are against implicit baseline only, it meets exclusion criterion E3 and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5. Thus it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study acquired BOLD data while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task. The paper reports within-task, parametric contrasts across risk levels (i.e., activation associated with increasing pump/risk levels) and examines whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (within-group effects and group comparisons are described). Participants are human (healthy MBA students). Results are reported in the main text with methods, results, and discussion present (full text appears complete). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6) and also meets participant and reporting acceptability (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans performing a mirror-reading lexical decision task (mirror vs normal) that manipulates perceptual difficulty and measures task-evoked whole-brain activation. The key contrast (mirror > normal) compares two task conditions (perceptual-hard > perceptual-easy) and therefore qualifies as a perceptual decision-making contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with peak coordinates reported. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (not a PET study, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (detecting short vs long digit sequences with implicit cues) manipulating uncertainty; it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing conditions (e.g., high vs low uncertainty checkpoints) and prediction-error contrasts (TERM>EXT, CHECK_HIGH>CHECK_LOW), with thresholding and cluster correction. Behavioral and fMRI methods, results and discussion are present in full text. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task of perceptual nature), I5 (condition contrasts such as CHECK_HIGH>CHECK_LOW, TERM>EXT), I6 (group whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria met: E3-E9 not applicable. Full text appears complete.

The study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task and reports whole-brain fMRI contrasts (e.g., final reversal errors vs perseverative errors; correct vs incorrect; perseverative vs probabilistic errors). However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (no risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy contrasts). Therefore it fails the key task-related inclusion criteria. Exclusion ID: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable: healthy, substance users), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast such as risky>safe or hard>easy). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which adolescents performed a risky decision-making lottery choice task during scanning. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses relating a parametric measure of risk (coefficient of variation; high-risk > low-risk contrast via parametric modulation) to BOLD responses, with cluster-level FWE correction. Results (whole-brain and ROI eigenvariates) are described in the text and supplements. Participants are a human sample (adolescents). Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The study used simultaneous EEG-fMRI during a two-choice gambling (risky) task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. However, the reported contrasts focus on feedback valence (gain > loss) and outcome magnitude (large > small) rather than a decision-phase contrast comparing risky vs safe or high-risk vs low-risk (e.g., choice-based 'high-risk > low-risk' or 'risk > certainty'). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in human participants using a probabilistic monetary-incentive delay task that systematically manipulated outcome probability (20%, 50%, 80%) and magnitude. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing high- versus low-probability anticipation (PRB: 80 vs 20%) and other decision-related contrasts, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach coordinates. These features satisfy the review’s requirements for (I4) an fMRI task involving probabilistic (risky) decision-related processing, (I5) at least one decision-related within-task contrast (high vs low probability), (I6) group-level whole-brain results, (I7) an acceptable participant group (healthy humans), and (I8) reporting of whole-brain results with coordinates and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/place discrimination with parametrically varied sensory evidence), satisfying I4. The authors report condition comparisons across levels of sensory evidence (e.g., 100% vs 50% evidence; hard > easy equivalents) and analyses of ambiguous trials, meeting I5. They performed voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analyses with multiple-comparison corrected z maps (voxel-wise ANOVA and whole-brain maps), meeting I6 and I8. Participants are healthy human adults (group-level within-subject contrasts reported), so I7 is met. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and is an empirical fMRI activation study. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans (n=17) that directly examines risky decision making (choices between learned and described win probabilities). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing learned versus described value (LV vs DV) and learned-risk versus described-risk (LR vs DR), with group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (whole-brain cluster-corrected and FWE-SVC p-values are reported) and ROI checks; results are presented as voxelwise activation maps in the text/figures. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete for screening (methods/task description, results, discussion present).

The study used fMRI but the task is a voluntary mental-imagery choice paradigm (choosing which grating to imagine). This does not constitute a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence, risk>safe). Accordingly, required inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and I5 (at least one accepted decision-making contrast) are not met. The manuscript does report group-level whole-brain searchlight decoding maps (satisfying I6), includes acceptable participant groups (I7), and reports coordinates/figures (I8). Because the task falls outside the targeted decision domains, the study is excluded under E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM).

This study is excluded because its task (Monetary Incentive Delay Task) probes reward anticipation and receipt rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps and whole-brain analyses are reported), I7 (participant groups are acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results are described in the text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI was not performed during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no decision-making contrasts of the form risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy; contrasts are gain vs nongain reward contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study directly examines perceptual decision-making: participants made forced-choice /aba/ vs /ada/ judgments of ambiguous speech (perceptual DM). The authors ran GLMs labeling trials by participant percept (/aba/ vs /ada/) and report group-level whole-brain functional contrast maps (post-test trials > baseline; exposure blocks > baseline) and a group PPI map; thus task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise/surface analyses were performed even though the univariate /aba/ vs /ada/ contrast yielded no significant clusters. Multivariate decoding was additionally applied within STC. The design includes within-task comparisons of decision outcomes (perceptual labels), meeting the requirement for a decision-related contrast. Participants are healthy human adults. Results are reported in full-text figures and analyses. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task decision contrast: /aba/ vs /ada/ perceptions), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), I7 (human participant group qualifies), and I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses human fMRI during a risky decision-making sequential investment task and reports group-level GLM maps of parametric decision-related regressors (signed TD, unsigned TD, fictive errors), but functional acquisition was restricted to a brainstem-centered slab (not whole-brain). The meta-analysis requires group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (I6). This study therefore does not meet I6 (no whole-brain coverage) and must be excluded. It does meet I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task parametric contrasts relating decision variables to BOLD), and I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants performed the Eriksen flanker (a perceptual/conflict decision) task and the authors report within-task contrasts (incongruent > congruent) that map onto perceptual-DM contrasts (hard > easy). They performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM12 with FWE-corrected results reported in tables/figures and conducted ROI follow-ups. Participant groups (schizophrenia and healthy controls) are acceptable per criteria. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a slot-machine decision-making task where participants make choices under hidden/probabilistic outcome distributions (i.e., uncertainty/ambiguity) and also observe agents—constituting decision-making under uncertainty. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM results (value and update/entropy regressors, chosen-value contrasts, and condition comparisons such as similar vs dissimilar) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides activation coordinates and NeuroVault maps. Thus it meets: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (within-task condition comparisons — similar vs dissimilar and task-related parametric contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (no only-baseline contrasts, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or only between-group contrasts).

The study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps. However, the primary reported neural contrasts are stop (safe) decisions relative to an implicit baseline (driving time between stoplights). The review’s eligible contrasts require condition-versus-condition or task-versus-control-task comparisons (e.g., risky > safe); the study does not report such decision-vs-decision or decision-vs-active-control contrasts. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only contrasts versus implicit baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (acceptable participant group: adolescents), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast such as risky>safe). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study investigates social cooperation games (prisoner’s dilemma vs stag hunt) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social/moral decision-making, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results reported), I7 (human participant group), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task per review definitions) and I5 (contrast is PD vs SH, not an accepted risky/ambiguity/perceptual contrast such as “risky>safe” or “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic reversal learning (reward-guided) decision-making task with uncertain probabilistic outcomes. It reports within-task contrasts (exploratory vs exploitative trials; model-based prediction-error regressors PEDU/PESU) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates). The task involves probabilistic reward contingencies (80/20) and adaptive decision-making under uncertainty, fitting the review’s risky/ambiguous decision-making domain. therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely solely on implicit baseline contrasts, is not PET, reports whole-brain task activations (not ROI-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It uses an fMRI speech-production task with a Rest–Speech contrast to examine default network deactivations and correlations with psychopathic personality traits. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task contrast was reported for Rest–Speech), I7 (human healthy participants), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making contrast of the types required, e.g., risky>safe or hard>easy). Full text appears complete and contains intro, methods, results, and discussion; therefore excluded because it does not address the review’s target decision-making paradigms.

This is an fMRI study of social/economic (Trust Game) decision-making focused on fairness and Machiavellianism. Although it reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (Fair–Control, Unfair–Control) and provides voxelwise results, the task is social/moral/economic (trust/reciprocity) rather than a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm targeted by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM — e.g., moral or social decision-making) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task vs active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which 24 healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (choose gamble vs guaranteed $10) while being scanned. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) showing neural correlates of decision risk (parametric modulation of gamble variance) and other decision variables. The key contrast is a trial-by-trial parametric effect of risk (i.e., high-risk > low-risk type effect) at the time of decision, reported as whole-brain maps and peak coordinates (Tables S1, S3). Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in whole-brain activation tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only, and not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI Methods). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between risky gambles and sure bets), with explicit contrasts of Risky Bet > Sure Bet (i.e., risk > certainty). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses are described (mixed-effects, cluster correction, tables of peak coordinates and figures), and ROI analyses supplement but do not replace whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI with a naturalistic risky decision (landing in fog) and included an active control (ILS approach without decision), but the reported analyses focus on ROI/small-volume results (bilateral caudate and other ROIs) and do not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (decision > active control/task contrast), I7 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain voxelwise task map reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6. Hence EXCLUDED.

This study used a delay-discounting (intertemporal) task rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task, therefore failing the primary domain requirement for inclusion (exclusion E5). Additionally, the reported analyses focus on region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with small-volume correction rather than reporting an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group map, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study contains within-task contrasts, e.g., immediate 'Today' trials vs. other decisions) and I7 (participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making) and I6 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise group activation map reported). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Given E5 (task domain) alone is sufficient for exclusion, the paper should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the task is a reinforcement-learning reward-guided decision-making task with probabilistic feedback and reversals, not a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review (e.g., no explicit risky>safe or ambiguity contrasts). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable — includes substance users and controls), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are reported/clearly described). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task does not clearly qualify as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making for this meta-analysis), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI during an olfactory self-preference task (exposure to 'self' vs 'non-self' MHC peptides and solvent) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criterion met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses were performed and reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy were presented). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used a visual food perception paradigm (Food > Non-Food) in healthy participants and reports group-level task effects. However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making: the task is passive viewing with attention targets and tastiness ratings, not a risky/ambiguous choice or a perceptual decision manipulation (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level task-evoked analysis/second-level random-effects contrasts were generated and whole-brain effects are reported/supplemented), I7 (participant group acceptable: healthy adults), and I8 (results reported in text/figures/supplement). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Hence the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human subjects performing a probabilistic reversal learning task in which choices lead to monetary outcomes with known probabilities (70%/30%), i.e., decisions under risk. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM random-effects analyses and contrasts comparing decision-making (choice) versus a non-choice imperative control, as well as contrasts isolating response maintenance vs switching and reward vs punishment; results are presented in figures and tables with coordinates. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (decision-making task > control contrast: choice > imperative, and within-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided).

This is an fMRI study in humans that manipulated sexual risk (high vs low) while participants made decisions about likelihood of having sex, constituting a risky decision-making task. The study reports a within-task contrast comparing risk conditions (low > high), performs a group-level whole-brain SPM analysis with voxelwise results and Talairach coordinates, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Participants are healthy adult women. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) fMRI during a risky decision-making task, (I5) at least one decision-condition contrast (high vs low risk), (I6) whole-brain group-level statistical maps reported, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) whole-brain results reported in text/tables. The full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, not non-empirical). The contrast direction (low>high) still represents a valid within-task risk condition comparison and is eligible for inclusion.

This fMRI study used a human sample performing a gambling task with explicitly shown probabilities (30% and 70%) and varying outcome magnitudes (€1 vs €5), i.e., a risky decision-making paradigm. The study reports within-task contrasts (EV+ coding, €5 vs €1 magnitude, 70% vs 30% probability) computed at the subject level and entered into group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses; peak coordinates and voxelwise results (with small-volume correction within anatomically defined ROIs) are reported. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported via coordinates/thresholded maps), I7 (allowed participant groups), and I8 (coordinates/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only without whole-brain voxelwise analysis, not resting-state/connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making task under probabilistic uncertainty (subjects infer reward probabilities that drift across trials), meeting the review’s domain (risky/ambiguous decision-making). The authors report within-task parametric contrasts (e.g., relative unchosen probability; relative chosen value) and use whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with reported MNI coordinates and cluster correction. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, fMRI acquisition and GLMs), Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task vs baseline only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a two-alternative forced-choice tactile perceptual discrimination (distinguishing parallelepipeds by oblongness). The manuscript reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g. P2a [suprathreshold/distinguishable] vs P2b [subthreshold/indistinguishable], and task phases vs recovery), which constitute perceptual decision-making contrasts (analogous to hard>easy or perceptual task>control). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 are presented (categorical contrasts with reported activation maps/coordinates). Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E9).

This study is excluded because its decision-making task is social (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is social decision-making, which is outside the review scope). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI was conducted while human participants performed a decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM and cluster-corrected maps were reported), I7 (participant sample is acceptable — healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results are described and depicted in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the contrasts reported — e.g., cooperate > defect, cooperation vs defect, SVO interactions — are social decision contrasts and do not match the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types required for the meta-analysis). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (Gabor detection) with asymmetric payoffs. The authors report group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (FDR/voxelwise thresholds) and provide peak coordinates and cluster results. The paper includes condition contrasts and parametric regressors relevant to decision-making (e.g., momentary evidence/contrast, decision-variable regressor, and comparisons across bias conditions: liberal > neutral > conservative), satisfying the requirement for decision-making contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral, modeling, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing), Results (behavioral, model comparison, whole-brain imaging), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task analyses of a social learning/advice-taking task (satisfies I4, I6, I7, I8). However, the task centers on social decision-making (inferring adviser fidelity and integrating social advice with probabilistic cues) rather than a pure risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as defined by the meta-analysis. The review’s exclusion criterion E5 disallows studies whose decision-making task is social (e.g., social learning, advice/gambling framed by social motives). Furthermore, the reported contrasts are model-based social prediction errors and adviser-fidelity/integration effects rather than the domain-specific contrasts required for inclusion (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore I5 (required contrast type for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) is not met and E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study does not investigate one of the target decision-making domains (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) in the way required by the review. Although it uses fMRI in humans (and reports whole-brain searchlight RSA) and involves choices about probabilistic inferences, the task is an inference-about-latent-causes paradigm and the neuroimaging analyses are representational-similarity/model-fitting (RSA) rather than standard condition-vs-condition task contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria requiring a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task contrast (I4, I5) and the requirement for a group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrast map as the target (I6). Included: I7 (participant group acceptable). Excluded criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face-based yes/no decisions), satisfying the review’s focus on perceptual DM. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., switch vs. stay trials) and other condition-wise comparisons, and presents univariate GLM results (group-level t-maps/contrasts) and whole-brain analyses (figures and statistical maps described), meeting the requirement for condition-versus-condition contrasts and whole-brain task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not a review. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination) with event-related GLMs and within-task contrasts (e.g., valid vs invalid cue conditions) that probe decision-related activity. The paper reports group-level voxelwise GLMs and refers to whole-brain cue and stimulus effects in the Supplementary Figures/Tables, and also presents ROI analyses; contrasts are condition-vs-condition rather than task>rest. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (I4), contains within-task decision contrasts (I5), includes group-level whole-brain results (I6) (reported in supplement), uses an eligible participant sample (I7), and reports whole-brain results in acceptable formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that manipulated response predictability (50% vs 100%) to dissociate anticipatory (high predictability/low uncertainty) and mnemonic (low predictability/high uncertainty) decision-making strategies. The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with tables/figures of activations and direct within-task contrasts (anticipatory > mnemonic and vice versa) and between-group comparisons. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for an fMRI study of decision-making under uncertainty with whole-brain group maps and condition-vs-condition contrasts.

This study does not meet the review’s task-type inclusion requirements. Although it reports group-level whole-brain fMRI results (I6) and includes eligible participant groups (I7) and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results (I8), the experimental paradigm is a probabilistic social reinforcement learning task (social reward learning) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. The paper does not report contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) or within-task risk/ambiguity contrasts; instead analyses focus on reinforcement learning (trial-wise RPE parametric modulation) and social vs non-social feedback. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (task not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Included criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of reward receipt/success vs failure rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Although outcomes were probabilistic, the paradigm does not involve choice under risk or ambiguity nor classic perceptual difficulty manipulations; contrasts focus on successes vs failures and stimulus-type interactions rather than decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level SPM results. Therefore it fails the review inclusion criteria requiring a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (I4) and a qualifying decision-making contrast (I5), and meets exclusion criterion E5 (task not risky/ambiguous/perceptual). It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Full text appears complete.

The study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. It uses the Monetary Incentive Delay task (reward anticipation/receipt) and a Probabilistic Selection (reinforcement learning) task, which probe reward processing and reinforcement learning rather than decisions under risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty. Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria requiring an fMRI task of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and the prespecified contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). The full text is complete and reports group-level fMRI ROI and PPI connectivity analyses, but these do not fulfill the required decision-making contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task type), I5 (required decision-making contrasts), I6 (whole-brain task-activation map for the decision-making contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (gambles varying in probability and amount). The study reports within-task contrasts (three-option vs two-option; targets vs competitors; decision-phase contrasts) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported coordinates and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and whole-brain activation results), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This fMRI study examines how expert reviewers’ opinions alter subjective value of songs (social influence on reward/valuation). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinate tables and healthy participants. However, the task is social valuation/reward receipt and does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Contrasts reported concern object reward, agreement vs disagreement with reviewers, and social influence on value—not the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 (task type) and I5 (required decision-making contrasts) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a forced-choice categorization task (valence classification of faces) during scanning. The task constitutes a perceptual decision-making paradigm with manipulated difficulty via congruent vs. incongruent background colors; the primary reported contrasts are condition-versus-condition (e.g., incongruent > congruent) within emotional categories. Group-level, whole-brain (SPM2) voxelwise analyses are reported with tables of coordinates, conjunction and interaction analyses, and ROI/PSC follow-ups. Participants (n=20) are an eligible human sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E9).

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) task, a decision-making paradigm involving choices under probabilistic uncertainty (risk). It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., lose-shift vs. win-stay; lose-stay vs. win-stay; lose-shift vs. lose-stay) that index decision processes and feedback-driven choice, satisfying the requirement for a contrast between decision-making conditions.
