Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistics (Monte Carlo-corrected thresholds) and report whole-brain results and ROI correlations. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and controls) are acceptable per inclusion rules. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., task>rest only, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a gambling/guessing task that manipulates reward probability and magnitude (risky decision making). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and corrected statistical maps, and includes contrasts directly comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., high vs low probability; gain > loss; EV+ vs EV− prediction/prediction-error contrasts). Thus it fulfills the review’s requirements for (i) fMRI during a risky DM task, (ii) condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making, (iii) whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, and (iv) acceptable participant sample (healthy adults). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the study only reports a decision-stage > baseline (implicit baseline) contrast rather than a condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast. Exclusion ID met: E3. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI acquired while human participants performed a decision-making task—the Iowa Gambling Task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction), I7 (healthy human participants qualify), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy, or task>active-control contrasts provided). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study does not meet the review’s core task inclusion requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the fMRI task is a monetary reward anticipation (monetary incentive delay) assessing reward sensitivity/anticipation and cue extinction effects, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 — a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported; I7 — human participant sample (patients with AUD) is acceptable; I8 — whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/supplement. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 — the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task; I5 — no contrast matches the allowed decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study does not meet the review’s task-domain inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the fMRI task is a working-memory n-back paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and maps are reported), I7 (human participant sample within acceptable ages; healthy adults from HCP), I8 (whole-brain results and ROI selection are clearly described in the text and methods). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI was not performed during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making, e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; contrasts are 2-back vs 0-back or task vs fixation which index working memory load, not decision-making under risk/ambiguity/perception). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present): fulltext_incomplete=false.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment (n=26) in which participants made choices between certain and risky monetary options, satisfying the risky decision-making domain. The authors performed group-level, voxelwise fMRI analyses (random-effects, voxel-wise threshold P<0.001, cluster-level small-volume correction) and report coordinates and parametric contrasts linking option/outcome-related signals (EVs, RPEs, CRs) to BOLD activity in ventral striatum and insula. These constitute within-task decision-making contrasts (e.g., gamble vs certain/parametric modulators related to risk and reward expectation) and provide whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study includes a probabilistic (risky) decision-making task conducted during fMRI and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (parametric SV maps and task contrasts), fulfilling the meta-analysis requirements. Specifically, (1) participants performed a probability/risk decision task while scanned (I4); (2) the paper reports within-task and between-task comparisons (parametric modulation of subjective value and paired t-tests comparing tasks), providing usable contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (I5); (3) analyses are whole-brain voxelwise with cluster correction and unthresholded maps available (I6); (4) participant group (healthy adults across adulthood) is acceptable for inclusion (I7); and (5) whole-brain results are reported in figures/maps and made available online (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not resting/ connectivity-only (E7), and does include appropriate condition-vs-condition and parametric task effects (not only task>baseline) so E3 is not triggered. Note: although the paper also reports effort and temporal discounting tasks (domains excluded if considered alone), the presence of a well-characterized probability/risky decision task with whole-brain maps supports inclusion for a meta-analysis of risky decision-making.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy humans performing a monetary gambling task that manipulates risk. It includes within-task condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., high-risk wins > low-risk wins; a risk-choice contrast modeling linear increase with risk magnitude), satisfying the required risky-DM contrast forms. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain (SPM8 second-level ANOVAs) with reported whole-brain clusters and ROI-corrected results, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are healthy adults. Results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not only baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), task is a risky decision-making paradigm (not excluded DM types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the paper reports task activations rather than only connectivity or between-group-only contrasts. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This fMRI study (BART during scan) meets I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported) and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/text). However, it does not present a qualifying condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast as required by I5. The reported analyses appear to be condition > implicit baseline contrasts (e.g., pumps/cash-outs modeled against the implicit baseline) and age regressions on these condition maps; there is no clear “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “pump > cash-out”, or other within-task risky-vs-safe or task-vs-control contrast presented. Because the study’s decision-making contrasts are only against an implicit baseline, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I exclude the study from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs. house categorization) inside the scanner, reporting group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps (face+house > rest; face > house; house > face) and ROI analyses. The study includes within-task condition contrasts (face vs. house) and analyses of difficulty/noise, and reports group-level voxelwise results in figures/tables. Thus it meets: I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (within-task condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an fMRI study of a perceptual estimation task (dot counts) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinate tables, it does not provide the required decision-making contrasts for perceptual DM specified by the meta-analysis (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence, or perceptual task > control task). The reported contrasts focus on social conformity (Conformity to In-group > Non-Conformity to In-group; Conformity to Out-group > Non-Conformity to Out-group) rather than perceptual-difficulty or task-versus-control contrasts. Thus I4, I6, I7, and I8 are met, but I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

This fMRI study tested PD patients performing a probabilistic roulette task with explicit risk manipulations (0.25 vs 0.75 win probabilities and $1 vs $5 stakes), i.e., a risky decision-making paradigm. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses: (a) outcome-induced BOLD changes and (b) trial-by-trial parametric modulation by reward prediction error (RPE) values, entered into repeated-measures ANOVAs. The RPE parametric contrast and categorical analyses of negative vs positive RPE constitute within-task decision-making contrasts relevant to risky DM (not simple task>baseline only). Whole-brain results are reported and thresholded, and coordinates/tables are provided. Participants are a clinical sample (PD), which is allowed. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study includes a probabilistic discounting (PD) task that is a risky decision-making paradigm (choices between sure €20 and probabilistic rewards), and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (parametric subjective-value regressors) with coordinates and statistical maps. The PD analysis provides within-task contrasts (subjective value correlation for probabilistic options) that constitute a decision-making effect appropriate for risky-DM meta-analysis. The full text contains methods, results, and figures/tables documenting whole-brain results (with SVC reported but based on group-level voxelwise maps). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and it includes within-task task effects rather than only baseline contrasts. Although the paper also includes delay-discounting (an excluded task type), the presence of a qualifying risky (probability) task and whole-brain PD contrasts satisfies inclusion. Therefore include.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy human adults performing a risky decision-making task (Card Guessing Game with monetary bets), includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (subject guess vs computer guess; win vs loss; streak effects) and choice-stage SG>CG contrasts, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster-corrected results and stereotaxic coordinates). Results are presented in text, figures, and coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI-only results, only baseline contrasts) are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This study used fMRI in human participants performing an odour detection task (a perceptual task) and reports group-level, voxelwise searchlight MVPA results with coordinates; participants were healthy and whole-brain results are reported. However, it does not include the required decision-making contrasts specified by the review (e.g., perceptual hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>control) nor any within-task contrasts comparing two decision-making conditions of interest. Instead, analyses focus on pre/post-conditioning changes, multivariate pattern classification and connectivity (PPI) related to associative learning and value, not contrasts of perceptual decision difficulty. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one qualifying decision-making contrast) is not met, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The fMRI study includes a non-verbal target-detection Decision task (press for target vs distractor), which constitutes a perceptual decision-making task. The authors report a Decision > (Count + Speech) contrast (i.e., task > active control) and used this contrast to localize domain-general activation. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE cluster-corrected) are reported, with coordinates and figures. Participants include patient and control groups (eligible per I7). Results and whole-brain coordinates are described in text and figures. Therefore the study fulfills the review’s requirements for (I4) fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task, (I5) a decision > control-task contrast, (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps, (I7) acceptable participant groups, and (I8) reporting of whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based whole-brain fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (PRLT) that uses explicit probabilistic feedback (80:20), i.e. decision-making under uncertainty/risk, and includes an affectively neutral active baseline control task. The authors computed within-task contrasts (monetary gain vs baseline, monetary loss vs baseline, reversal vs baseline) and performed group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2, random effects) with whole-brain thresholding and tabulated/figured results. Participants include clinical and control groups. Thus the paper meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (experimental task > active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; contrasts are against active control not implicit baseline; within-group task effects reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Jackpot play/pass with 33% vs 67% probabilities), includes within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices (Play > Pass and Gain/Loss > Pass) and contrasts between contexts (Social vs Monetary Play), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Participants are human and eligible. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This document is a commentary/preview summarizing and discussing Juechems et al. (2017) and related literature, not an original empirical fMRI study. Exclusion criterion met: E9 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none (inclusion_criteria_applied = []). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no original fMRI scan reported on human participants performing a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no reported task contrasts from an original experiment), I6 (no group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or results). Additionally, the provided full text lacks core empirical sections (methods/results), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This study is excluded because the task is primarily social/vicarious reward prediction (self vs other empathy paradigm) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is social decision-making/motivated by empathy rather than a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task). The study does meet several methodological inclusion requirements: I6 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation with FWE-corrected results), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (reports coordinates/figures). However it does not meet I4 (the paradigm is not a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task—participants made expectedness judgments about observed/probabilistic outcomes rather than making risk/ambiguity or perceptual choice decisions) and I5 (it does not provide contrasts that map onto accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because its reported fMRI contrasts are condition-versus-baseline (e.g., wins > baseline, lose/shift > baseline) rather than condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrasts (violates E3). Additionally, the imaging analysis was performed using a region-of-interest approach with no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps reported (violates E6). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant groups are acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm that is not clearly one of the specified risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM tasks as operationalized by the review), I5 (no eligible decision-versus-decision or task-versus-control contrasts presented), I6 (no whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete. Overall confidence in this exclusion decision is high.

This study meets the meta-analysis entry criteria: it acquired fMRI while participants (adolescents) performed the Risky-Gains task (risky decision-making) and reports a risky > safe (risky vs. safe) contrast. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise (SPM8) with correction and reported coordinate results. Participant groups (healthy and excess weight adolescents) are within eligible populations and results include within-group and between-group task activations and contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only) apply.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (healthy human participant sample), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a perceptual decision-making task (judging whether a comparison interval was shorter or longer than a standard), providing whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and clearly described results in the full text, so it meets I4, I6, I7, and I8. However, the reported neuroimaging contrasts and spatial-extent analyses appear to evaluate task activation/time courses and phases relative to a baseline (filler images) and examine ON vs OFF medication and group differences, with no clear within-task condition contrast of decision difficulty (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence) or a task > active control contrast. Therefore the study does not satisfy I5 and instead falls under exclusion E3 (contrasts only vs implicit baseline/rest). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

This is an fMRI study with full methods and whole-brain group analyses, but it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. The tasks are Go/No-go (response inhibition), oddball (target detection), and two-alternative forced-choice response selection manipulating stimulus frequency, not risk/ambiguity or perceptual difficulty (e.g., hard>easy, low>high coherence). Therefore it fails the core inclusion requirements for (I4) (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and (I5) (no eligible decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). The study does satisfy other technical inclusion aspects: group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps were reported (I6), any participant group is acceptable (healthy adults; I7), and whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (I8). Based on exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM), the study should be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study used fMRI during a lexical decision task to investigate emotional word processing, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps were reported), I7 (healthy human participants were tested), and I8 (whole-brain results and cluster coordinates/activations are clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is reading/lexical decision, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm of the types specified) and I5 (no contrasts matching risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or perceptual hard>easy; contrasts are emotional/lexical conditions such as words>pseudowords and valence×arousal). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude from the meta-analysis focused on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses functional MRI while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (I4), reports task contrasts comparing decision conditions including gamble > sure (choice regressor; I5), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with random-effects statistics and whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and stereotactic coordinates (I6, I8), and includes an eligible participant group of healthy adults (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods (task, behavioral modeling, fMRI acquisition and GLM), results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging tables/coordinates), and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (phoneme categorization /ba/ vs /da/) during scanning; searchlight MVPA produced condition-vs-condition (binary) contrasts entered into group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses (voxelwise p<0.001, cluster correction), with results reported in figures and corrected p-values. Thus the study meets I4 (perceptual DM), I5 (within-task condition contrast /ba/ vs /da/), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy participants included), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria E3–E9 apply. Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of saccade countermanding (inhibitory control/performance monitoring), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) and E6 (analysis is ROI-based without a reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map). Inclusion criteria: none apply. Specifically, it does not meet I4 (fMRI during a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (required contrast forms for risk/ambiguity/perceptual DM are not present), or I6 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study used simultaneous fMRI while participants performed a monetary gambling task (inclusion I4 met). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/figures of activations (I6 met) in a healthy adult sample (I7 met) and presents whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8 met). However, the reported primary contrasts are outcome-based (monetary wins vs. losses; FRN, alpha- and theta-informed GLMs examining win>loss), which index reward/outcome processing rather than a decision-making contrast of the forms required for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk, risk>certainty, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). The paper does not present contrasts that directly compare decision-making conditions varying in risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria from the meta-analysis (E3–E9) are directly triggered. Therefore, the study must be excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the fMRI task does not probe risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making: the scanned task was an attentional/conditioned-cue probe (CS+ vs CS−) and the decision-making task (delay discounting) was performed outside the scanner. Therefore this study does not address risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM and fails the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Exclusion ID met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion IDs met: I6 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses), I7 (human participant sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted while participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy was reported for an in-scanner decision task). Given these mismatches, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This paper reports a behavioral study of probabilistic reinforcement learning in adults with ASD and typically developing controls; no fMRI scanning or neuroimaging data were collected or reported. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant groups qualify). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no reported within-task or task>control contrasts from imaging data), I6 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinates). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion, but it lacks any imaging/whole-brain activation results required for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet the core imaging-related inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6).

This study collected simultaneous fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (so I4 satisfied) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (I6). Participants are an eligible sample (healthy adults) (I7), and whole-brain results are described in the text/supplementary figures (I8). However, the paper does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the review (e.g., risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk, ambiguity contrasts, or perceptual hard>easy). Instead, the analyses focus on outcome valence (positive vs negative), EEG-informed parametric regressors, and connectivity (PPI/DCM). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no qualifying decision-condition vs decision-condition or task>control contrasts). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) otherwise apply. Based on these criteria the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of delay-of-gratification / willingness-to-wait (intertemporal persistence), not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM; it is intertemporal/delay discounting). Inclusion criteria that are satisfied: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (participant group acceptable—healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task) and I5 (contrasts are not of the admitted risky/ambiguous/perceptual forms). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (orientation discrimination) with no external feedback. The analyses include within-task condition contrasts (e.g., BOLD comparisons across behavioral confidence tertiles; model-based contrasts of confidence prediction errors and expected confidence), which constitute condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts relevant to perceptual DM. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain t-maps, searchlight cvMANOVA, and coordinates for active clusters) and provides coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy humans. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study used fMRI during monetary incentive delay (MID) and a probabilistic reward (response-bias) task in nonsmokers, with whole-brain, group-level contrasts (Reward Cue–Neutral Cue; Loss Cue–Neutral Cue). However, neither task matches the review’s target decision-making domains. The MID probes anticipation of monetary gains/losses and simple RT performance rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis (eg, risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). The probabilistic reward task is a reward-learning/perceptual discrimination with asymmetric reinforcement but the reported contrasts focus on response bias rather than accepted perceptual-DM contrasts (eg, hard>easy or low vs high coherence). Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5, despite meeting other criteria (whole-brain group maps present). Full text is complete.

Exclusion reason: E5 applies — the task is the Monetary Incentive Delay (MID) task (reward anticipation), which is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses with SPM and FWE cluster correction), I7 (healthy participant group — healthy volunteers included), and I8 (results reported as whole-brain activations/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task — NOT met), and I5 (contrast comparing risky vs safe, ambiguous vs nonambiguous, or perceptual hard vs easy — the reported contrasts are reward magnitude [£5 vs neutral], not qualifying decision-making contrasts). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (full article content including methods, results, discussion provided). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks.

This study does not examine risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. The in-scanner task was passive viewing of “fattening” versus “nonfattening” food images; participants did not perform a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast of the accepted forms) are not met. The paper does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses were conducted), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results and contrasts are clearly described). Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Consequently the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

This fMRI study (N=30) acquired whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps while participants performed perceptual decision tasks (gender identification of faces and shape identification). It reports direct task-vs-task contrasts (e.g., face gender identification > neutral shape identification) and whole-brain second-level analyses (random-effects ANOVA; FWE-corrected results), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. The tasks qualify as perceptual decision-making (choice reaction tasks requiring perceptual discrimination), and the contrasts compare decision-making conditions against an active control task. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state; not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision tasks), I5 (task>control and between-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criteria applied: none.

The study is an fMRI experiment with whole-brain analyses during decision-making (trust and an ambiguous NS control) but its primary task is social (trust) decision-making, which falls outside the meta-analysis scope. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the decision-making task is social/trust rather than a pure risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during human decision-making), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps and whole-brain/exploratory analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (results reported in tables/figures/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the study does not provide a contrast matching the meta-analysis’ required forms for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous, high-risk > low-risk, or hard > easy). Although an ambiguous lottery was used as a control, the critical contrasts focus on social (trust) vs control and on threat effects, not on standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts required by the review. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion: E5 met — the task is an implicit Pavlovian/learning salience paradigm (outcome discrimination with cue-outcome learning and prediction-error modeling), not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps/GLM results with voxelwise FWE and small-volume corrections), I7 (participant group — schizophrenia patients and healthy controls — is acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not performed during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no eligible decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; reported contrasts/parametric modulators concern relevance-weighted prediction errors and group comparisons, not the required decision-making condition contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the target meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a probabilistic reversal learning task involving uncertainty/ambiguity in reward outcomes (risky/ambiguous decision-making). The authors report voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level analyses of task-related parametric modulators (expected value/high vs low and positive prediction error), with thresholding and cluster correction and within-group maps and between-group comparisons (controls vs depressed vs suicide attempters). Participant groups are acceptable. Results are presented as whole-brain maps, figures, and tables. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) administered during whole-brain BOLD acquisition. The authors report within-group (one-sample t-test in healthy men) and group-level random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses, and used parametric modulators of explosion probability (risk) for Inflate and Success events—i.e., risk-related contrasts (parametric high-risk > low-risk). Results are reported at whole-brain level with cluster correction and described in text/figures. The study therefore satisfies the meta-analysis criteria for (1) fMRI during risky decision-making, (2) condition-vs-condition/parametric risk contrast, (3) whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps, (4) eligible participant groups, and (5) reporting of whole-brain results in text/figures. Full text appears complete.

Although this study used fMRI with human participants and included a perceptual judgment of acoustically ambiguous stimuli (word vs. pseudoword), it does not provide the required decision-making contrast specified by the review (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous, high uncertainty > low uncertainty, hard > easy, or task > active control). The reported contrasts are between subjectively word- versus pseudoword-perceived trials (content-based lexical/phonological contrasts) rather than formal decision-making condition contrasts manipulating uncertainty or perceptual difficulty. The paper does report group-level, whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables, and participants were appropriate, but the critical inclusion criterion I5 (at least one acceptable decision-making contrast) is not met. Therefore it should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (face same/different discrimination with morphed stimuli). It reports within-task contrasts (subjective ‘same’ vs ‘different’ and parametric modulation by morphing distance corresponding to perceptual difficulty/hard>easy comparisons), performed with whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM) and reports coordinates/tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not task>rest only). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study used an fMRI cue-reactivity task (passive viewing of cocaine-related vs natural scene images) and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps. However, it does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task nor contrasts of decision-making conditions (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. It does meet I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups: substance users/controls), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) is thus met, so the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI to investigate visual pattern recognition learning (Igo puzzles) with participants instructed to passively view stimuli during scanning. Although whole-brain, group-level activation maps and contrasts (Igo vs non-Igo, Day-3 vs Day-1) are reported (meets I6 and I8) and the participant sample is acceptable (I7), the fMRI task was not a risky, ambiguous, or clearly defined perceptual decision-making task: subjects were instructed not to solve problems during scanning and the paradigm targets learning/recognition rather than an explicit perceptual decision contrast (hard>easy or low>high coherence). Therefore the key inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (a decision-making contrast) are not met. This study is excluded under E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of cognitive control/conflict (MSIT) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (Type 2 > Type 0) and whole-brain voxelwise analysis, but the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I7 (participant group acceptable: human patients within eligible age range), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (required decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy for perceptual DM). Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study includes an fMRI gambling task (meets I4), but does not provide evidence of required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe) nor clear whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (I5 and I6 not met/unclear). Cannot verify whether any eligible within-task contrasts were reported. Because key inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied or cannot be confirmed from the available content, the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4. Inclusion criteria not met / unclear: I5, I6. No explicit exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E9) are clearly met based on the available abstract alone. Full text incomplete prevents definitive determination; recommend obtaining the full article to reassess.

This study reports an fMRI experiment with human participants performing a sequential risk-taking task (opening boxes with a hidden ‘devil’) during scanning, satisfying I4. It provides within-task contrasts comparing outcome conditions relevant to risky decision-making (Optimum, Miss, Devil) and interaction/parametric contrasts tied to decision-related states (regret vs. relief), meeting I5. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results are reported with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (tables and figures), satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adult humans, so I7 is satisfied. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (contrasts are condition-vs-condition, not task>rest only; whole-brain analyses reported; not PET; task is risky decision-making). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of risky decision-making fMRI studies.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key fMRI-specific inclusion criteria required by the meta-analysis. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (the paper contrasts high-risk vs low-risk decision conditions in its analyses) and I7 (participant group is acceptable). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (no fMRI scan was conducted in this study — it is an EEG study that used fMRI activation foci from a prior separate study as priors) and I6 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked fMRI statistical maps are reported). The paper presents EEG/ERP and fMRI-constrained source analyses but does not provide the required original whole-brain fMRI activation maps or within-task fMRI contrasts needed for inclusion in an fMRI activation meta-analysis. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the task is social/moral decision-making (forgiveness after an apology), which falls outside the review scope (Exclusion E5). The study does include fMRI during a decision task and reports whole-brain group analyses, but it does not provide the required risky/ambiguity/perceptual decision contrasts as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Specifically: exclusion met: E5. Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI during a decision task), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion NOT met: I5 (no contrast matching the risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts required). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a human fMRI study in which participants performed a 4-arm bandit decision-making task involving uncertainty (reward probabilities, reversals). The authors report whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (GLMs) and thresholded statistical maps (with multiple-comparisons correction) and have uploaded maps to NeuroVault. Key contrasts/regressors include model entropy (changes in uncertainty/high vs low entropy) and exploitation vs exploration, which correspond to ambiguous decision-making contrasts (high uncertainty > low uncertainty) and within-task condition comparisons. Results are reported across the whole brain (figures, corrected maps, ROI/peak coordinates) and not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Participants are healthy human volunteers. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not violate exclusion criteria (no PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, empirical fMRI data reported).

This study is excluded because its fMRI tasks are cue-reactivity and response-inhibition, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks (Exclusion E5). Additionally, the imaging analysis was restricted to an ROI mask rather than a whole-brain task activation map, meeting Exclusion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant group qualifies) and I8 (whole-brain results may be reported in tables/coordinates — the paper reports activation coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no eligible decision-making contrasts of the accepted forms such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), and I6 (no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation with whole-brain, group-level analyses (I6), includes an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures (I8). However, the task is a noninstrumental, deterministic outcome-prediction task using appetitive and aversive cues without any manipulation of risk, uncertainty/ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty; it therefore does not satisfy I4 (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) nor I5 (relevant decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). This violates exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E5.

This fMRI study used a food liking/wanting rating and food-choice paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. No contrasts matching risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy are reported. Analyses focus on ROI parameter estimates and regressions linking ratings to ROI activations rather than group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps. Therefore it fails the review's task-domain and methodological requirements.

This is an fMRI study including a perceptual decision-making task (visual size discrimination) performed by human participants (n=34) with concurrent fMRI (I4). The paper reports direct task contrasts (e.g., DISC S > DISC E and DISC E > DISC S), i.e. between-task decision-making contrasts qualifying as decision-task versus another condition (I5). Analyses are voxelwise, group-level, whole-brain SPM8 results with coordinates and cluster statistics reported (and unthresholded maps available), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I6, I8). Participants are healthy adults (I7). Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and neuroimaging details; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a perceptual, ambiguous decision-making task (categorization of ambiguous shapes) performed during fMRI. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (indicated vs. contraindicated targets; analyses across ambiguous vs. non-ambiguous bins) rather than task>rest contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (random-effects GLM, cluster correction) and surviving clusters and their coordinates/ROIs are reported. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and does not trigger any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face detection with graded noise). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with thresholded cluster maps and tables, and links neural activity to task difficulty via correlations with reaction time (a parametric within-task effect analogous to hard>easy or low coherence>high coherence). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and ROI conjunctions. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (risky decision-making). It includes task-versus-active-control contrasts (reward pumps vs. control pumps) and parametric pump-vs-control analyses that index risk, reported at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise results (FDR-corrected) and coordinates/tables/figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (whole-brain, task>control contrasts).

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans using a near-threshold pain-detection paradigm (perceptual decision-making). The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (pain vs no pain; high threat vs low threat; interaction contrasts) relevant to perceptual decision-making, and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates. Results include anticipation and stimulation contrasts and whole-brain SPM analyses. The task is a perceptual decision task (detection/classification of stimulus as painful vs nonpainful), satisfying the perceptual-DM domain. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study does not meet the review’s key inclusion requirements for decision-making tasks. While it reports group-level, whole-brain fMRI results (I6), includes an acceptable participant group (healthy adults; I7), and provides whole-brain results in text/figures (I8), it does NOT involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (participants provided pleasantness/anticipation ratings rather than making risk/ambiguity/perceptual choices) and does not report decision-making contrasts of the admitted forms (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not satisfied. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is a valuation/anticipation paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Conclusion: EXCLUDE (E5).

This is an fMRI study in humans using a Wheel of Fortune task manipulating reward magnitude, probability, and risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts including risky > safe (risk contrast), probability contrasts (low vs high), and magnitude contrasts (high vs low) during the selection phase. Group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses are reported with coordinate tables and corrected cluster thresholds. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) task probing reward sensitivity and cognitive flexibility, not explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts required by the review. The reported contrasts (reward vs punishment; shift vs stay) do not match accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore Exclusion E5 applies. The study does satisfy whole-brain group-level fMRI reporting and acceptable reporting formats (I6, I8) and uses human participant groups that are admissible (I7). Inclusion criteria I4 (task is a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and I5 (at least one accepted risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrast) are not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of repetition priming/semantic classification (size/organic judgments), not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy adults), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrast such as “risky>safe” or “hard>easy”). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (a gambling task) with parametric contrasts for variance, loss probability, and maximum loss. The analysis includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLMs and reports cluster-corrected whole-brain results and peak MNI coordinates for the variance (risk) regressor. The variance parametric modulation effectively tests activity increasing with risk (analogous to high-risk > low-risk). Therefore the study meets I4 (fMRI risky DM), I5 (within-task contrast/parametric high-risk vs low-risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not task>rest only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adults that used a risky decision-making task (approach–avoidance gambles with probabilistic loss) during scanning, and includes within-subject contrasts between risky (Ap/Av) and control (Ap/Ap) conditions and choice-related contrasts. Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise GLMs (whole-brain analyses with SPM; results reported with FWE correction and figures/tables), and whole-brain task-evoked maps and contrasts are described. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (condition and decision contrasts, e.g., Ap/Av > Ap/Ap and choice contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (healthy human participants included), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not resting-state/ROI-only, not task>rest only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study is whole-brain and used tasks including a perceptual color-detection task, but it does not contain an eligible decision-making contrast as required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (healthy adult participants allowed), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 — the paper does not report an accepted decision-making contrast (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or perceptual hard>easy / perceptual task>control). The main contrasts are social/intention (Shared vs Parallel Intentions) and task attention (Intention vs Color), not perceptual difficulty or decision-making contrasts per the meta-analysis definitions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

The fMRI in this study was collected during a passive Pavlovian learning task (cue–reward associations and reward omission), whereas the risky decision-making (choice between low- and high-return cues) occurred in a separate behavioral session months later outside the scanner. Exclusion criterion met: E5 — the study’s fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (it assesses Pavlovian learning/reward omission without uncertainty manipulation). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain analyses are reported), I7 (eligible participant group: healthy human males), I8 (whole-brain results are described in the text/supplement). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I4 (no fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), I5 (no decision-making contrasts during fMRI such as risky>safe). fulltext_incomplete set to false (full article content present).

This is an fMRI study in humans (n=16) where participants performed a resource-allocation task that operationalizes decision-making under risk (variance minimization). The authors report group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects) with parametric contrasts (e.g., correlation coefficient and correlation prediction error; binned high vs low correlation effects) and provide peak MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. These constitute within-task condition contrasts (high vs low correlation/parametric modulation) rather than task>rest, satisfying contrast requirements. Participants are healthy adults. Whole-brain results are reported in the main text with coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a visual categorization (perceptual) decision-making task, with within-task contrasts (e.g., RB vs II trials; high-competition vs non-competition trials) and trial-type contrasts used to identify task-evoked activations. Analyses include group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (with reported cluster coordinates and thresholds) and ROI analyses; coordinates and cluster information are provided. Participants are healthy adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, connectivity-only, baseline-only contrasts, ROI-only results, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and is eligible for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

Exclusion E5 met: the task is a value-based crowdfunding choice, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported), I7 (healthy human participants were scanned), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in the text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not classified or manipulated as risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM), and I5 (contrasts are fund vs no-fund rather than the specified risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Therefore the study must be excluded per E5. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, the study used fMRI in a two-choice prediction task (meets I4) and reports success-related activation implying within-task contrasts (meets I5). However, the provided content does not allow verification of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (I6 not verifiable) nor clear evidence that the task falls into the review’s target categories (risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Because key inclusion criterion I6 cannot be confirmed from the available text and the full article (methods/results) is not provided, I exclude the study. Full text incomplete; recommend obtaining full article to confirm eligibility.

The study used fMRI during a probability-discounting (risky decision-making) task and reported probability vs certain condition comparisons in behavioral and ICA-based imaging analyses, and participants meet acceptable groups. However, the imaging results are reported via independent component analysis (component spatial maps and component-level beta weights) rather than as a group-level, voxelwise task activation contrast (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/voxelwise contrasts such as probability>certainty are presented). This means it fails inclusion criterion I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps) and falls under exclusion E7 (reports ICA/task-based network analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports empirical fMRI data collected while human participants made risky and ambiguous decision-making choices (I4). It includes condition-wise comparisons and parametric contrasts (subjective value under ambiguity vs risk; ambiguous > risk) and thus meets the contrast requirement (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLMs with corrected thresholds and reported activation maps/tables (I6, I8). Participants are healthy human volunteers (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only task>baseline contrasts, and is empirical. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and figures/tables descriptions, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports an fMRI experiment where human adolescents performed a two-choice facial emotion identification task (perceptual decision-making) during scanning. The authors computed a FACE versus OVAL sensorimotor control contrast (i.e., perceptual task > control task) and performed whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster correction and reported MNI coordinates. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (perceptual task > control task contrast), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (coordinates and maps described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a methods/software paper (HDDM) describing a Python toolbox, simulations, and an EEG example; it does not report any fMRI data or fMRI task-activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the reported decision-making task/data are not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making in the sense required by the meta-analysis). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan during task), I5 (no qualifying fMRI contrasts between decision conditions or task vs control), I6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI statistical maps reported), I8 (no whole-brain fMRI results reported in tables/figures/text). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study used an fMRI monetary incentive reaction-time task focused on reward anticipation (gain vs. no-gain, loss vs. no-loss) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM (it is an incentive/reactive reward-anticipation task). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task contrasts comparing conditions such as $4 vs $0), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (human participants; healthy sample), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). No other exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, rest-baseline-only) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded from this meta-analysis because it does not address the specific types of decision-making tasks required.

Excluded because the study does not investigate a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis (E5). The experiment probes action planning/motor preparation (specific vs. general vs. no-go cues) rather than perceptual difficulty, risk, or ambiguity in the target sense. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI maps reported), I7 (healthy adult participants), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task per the review scope), I5 (no qualifying contrast of the target types such as hard>easy, low coherence>high, risk>safe; the reported contrasts (e.g., double-cue > no-go) reflect action planning vs. no-action rather than the perceptual/uncertainty contrasts targeted). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI scan during a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) in human adolescents (I4). It includes explicit condition contrasts comparing high-risk versus low-risk choices (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (3×2×3 ANOVA) reported in the results and tables (I6). Participant groups (adolescents with depression/suicide attempt and healthy controls) are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), the modality is fMRI (not PET), the task is a risky decision-making task (not excluded types), whole-brain results (not only ROI or connectivity) are reported, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study acquired group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (reporting 1- vs 2-stream percepts) and an objective detection task (shift detection). The paper reports voxelwise RFX-GLM analyses (t ≥ 4.5, p < 0.002), lists brain regions/coordinates, and performs condition-wise comparisons (small/medium/large Δf; post-hoc t-tests between conditions, e.g., small vs large) rather than only task>rest. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task condition contrasts, e.g., small vs large Δf and condition > baseline and pairwise condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants included), and I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only task>rest contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (Exclusion E5). The task is a serial reaction time sequential prediction task, not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm, and it does not report contrasts of the forms required by I5 (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Satisfies other methodological criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses are reported (I6), participant sample is acceptable (I7), and whole-brain results/coordinates are provided in supplementary tables (I8). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (appropriate decision-making contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary material).

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that directly examines perceptual decision-making (emotion vs. gender categorizations of faces). It reports condition-vs-control contrasts (emotion > control, gender > control) and direct decision-condition contrasts (emotion > gender and vice versa), meeting the required perceptual-DM contrast forms. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise maps with corrected cluster thresholds and reported activation coordinates/tables/figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and contrasts are against an active control task rather than implicit baseline).

The study used an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (social/economic exchange) task focusing on social feedback and cooperation/defection, which constitutes social decision-making rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. This violates exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses/SMAPs reported or referenced), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/supplement). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — contrasts are cooperate vs defect, reciprocated vs unreciprocated feedback, and anticipation after cooperation/defection, which do not match the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore the paper should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is a probabilistic reinforcement-learning paradigm focused on reward prediction errors and model-based valuation, and the authors explicitly note the task “was not a risky decision making task per se.” Thus the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (human participant groups across ages qualify), and I8 (whole-brain results and ROIs are described in text/online supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), and I5 (no admitted contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; analyses are model-based parametric modulators rather than the required decision-making condition contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study is not an fMRI decision-making paper. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (PET study — the imaging modality used is 18F-FDG PET/CT), E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task — the study is diagnostic imaging of glottic cancer, with no behavioral decision-making paradigm or contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan during a decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), I6 (no whole-brain group-level fMRI task-evoked maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the fMRI decision-making meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic/hypothesis-comparison decision task (deciding whether to accept a focal hypothesis based on known probabilities), which constitutes decision-making under uncertainty (risky/ambiguous category). It includes within-task contrasts (Accept Focal vs Reject Focal) and a task vs active control contrast (Hypothesis Comparison vs Evidence Assessment). Analyses are group-level and whole-brain: CPCA-derived functional networks are computed from whole-brain voxel time series and spatial component maps are displayed and analyzed at the group level. Participants are healthy adults. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, PET, or baseline-only contrasts) apply. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion met: E5 - the task is a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement-learning) task focused on contingency learning and prediction-error signaling, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses with reported coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds), I7 (participant sample falls within acceptable groups/age range), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not classified as a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm per the review definitions), I5 (the reported contrasts—punished reversal errors vs rewarded correct responses—are within a reversal-learning framework and do not match the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study reports fMRI during a risk-sensitivity decision-making task (choices between larger risky vs smaller certain rewards), and presents within-task contrasts (categorical regressors for selecting the variable/risky option versus not, and parametric subjective value regressors). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected) and ROI analyses are also described. Participants are healthy young adults and results are fully described across methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task decision contrasts such as variable/risky option selected vs not, and value-related regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to task>baseline contrasts only; includes condition contrasts and parametric effects; not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI (MID task) but the fMRI task is a reward-processing/anticipation paradigm without an uncertainty or choice manipulation characteristic of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps reported), I7 (human participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (contrasts are reward-anticipation vs no-reward/loss vs no-loss, which do not match the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous or perceptual decision-making task; it is reward receipt/anticipation without uncertainty manipulation). Full text appears complete. Therefore study is excluded.

Exclusion E8 met: the paper reports only between-group contrasts (MS > HC during reward anticipation and control anticipation) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect or a task>control (e.g., reward>control or risky>safe) group-level contrast necessary for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making card-guessing task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported contrast comparing decision-making vs active control or risky>safe; the paper reports between-group comparisons only). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of causal/one-shot learning but it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined by the meta-analysis. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (human participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that directly manipulated and measured perceptual decision-making (spatial-frequency discrimination) during scanning (I4). The authors modeled task difficulty as a parametric modulator (effectively hard > easy contrasts) and report contrasts of difficulty/modulation and an age-by-orientation interaction (I5). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level SPM analyses are reported with FWE-corrected results across the whole brain (I6). Participants are human (younger and older adults); participant characteristics do not warrant exclusion per review rules (I7). Whole-brain results are reported and described in the text and figures (I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that used a risky decision-making task (50/50 gambles over numbers of electric shocks) while scanning. The authors performed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) focused on the decision period, including parametric modulation by expected value and separate modulators for number of shocks less vs more; results are reported as whole-brain statistics, tables, and figures. The task involves within-task condition comparisons (variation in gamble EV; accept/reject decisions) rather than only task>baseline contrasts. The paper contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E6 (reporting focuses on ROI analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion met: I7 (participant group qualifies: healthy human participants).
