Inclusion NOT met: I4 (fMRI was acquired during a Monetary Incentive Delay task, which probes reward anticipation/receipt rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making), I5 (no decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy; primary contrasts were win vs no-win outcomes), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported; analyses focused on basal ganglia ROIs). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain group analyses (I6) in healthy participants (I7) and reports coordinates/whole-brain results (I8). However, the experimental task is a multiple-cue judgment (estimating toxicity of fictitious items) intended to induce exemplar-based learning, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation. Therefore it fails to meet I4 (task must be risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) and the required decision-making contrast forms in I5 (the contrasts involve judgment learning and task-vs-dot-bug control but do not constitute a perceptual/risky/ambiguous decision contrast as defined). Exclusion criterion E5 is therefore met (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) with a within-task contrast comparing speed vs. accuracy (S > A), i.e., a decision-condition vs. decision-condition contrast. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected maps, voxel-thresholded maps, and coordinate tables). Results are clearly described in methods and results (behavioral and whole-brain fMRI), and the full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic classification learning (PCL) task that required trial-by-trial decisions between two outcomes under uncertainty (weather prediction / epidemic prediction). The authors report contrasts of the PCL task versus an active control condition (“hardware check”), satisfying a task-versus-control contrast. Analyses were conducted at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM random-effects models and whole-brain results are reported (ROI and exploratory whole-brain analyses and tables/figures). Participant groups (OCD and healthy controls) are acceptable per inclusion rules. Although the PCL is not a canonical economic gambling task, it is a decision-making task under probabilistic uncertainty and meets the meta-analysis criteria for risky/ambiguous decision-making paradigms. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, rest-baseline-only contrasts, ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study (human participants) that implemented a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) and directly contrasts difficulty levels (hard [low coherence] vs easy [high coherence]). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (interaction of difficulty and time; ROI selection with leave-one-out; whole-brain maps and tables), satisfying requirements for a within-task contrast (hard > easy / low coherence > high coherence). Participants are healthy adults. Results are presented in full article text with methods, results, tables, and figures (whole-brain maps and coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts, empirical fMRI with appropriate contrasts).

Exclusion rationale: E5 (task not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and E8 (study reports only a between-group contrast with no unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported), I7 (human participant group qualifies), and I8 (whole-brain results are described in the text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the fMRI task involved viewing deceptive vs. non-deceptive advertisements and post-scan ratings of comprehension/purchase intent, which does not clearly match the review’s definition of a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (the paper does not report a qualifying condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast such as deceptive>non-deceptive or a risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrast at the whole-brain level; instead analyses used parametric regressors and a between-group contrast). Full text completeness: full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This fMRI study administered a number-comparison task manipulating symbolic distance (closer = harder) and analyzed BOLD signal correlated with numerical distance (a hard>easy perceptual decision contrast). Experiment 2 reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with multiple-comparison correction and tabulated significant regions; results include within-task contrasts (linear trend for distance). Participants were healthy young adults (eligible per criteria). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for (I4) fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task, (I5) at least one decision-making contrast (hard>easy via symbolic distance linear trend), (I6) whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) whole-brain results reported in text/tables. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal decision-making task with anticorrelated reward probabilities—an uncertainty/risk-based decision-making paradigm. The authors provide whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps and contrasts (parametric regressors for model-derived RPEs, and comparisons between RPEDU and RPESU) with FWE-corrected results reported in the text and tables. The task and contrasts constitute within-task, condition-versus-condition analyses relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. Participants include both clinical (alcohol-dependent) and healthy groups, and whole-brain results are clearly reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI of risky/ambiguous decision-making and reports appropriate whole-brain contrasts.

This study meets the review inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a decision-making task under uncertainty (4-armed bandit; I4), reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (explore > exploit and exploit > explore; I5), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with multiple-comparison correction and tables/coordinates (I6 and I8). Participants are healthy adults, so participant criteria are acceptable (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and core whole-brain results are reported, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are triggered: contrasts are not against implicit baseline/rest (E3), modality is fMRI not PET (E4), the task involves decision-making under uncertainty (not an excluded task class; E5 not met), whole-brain results are provided (E6 not met), and this is an empirical fMRI activation study (E7, E8, E9 not met).

This is an empirical concurrent TMS-fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (visual detection) task. The paper reports within-task, decision-related contrasts (misses vs. hits; misses vs. correct rejections) and tests interactions with TMS, which are valid decision-making condition contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (permutation-based cluster correction across the whole brain) and results are reported in the text, figures and tables. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and is complete for screening. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports whole-head fMRI in human participants performing a perceptual decision task (bistable/ambiguous visual perception where subjects reported ‘‘line’’ vs ‘‘object’’ percepts), and directly contrasts brain activity between the two perceptual states. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and group maps/statistics (including voxel coordinates, t-values, permutation testing) are provided. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast: object vs line percepts), I6 (group-level whole-brain evidence), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used an experiential risky decision-making task (choices between sure and risky monetary options). The paper reports within-task contrasts and model-based regressors (e.g., RSTD prediction error; contrasts comparing risk-related trials to other trials) and performs a group-level, whole-brain, random-effects analysis with familywise error correction, reporting surviving clusters and coordinates (Table 1). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts/model regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI was acquired while human participants performed a probabilistic monetary decision-making task involving risk), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps of PE-related BOLD responses are reported), I7 (participant groups are acceptable – healthy controls and schizophrenia patients), and I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in the text). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the paper does not report a contrast comparing two decision-making conditions of interest, e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, or an experimental risk task > control task). Instead the main task-related effect is a parametric modulation by prediction error at reward presentation, which does not match the required decision-level contrasts specified in I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I5 is not met, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study re-analyzes a stop-signal (response inhibition) fMRI task (Aron et al.) and does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It meets inclusion criteria I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are present), I7 (human participant sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). However it does NOT meet I4 (fMRI during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (contains no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Therefore it is excluded under E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion based on E6: the paper reports ROI-based BOLD time-series analyses (MarsBar masks and ROI averages) rather than providing group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (human fMRI during a risky decision-making investment task), I5 (within-task condition comparisons: positive vs negative returns, RPE>0 vs <0, bet-size conditions), and I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps reported). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis that requires whole-brain voxelwise task maps; ROI-only results violate E6.

Exclusion criteria met: E3. This study performed fMRI while participants completed a risky decision-making task (IGT) and provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps, but the reported within-task contrasts are task versus rest (implicit baseline) and the group comparisons are between FH+ and FH-; no condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control decision-making contrasts (e.g., 'risky > safe', 'high-risk > low-risk', or 'task > control task') are reported. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (results described in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not satisfied: I5 (no appropriate decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because E3 is met, study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making with human participants (meets I4) and includes within-task contrasts (e.g., £7 vs £1, context comparisons) and reported coordinates (meets I5 and I8). However, the imaging used a partial-volume acquisition focused on ventral brain and the reported analyses are ROI-focused with small-volume corrections; no unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps covering the whole brain are provided. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and effectively reports only ROI/partial-volume results (violating E6). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a probabilistic (uncertain) two-step decision task with monetary outcomes (decision-making under risk/uncertainty). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) and presents task-related contrasts/parametric modulators comparing neural responses as a function of prediction-error magnitude (high vs low SPE/RPE) and direct contrasts (e.g., SPE vs abs(RPE)). These are within-task, condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts tied to uncertainty and hence relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. Whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures. Participants are healthy humans. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

(a) Exclusion met: E5 — the task is an interoception (heartbeat counting/exteroception) task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported and used in analyses), I7 (clinical participant group — PD/AG — which is acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results and contrasts are clearly described in the text and supplementary material). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making contrast of the accepted forms such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy appears; contrasts are interoception vs exteroception). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded.

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It uses an incentive delay task and an exchange task to measure valuation of social and monetary rewards (reward receipt/valuation), without manipulations of uncertainty/risk or perceptual difficulty. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task maps are reported), I7 (human participants acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe or hard>easy). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual; study examines social reward valuation/reward receipt without uncertainty). Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement learning) task and reports whole-brain PE-related activation, but it does not present contrasts matching risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons (e.g., "risky > safe", "ambiguity > non-ambiguous", or "hard > easy"). Instead, the primary fMRI regressor is a prediction-error parametric modulator and multinomial regressions relate learning/activation to motivational types. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 and is excluded under E5 (task not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as required). Met inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task with probabilistic outcomes), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise PE maps reported, FWE-corrected), I7 (participant group allowable: healthy adolescents), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Not met: I5 (no condition-vs-condition or task-vs-control contrasts of risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Exclusion criteria applied: E5. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI experiment with whole-brain, group-level analyses (random-effects) reporting coordinates, but the task is an information-search/personal-involvement paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Therefore it does not meet the review’s required task domain. Exclusion applied: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported via coordinates/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task — NOT met), I5 (required risk/ambiguity/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy — NOT met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used a perceptual target-detection task with morphed stimuli that manipulated ambiguity and perceptual similarity. It reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., morph1 vs. target) and uses similarity and ambiguity regressors to predict BOLD, including whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FDR correction; coordinates and activation maps are reported. Participants are human healthy volunteers. Therefore it meets criteria for an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (I4), provides condition-wise contrasts (I5), reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results/maps (I6), includes an eligible participant group (I7), and provides whole-brain results/coordinates in text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans (n=19) that manipulates perceptual uncertainty (blurred vs clear pictures) and reports contrasts between conditions (e.g., blurred > clear; reduction of uncertainty: B–C vs B–C). Group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects analyses and cluster-corrected statistical maps are reported (with coordinates and figures). The task targets perceptual processing/uncertainty that maps onto perceptual decision-making contrasts (analogous to hard>easy or perceptual task>control). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contrasts are condition-vs-condition rather than task>rest. Therefore the study meets I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

The study used fMRI while participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT), so it meets I4 (task fMRI) and participant inclusion (I7). However, it does not report any within-task contrasts of decision conditions (e.g., risky>safe) or a decision-task versus an active control task, and instead focuses on connectivity/graph-theoretical metrics and comparisons to rest. It therefore fails I5 (no condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts) and I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps). This violates exclusion criteria E3 (only contrasts against rest/implicit baseline) and E7 (connectivity-only analyses without whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study should be excluded from the activation-based meta-analysis.

This fMRI study had healthy human participants performing a dual-choice card gambling task that manipulated risk (high-risk vs low-risk) and used a parametric regressor for chosen risk. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported (SPM8) with FWE correction and whole-brain results (and ROI-constrained results) presented in tables and figures. The reported contrasts include risk-related activation scaling with risk magnitude (equivalent to high-risk > low-risk). The task and contrasts align with the review objective (risky decision-making). Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

EXCLUDED because the study used a delay-discounting (intertemporal choice) task, which is explicitly outside the review scope (E5). The study did perform whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses (I6), used an acceptable participant group (I7), and reported whole-brain results in the text (I8). However, it did not evaluate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (I4 not met) nor provide the required types of contrasts for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM (I5 not met). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that acquired whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps while participants performed a prediction task based on perceptual sequences. The study includes condition contrasts of interest (structured vs. random sequences; i.e., decision/perceptual task vs. an active control sequence condition), reports whole-brain voxelwise GLM results and corrected statistical maps, and provides coordinates/figures. The task constitutes a perceptual decision-making paradigm under uncertainty (prediction of next stimulus), fitting the review’s perceptual-DM domain. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports combined fMRI and PET during a probabilistic reversal learning task and focuses on reward prediction error (RPE) signals. While it provides a voxelwise whole-brain (SPM) analysis with results reported (ventral striatum) and includes human participants (controls and patients) — satisfying I6 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), I7 (participant groups acceptable) and I8 (results clearly described) — it does not meet the review’s task definitions. The task is a reversal learning/reinforcement-learning paradigm rather than an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. Crucially, the paper does not report contrasts of the form required by I5 (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy); the main fMRI regressor is a parametric RPE modulator rather than an uncertainty/risk/perceptual difficulty contrast. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (task not in risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5. Exclusion IDs met: E5.

This fMRI study investigates multisensory social-norm inference/mentalizing (congruency of vocal reactions to visual scenes). It does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm) and I5 (no contrasts of the form risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or perceptual hard>easy; the main contrast is social congruent vs incongruent). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using an ambiguous (Rubin vase) perceptual decision-making task during scanning. The authors report condition-versus-condition contrasts including ambiguous > non-ambiguous and pre- vs. post-training ambiguous blocks, and present group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level F-contrasts, FWE-corrected peaks and coordinates). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (ambiguous > non-ambiguous and pre/post training contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps reported), I7 (human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not resting-state/only connectivity, not task>baseline only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a choice reaction time (CRT) task (so I4 met) and reports group-level analyses/whole-brain maps (I6 met) and detailed whole-text results (I8 met). However, it does not include any decision-making contrast of the form required by the meta-analysis (e.g., hard > easy, low coherence > high coherence, perceptual task > control task, or risky/ambiguous contrasts). The main contrasts are threat versus safe context and trial-by-trial BOLD–RT correlations, which manipulate emotional context rather than the decision-making variable (I5 not met). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and falls under exclusion criterion E5 (task is not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrast as defined).

This is an fMRI study in which healthy human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (discriminating concentric vs. radial Glass patterns across multiple signal/coherence levels). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise searchlight results (second-level t-tests on classification accuracy) identifying regions where category information is decodable, and analyzes classifier performance across stimulus signal levels (analogous to low-coherence vs. high-coherence/perceptual difficulty). The study also includes a control (letter-detection) task and reports within-task comparisons and ANOVAs across conditions/ROIs. Participants are within eligible groups and full methods/results/discussion are present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET only, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only) apply. Hence it meets inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI whole-brain evidence.

The study used fMRI in human participants performing a face-authenticity judgment (a perceptual-type judgment) and reports whole-brain group analyses, but it does not provide any decision-making contrast that matches the meta-analysis inclusion forms (e.g., hard>easy, perceptual task>control). The reported within-group maps are task>implicit baseline contrasts and the main between-instruction comparison is a between-group contrast. Because the study’s reported task effects are only versus an implicit baseline (and no active control or condition-versus-condition decision contrasts matching I5), it violates exclusion criterion E3. Therefore it must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects that manipulated reward probability/uncertainty (slot machines A–D) during task performance and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Delay Slot_B > Delay Slot_A: high uncertainty > lower uncertainty). Group-level whole-brain, random-effects SPM analyses are reported with coordinate tables and figures. Contrasts correspond to ambiguous/risky decision-making comparisons (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (vibrotactile faster-slower and same-different judgments) with group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses and reported voxelwise contrasts (e.g., same-different > faster-slower; different > same; regular > noisy). The task directly manipulates perceptual decision variables (precision/noise) and contains condition-versus-condition contrasts suitable for meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making. Whole-brain, random-effects, FWE-corrected results and cluster coordinates are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state/only connectivity; not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Thus all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that used a perceptual decision-making task (time discrimination) with an active control (temporal order judgment), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and cluster results. The contrast of interest is time discrimination > temporal order (an active control), matching the perceptual-DM contrast type (perceptual task > control task). Whole-brain permutation-based analyses and cluster-level results are presented, and results are reported in the main text (tables/figures). Participants were healthy human subjects (males, ages 10–53). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human adults performing a perceptual decision-making (visual target detection) task with manipulations relevant to decision processes. It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Cue-Low vs Cue-High; prev-Decision (+) vs prev-Decision (−); Target(+)>Target(−)) rather than task>rest, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 second-level one-sample t-tests with cluster correction). Results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met.

This study reports event-related fMRI collected while human participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (coherent motion discrimination), satisfying I4. The experiment manipulated perceptual difficulty (multiple coherence levels and two durations), providing within-task contrasts appropriate for perceptual-DM (e.g. low coherence vs high coherence, short vs long duration), satisfying I5. The paper describes group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) analyses in addition to ROI analyses (group analysis results and thresholds are reported), satisfying I6 and I8. Participant groups (ASD and matched controls, ages 15–27) are acceptable under the review’s participant inclusion rules, satisfying I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: the study does not rely solely on task>rest contrasts, is fMRI (not PET), reports task activation analyses rather than only ROI/connectivity results, and provides within-group effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This study reports an empirical fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (accept/reject gambles) with wealth shocks; it performs group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (SPM8, random-effects) and reports whole-brain results (cluster-level FWE-corrected coordinates) including contrasts (neural loss-aversion parametric contrasts and CONTINGENT > RANDOM contrasts across runs). The task constitutes risky decision-making and includes within-task and between-condition contrasts relevant to risk (e.g., neural loss aversion contrasts, CONTINGENT vs RANDOM for Run2). All required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not only baseline contrasts, whole-brain results reported, not only ROI/connectivity, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study used fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (observers reported perceived motion direction; satisfies I4), included condition comparisons involving coherence/ambiguity (0% ambiguous vs 50/100% unambiguous; satisfies I5), and tested healthy human participants (satisfies I7). However, the paper reports ROI-based multivoxel pattern classification results (V1–V4v, V3a, hMT+, IPS, FEF) rather than a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation map or univariate whole-brain contrasts. It therefore does not provide the required whole-brain evidence (fails I6) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Accordingly, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment (Exp. 3) in which human participants performed perceptual decision-making (tilt/color flanker) while BOLD data were acquired. Group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses are reported (voxelwise results, FDR-corrected peaks and ROI leave-one-out results; tables and coordinates referenced), and parametric contrasts (e.g., target decision variable, flanker mean, interactions) are used to test decision-related effects. Thus the study contains (I4) fMRI during perceptual decision-making, (I5) within-task parametric contrasts/condition comparisons, (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps, (I7) an acceptable participant group, and (I8) results reported as coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, empirical fMRI task data present). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that manipulated target-location uncertainty (p=0.5 vs p=1) during a visual search task and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts. The critical contrast CoTv (50% predictability) vs CoTf (100% predictability) directly corresponds to an uncertainty/ambiguity comparison (high uncertainty > low uncertainty) relevant to ambiguous decision-making. Analyses were whole-brain GLMs with group-level mixed-effects and reported voxelwise results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not report the required decision-making condition contrasts specified by the review (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). Explicitly: exclusion criterion met: E3 (the reported analyses focus on parametric model-based regressors—associability and prediction error—rather than condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a human probabilistic learning task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for model-based regressors), I7 (participant sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no contrast comparing two decision-making conditions or a decision-making task vs an active control task of the kind required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM meta-analytic inclusion). Therefore the paper does not provide the appropriate within-task contrasts required by the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an explicit audio-visual associative learning task that required trial-by-trial categorical predictions (a perceptual decision about visual stimulus category). The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected) for task-related parametric modulators, including precision-weighted prediction errors and measures related to expected uncertainty (ε3/ψ3), which correspond to contrasts of high vs. low uncertainty/conditional probability (ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). Results are reported in the main text with whole-brain maps and ROI-corrected analyses. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during perceptual decision task), I5 (within-task parametric contrasts mapping to high vs low uncertainty/conditional probability), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article is a narrative review summarizing neuroimaging findings on alexithymia rather than reporting original fMRI whole-brain task activation maps for risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It discusses PET studies and three prior imaging experiments (facial processing, visceral stimulation, and the Iowa Gambling Task) but does not provide fMRI acquisition or whole-brain voxelwise group maps/coordinates for a qualifying decision-making contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E9 (non-empirical review/narrative article) and E4 (PET imaging discussed; not fMRI). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast reported in fMRI context), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task maps presented). Full text appears complete for assessment.

This is a task-fMRI study of risky decision-making (I4) that performs within-task contrasts comparing risky (LP) vs safe (NP) conditions (I5) and includes allowable participant groups (ADP and HC; I7). However, the paper reports ICA-derived network/component results and tests component timecourses (beta-weights) rather than providing group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-activation contrast maps or coordinate-based activation results required for the meta-analysis. Thus it does not meet I6 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) and effectively reports only task-based connectivity/network analyses without the required whole-brain activation maps, meeting exclusion E7. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment (Experiment 2) in which healthy human males made decisions in a risky decision task (Stag hunt) while being scanned. The authors computed subject-level Stag > Rabbit contrasts and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (two-sample t-tests) and report cluster coordinates (left dlPFC) and functional connectivity results. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during human risky decision-making), I5 (explicit Stag > Rabbit condition contrast analogous to risky > safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (coordinates/tables and clear description). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and reports within-task contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Excluded because the fMRI task (Monetary Incentive Delay) is a reward-anticipation/impulsivity paradigm rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task (violates I4 / meets exclusion E5). The main reported contrast is “anticipation big win vs. baseline” which is a task-versus-implicit-baseline contrast rather than a condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrast required by the review (violates I5 / meets exclusion E3). The study does include group-level whole-brain maps and reports ROI and whole-brain results (I6 met), uses an acceptable participant group (adolescents; I7 met), and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables (I8 met). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 and I5. Exclusion criteria met: E3 and E5. Therefore the paper should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 - the task is a language rhyme-detection task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (human participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported with stereotaxic coordinates). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not performed during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no decision-making contrasts of the types required — contrasts are language task vs control, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

Exclusion: E5 (study is social decision-making/trust game). Although the task involves monetary risk, it is a social trust paradigm (investor–trustee interactions/Cyberball manipulation) and thus falls under the explicit exclusion of social/moral decision-making (E5). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI collected while participants performed a decision task with risky choices), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing decision types: keep vs share; decision-type ANOVA), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: None of the required inclusion criteria (I4–I8) are lacking; the study would otherwise qualify on those grounds, but it is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines multiple-cue judgment (toxicity estimation) and contrasts judgment task > active visual-detection baseline, but it does NOT probe risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (no risk/probability, ambiguity/uncertainty manipulation, or perceptual-difficulty/coherence manipulation). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 (task domain) and I5 (required decision-making contrast in the targeted domains). It does meet whole-brain fMRI reporting (I6), uses acceptable participant groups (I7), and reports whole-brain results clearly (I8). Exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous or perceptual DM) applies, so the study must be excluded.

This fMRI study uses an aversive avoidance-learning (fear conditioning) task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Exclusion applies because the task does not manipulate or operationalize risk, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty as defined by the review (E5). Met inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM contrasts are reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). Not met inclusion criteria: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and I5 (no decision-making contrasts of the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual forms). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This methods-focused paper presents simulations and fMRI analyses to evaluate approaches for estimating missing nodes in Dynamic Causal Modeling (DCM). Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI data collected during tasks — Go/No-Go and Simon tasks), I5 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g., Congruent > Incongruent), I7 (healthy human participants). Inclusion NOT met: I6 (paper does not provide or report a usable group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or coordinates suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis), I8 (no whole-brain results/coordinates or clearly described voxelwise group maps are provided for meta-analytic extraction). Exclusion applied: E6 (study effectively reports ROI/VOI-based and DCM/effective-connectivity analyses without providing whole-brain, voxelwise group activation results needed for this meta-analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet the required whole-brain/group-level reporting (I6) for inclusion.

Although this is an fMRI study with healthy human participants and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps, it does not contain any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe; high uncertainty > low uncertainty; hard > easy). The reported contrasts probe learning/update signals (signed/unsigned Bayesian updates, reward payout effects) and cross-stimulus suppression (HC vs LC association strength during probe blocks), but these are not equivalent to the admissible risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts listed in I5. Therefore it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI on humans performing a decision-making task under uncertainty/learning), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no eligible decision-making condition contrast as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E9 apply.

Exclusion IDs met: E5, E6, E7. (E5) The study’s tasks are verbal working memory and resting-state/simulation—not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. (E6) Analyses are ROI-based effective connectivity models with no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. (E7) The paper reports directed/effective connectivity and resting-state analyses without reporting a whole-brain task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (participant groups are human subjects within allowable ranges). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (no fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making), I5 (no decision-making contrasts of the admitted forms), I6 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete and contains methods/results/discussion. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

Excluded per E5: the task is a social trust game (interpersonal/social decision-making). The review’s exclusion E5 explicitly lists social decision-making as outside scope. Met inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI collected while participants performed a decision task involving uncertainty/risk), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy participant group qualifies), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates described). Not met: I5 (no reported decision-phase contrasts of the form risky>safe or equivalent; the reported fMRI analyses focus on outcome-phase contrasts and identity/outcome conditions rather than classic risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts required by the meta-analysis). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s scope and is excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task with decision-making under uncertainty (70% vs 30% reinforcement). It includes within-task condition contrasts (experienced outcome contrasts such as Gain vs Loss-avoidance and expected-value contrasts [Positive – Negative]) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported in figures/tables. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and control groups (allowed). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during decision-making under probabilistic outcomes), I5 (within-task condition contrasts comparing decision conditions: experienced and expected valence contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>rest), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in humans that examines perceptual and categorical (ambiguous) decision-making. It includes within-task condition contrasts (perceptual > categorical; covariation with degree of uncertainty; prior-knowledge vs naïve conditions) and decision-trial analyses (e.g., decision vs blank, and condition comparisons), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrast requirements. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with corrected cluster inference and tables of coordinates reported. Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in full (methods, results, coordinates/tables). Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a two-alternative forced-choice perceptual discrimination task (Thatcher illusion) during scanning, satisfying the perceptual decision-making domain. The imaging analysis reports within-task contrasts (upright vs inverted face discrimination) during the decision task (a condition-vs-condition contrast), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME, FDR-corrected). Participants are healthy adults and whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not baseline-only contrasts, not ROI-only). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8.

This study is excluded because it only reports task > rest (experimental blocks vs rest) fMRI contrasts rather than condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts required for inclusion. (a) Exclusion met: E3 (only contrasts against rest/implicit baseline). (b) Inclusion met: I4 (fMRI acquired during a perceptual decision task: CrossSquare simple choice), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps were computed), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). (c) Inclusion not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as hard>easy or task>active control; the reported fMRI contrasts were experimental vs rest). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study used a trust game (social decision-making) to examine conformity and reports whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., trust-influence > baseline; conformity > non-conformity). However, the meta-analysis includes only risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. The trust game is a social decision-making paradigm and therefore falls under exclusion criterion E5 (social decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results/coordinates are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review) and I5 (no decision contrasts of the forms required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete. Therefore, exclude (E5).

This fMRI study does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Participants passively viewed surprised faces during scanning; although faces varied in valence ambiguity, the paradigm assessed emotion perception (valence/arousal) rather than participants making decisions under risk/ambiguity or performing a perceptual difficulty task. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) an fMRI decision-making task and (I5) a decision-making contrast (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported) and I7 (healthy human participants). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because the experimental task does not meet the decision-making task requirements (I4, I5 not met).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (N=33) using a stop-signal paradigm that the authors explicitly frame as an indirect analog of risk-taking. The paper reports a within-task contrast comparing post-go speeding (interpreted as risk-taking) versus post-go slowing (risk-aversive) and provides group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM results with voxel coordinates and corrected clusters. Healthy adult participants were used. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4: human fMRI during a risky/decision task; I5: a decision-making contrast risky>safe analogue; I6: group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported; I7: participant group acceptable; I8: whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

E3: The study’s fMRI contrasts used for the primary analyses are condition-versus-baseline contrasts (e.g., Anticipation > baseline, Safe outcome > baseline, Risky outcome > baseline). While the task is a risky decision-making task (Stoplight Task) and the paper reports group-level whole-brain activation maps, the study does not report condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., risky > safe) or task-versus-active-control contrasts required by the meta-analysis. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast such as risky > safe). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (choices between lotteries) while scanned. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., analyses of risk-adjusted return at the decision stage, contrasts of social > private risk-adjusted return and comparisons between high-risk and low-risk choices and related treatment contrasts). Whole-brain results and ROI analyses are reported with coordinates and thresholds. Participants are healthy humans. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, and not non-empirical). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a perceptual odor discrimination task (meets I4). It reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses with coordinates and FWE-corrected results (meets I6 and I8) in a healthy sample (meets I7). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain contrast that corresponds to a decision-making condition comparison required by I5 (e.g., hard>easy, different>same, perceptual task>control). Reported imaging contrasts are stimulus-based (citral > mix1), feedback-based (correct > incorrect), and order-based (first > second), none of which directly compare decision-making conditions (same vs different or difficulty levels). Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

This is a methods/protocol paper describing the PROCAN cohort and planned neuroimaging; it does not report original task-evoked fMRI results or whole-brain, group-level statistical maps or contrasts. While the protocol includes fMRI acquisition and tasks (emotional go/no-go, monetary incentive delay, working memory), these are not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks as defined by the review, and no within-task decision contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) or whole-brain activation results are presented. Therefore it is non-empirical with respect to the meta-analysis question and lacks the required contrasts and maps.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain group analyses, but the task is a spatial/orientation (Relative Heading) task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion is based on E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I7 (healthy human participants included), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (decision-making contrasts of the types required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Full text appears complete.
